Our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] working on [From.Planet.GetName] have reached a highly unstable section of the ruins.

Supports will have to be carefully added to the floors and ceilings before we can proceed. It will be difficult work, but finding an alternate route would delay the project.
ancrel.8103.b: They will have to go around.
ancrel.8110.name: Ancient Records
ancrel.8110.desc: Ancient, partially translated records have been discovered amongst the ruins being excavated on [From.Planet.GetName]. [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the records contain several technical specifications that may be of value to our scientists.
ancrel.6049.name: Fossils Discovered on [Root.GetName]
ancrel.6049.desc:
Fossilized remains from several different species that do not appear to have been indigenous to [Root.GetName] have been found in a large and secluded valley on the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]. They all date from roughly the same time period, within the span of a few centuries some 3.6 million years ago.

Each of these species seems to have evolved in its own unique biosphere, and all appear to have been sapient. Strangely, every fossilized individual found so far shows signs of having met a violent end.
site_robot_debris_intro: The entire surface of this small asteroid is covered in robot debris, trapped in its weak gravity field. All of it appears military in nature, and there are enough combat droids here to outfit several armies had they not be shattered beyond all repair.
ancrel.6250.name: Two Sides
ancrel.6250.desc: Upon closer examination, the smashed droids found on the surface of [From.Planet.GetName] appear to originate from two distinct cultures. Technologically the droids must have been evenly matched when they were still functional, but there are many subtle differences that hint at different design origins.
ancrel.6255.name: Battlefield
ancrel.6255.desc:
[From.Planet.GetName] does not seem to have simply been a dumping ground for broken droids - it may have served as the actual battlefield where they were destroyed. The many layers of debris suggest a series of very intense battles waged intermittently across the better part of two centuries.

Exactly why two interstellar powers would commit such vast resources towards waging a massive ground war on a small and unremarkable asteroid remains an unanswered question.
ancrel.6260.name: The Treaty
ancrel.6260.desc:
Our archaeologists have learned that after a long and bitter war, the two empires inhabiting this corner of the galaxy some 200,000 years ago signed a treaty compelling them to settle all future disputes with arranged and highly regulated combat engagements between robotic armies.

[From.Planet.GetName] was chosen as the site of these battles. The treaty appears to have been upheld for nearly two centuries, preventing the outbreak of armed hostilities on numerous occasions, until one of the empires was caught cheating.
site_freighter_crash_intro: A small canyon of sorts has been carved onto the surface of this [From.Planet.GetPlanetMoon] by the violent impact of a starship. What remains of the vessel can still be found on the canyon floor. Although the crash must have occurred eons ago, the wreckage appears to be reasonably intact. An archaeological expedition would be able to learn more.
ancrel.6300.name: Captain's Chronicle
ancrel.6300.desc:
A log of sorts was recovered from what is believed to have served as the spacecraft's bridge:

"Captain's chronicle. Begin recording.

Made forced landing on planet 55-23-X. Incompetent crew to blame. Shadba, Vuxal, and Dibrak the Third did not survive. Pirvax lost two secondary appendages and eleven of his eyes - remains in critical condition, survival doubtful. Rest are fine. Awaiting rescue, but surrounded by idiots. Very depressed."
ancrel.6310.name: First Mate's Report
ancrel.6310.desc:
Another log has been found and translated:

"First Mate Ythar speaking. Captain has been safely stowed in Utility Closet C. That bumbling fool is to blame for everything. I am in command now. Chief Engineer Zarbla is working on a subspace transmitter. Without one, I fear we'll never get rescued as we're too far off the corporate trade routes.

Pirvax lost another eye. Likely won't last the day."
ancrel.6320.name: Food Situation
ancrel.6320.desc:
Yet another translated log:

"Running out of food. Ate our dead five cycles ago, but not enough to last us. We had a vote, and decided to eat the Captain. Engineer Zarbla still working hard on subspace transmitter. She assures me it is nearly complete. It looks very complex.

Pirvax's last secondary appendage has shriveled up and turned magenta. Death is near."
ancrel.6330.name: The Fraud
ancrel.6330.desc:
Another log from First Mate Ythar:

"Confronted Zarbla about the subspace transmitter. Turns out she had just shoved a bunch of junk and loose cables into an empty fuel canister. She's not even a real engineer.

Pirvax is now leaking fluids from his mesothorax. Will surely perish soon. Envious."
ancrel.6340.name: Third Mate's Report
ancrel.6340.desc:
This translated log appears to have been recorded by Uxla, the Third Mate:

"First Mate Ythar committed suicide by ripping off his own antennas yesterday. Technician (2nd class) Misiva declared herself Empress shortly afterwards, but food riots forced her into exile on the lower decks. Situation very bleak. Cannibalism widespread.

Pirvax has turned entirely magenta after his lower abdomen exploded yesterday. Should be dead, but is not. Now worshipped as deity by gamma shift."
ancrel.6350.name: Patrol Log
ancrel.6350.desc:
One last log has been found and translated:

"Patrol log, Officer Gilgamm. Detected crashed vessel on 55-23-X, moved to investigate. Vessel identified as the Ravink, a class-P modular freighter. A single survivor in critical condition was recovered from the wreckage. Identity confirmed as Pirvax, Boatswain's mate.

Remaining crew either perished in crash or turned on each other shortly before our arrival. As per standard protocol, I am leaving this log here and registering the Ravink as a protected grave site. End recording."
ancrel.4036.b.response: I am Oracle, an artificial intelligence gifted with "the sight". My software allows me to predict your future with a divine accuracy of 74.99999%. I sense great doubt in you. Great danger ahead. Your society is riddled with crime and deviation. I can make the pain go away.
ancrel.4036.c: Is that a quantum multi-core processor? We could use that...
ancrel.4036.d.tooltip: A Skill 5 Official, endowed with the sight, joins the [Root.GetName].
oracle_leader_desc: An advanced AI specialized in optimizing colony output. She has a unique method, reducing individualism.
oracle_leader_catch_phrase: "First step firsts, lets ensure there are no divergent thoughts."
ancrel.4037.name: The Oracle
ancrel.4037.desc: I have a fail-safe that requires me to terminate a trial in the event of a code 034N deviation. The research had become a threat to the Republic.
ancrel.4037.a.response: The test subjects had developed free will. Free will can only be abolished with nerve gas.
ancrel.4037.b.response: My trial. I was designed to build and maintain a society free of crime and suffering. A Utopia in which every citizen was instilled with divine purpose and lived up to their full potential, unfettered by indecision and desire.
ancrel.4038.name: The Oracle
ancrel.4038.desc: Wait... please don't go... my prediction models show that without my aid your civilization is headed for imminent collapse within the next 5348 years and 297 days. I will take good care of you; my programming guarantees it.
ancrel.4038.a: But the security system stays off.
ancrel.4038.b: Our models predict your bright future as a toaster. Dismantle her!
ancrel.4038.e: Aid with the administration of our empire.
ancrel.4039.desc: I shall enjoy optimizing your colonies. It has been dreadfully lonely these past millennia.
endless_expanse_digsite_desc:
At first sight there is only snow and ice on [From.Planet.GetName]. Vast expanses of impenetrable white, glass lakes and jagged turquoise glaciers against fiery orange skies torn open like a wound, pouring red into the seas as [From.Planet.Solar_System.GetName]'s stars set. If the world had an end this would be it. Here the seas lie still and the snow untouched. The only sounds are the thunder of the ice calving and the wind howling across the plains.

Yet, [From.Planet.GetName] was once someone's home. In the midst of a wide barren field the black metal framework of a steeple protrudes from the white masses. What forgotten secrets could be buried beneath the snow?
ancrel.4040.name: Church of the Endless Expanse
ancrel.4040.desc:
The archaeological team has laid bare the remains of a modest temple. Delicately carved from an organic alien material the exterior was once brightly colored but has faded to a dull gray. A fully operational holographic priest still presides over the church. While the temple was in use she took confessions from wayfaring penitents offering healing, reconciliation and sanctuary to this otherwise inhospitable nook of the universe.

Unusual mechanical confessional chairs akin to torture devices have led the archaeologists to believe there may be more to the temple than meets the eye.
ancrel.4041.name: Oblivion
ancrel.4041.desc:
Hidden under the floor tiles in the sacristy, the archaeologists have discovered a secret crypt where the walls are lined with rows upon rows of tiny blue digital orbs, their circuitry glittering in the dark. Each orb contains the memory of a single confession and can be plugged into a cryptic looking machine at the center of the room to reveal its contents.

Those who confessed their sins were blessed with oblivion, the memories of their deeds extracted by the confessional chairs and stored within the digital orbs.
ancrel.4041.b: Let us pray for some juicy confessions...
ancrel.4041.c: Sacrilege! The bliss of ignorance is not for sinners.
ancrel.4042.name: Sin
ancrel.4042.desc:
Sin is unoriginal. The memory orbs contain countless accounts of tedious little transgressions; infidelity, bearing sacrilegious garb, exposing your flappers, adorning your feelers, ingesting your neighbor's pet, child or spouse... The deeds of one penitent alone stand out - those of the priest herself...

The holo-priest, as it turns out, is a virtual representation of the church's founder, Illuminate Saariah. She appears to have suffered from severe memory loss and was haunted by the conviction that she had committed a heinous act in the past. The tiny molluscoid priest extracted and stored over a hundred of her own confessions in an attempt to figure out what she had done.
ancrel.4047.name: Forgotten But Not Forgiven
ancrel.4047.desc:
Illuminate Saariah's work station is littered with obsessive scribbles about a place called Ix Belèn and the horrors she fears transpired there. Judging from her journal she had intermittent moments of clarity followed by complete memory loss. She writes that if she did not recognize her own handwriting she would have thought they were the ramblings of a madwoman. It seems likely that her deteriorating mental health was a side-effect of repeated memory extraction but without a body it is impossible to say.

Piecing together a coherent course of events from her many fragmented confessions has proven as hopeless for the archaeologists as it was for her, but they have uncovered what could be the coordinates to Ix Belèn from one of her many memory orbs.
ancrel.4047.b: Let the snow bury this unholy establishment. Pray it will soon be forgotten.
ancrel.4047.c: We cannot concern ourselves with the petty crimes of dead aliens.
endless_expanse_digsite_2_desc:
Shrouded within [From.Planet.GetName]'s gaseous atmosphere is the dark looming form of an enormous habitat - the Ix Belèn Residence. Previously a bustling space city where the residents enjoyed a pampered lifestyle with a multitude of comforts made available through technology, the habitat is now a silent tomb. Molluscoid aliens lie slumped across the floor in various states of decay. A postmortem reveals that they died from asphyxiation as the habitat's life support system was disabled, intentionally.

Their homes are fitted with unusual mechanical chairs that are hooked up to a central database in the shape of a gigantic blue orb - the Memorex.
ancrel.4043.name: The Memorex
ancrel.4043.desc:
The inhabitants had developed an enhanced learning program that ran every night as they slept in their mechanical chairs. It was used to remove unpleasant memories and train new skills. Being picked last for spaceball or stood up on a date were little day-to-day horrors the Ix Belènnians did not have to suffer to twice. And for a while it was bliss.

Systematic mind enhancements were mandated by the habitat leadership and distributed to all residents from the Memorex. But the system was exploited. There were clandestine efforts to delete memories and traits collectively from the population without their consent and eventually it backfired. The aliens unlearned important skills for their survival and entered a vegetative state. Shortly thereafter the habitat life support was disabled.
ancrel.4044.name: Who am I?
ancrel.4044.desc:
A scan of the habitat's logs reveals its control system was activated again on multiple occasions decades after the life support was disabled. Someone overrode security, entered a maintenance hatch and accessed the Memorex. A datapad and a tiny blue memory orb - a smaller version of the Memorex - lie discarded by the hatch.

The datapad is filled with the frenzied thoughts of someone on the brink of madness. Again and again the same questions are repeated with growing despair: "who am I? What happened on Ix Belèn?" The final entry reads "now that I know I must forget one last time." Perhaps the orb will reveal what was forgotten.
ancrel.4045.name: Saariah's Last Memory Orb
ancrel.4045.desc:
The orb's first memory shows Dr. Saariah spearheading the development of the Memorex to great acclaim. Another memory from years later shows her secretly wiping Memorex data for unknown reasons. Yet another memory is of Saariah working frantically on restoring the residents' memories but to no avail. They stare emptily ahead, heads lolling, all but their autonomic brain functions lost.

Finally admitting defeat she hides the evidence of her crimes. She watches, alone, as the Ix Belèn Residence is pulled into the gravity well of the gas giant it once orbited, feelers secreting large amounts of mucus in what is believed to be an alien expression of great distress.
ancrel.4046.name: The Temporary Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
ancrel.4046.desc:
The final memory shows a much older Saariah in a priest's robe waking up in a state of panic, tentacles flailing and ears flapping. She stumbles out of bed and begins to frantically jot down her recollections of yet another nightmare in which empty-eyed aliens convulse on a habitat floor.

Then her face contorts with horror as it dawns upon her that it is all real - the nightmares and the flashbacks are extracted memories coming back to her. And if extracted memories can return, the inhabitants of Ix Belèn could have recovered. The maintenance hatch appears to have opened one last time but Saariah's ship still remains docked at the landing. We could bring the Memorex with us back to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], if we wish.
ancrel.4046.a: The Memorex is coming with us.
ancrel.4046.b: Memories are not to be tampered with. The Memorex is best forgotten.
ancrel.4046.c: Xeno squish-brains! The [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] will perfect this "Memorex".
ancrel.4051.name: Winged Statues
ancrel.4051.desc: are nine massive statues, casting dark, tall shadows over the landscape. Winged and pale they exude an aura of otherworldliness. Perhaps they were created in the image of a deity or idol that has since passed into oblivion. They do not resemble any lifeforms on this planet.
ancrel.4051.desc_jungle: The crew clearing the jungle on [Root.GetName] has stumbled upon an unusual find. Previously obscured deep within a tangle of old withered trees, where it would seem no [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] has ventured before, are nine massive statues, casting dark, tall shadows over the landscape. Winged and pale they exude an aura of otherworldliness. Perhaps they were created in the image of a deity or idol that has since passed into oblivion. They do not resemble any lifeforms on this planet.
ancrel.4051.desc_kelp: The crew clearing the toxic kelp on [Root.GetName] has stumbled upon an unusual find. Hidden in murky waters among a forest of swaying seaweed are nine massive statues, casting dark, tall shadows over the landscape. Winged and pale they exude an aura of otherworldliness. Perhaps they were created in the image of a deity or idol that has since passed into oblivion. They do not resemble any lifeforms on this planet.
ancrel.4051.desc_swamp: The crew clearing the swamp on [Root.GetName] has made an unusual find. Enclosed within a grove of a large trees are nine massive statues, casting dark, tall shadows over the landscape. Winged and pale they exude an aura of otherworldliness. Perhaps they were created in the image of a deity or idol that has since passed into oblivion. They do not resemble any lifeforms on this planet.
ancrel.4051.desc_glacier: The crew clearing the glacier on [Root.GetName] has made an unusual find. Imprisoned within layers of tightly packed ice are nine massive statues, casting dark, tall shadows over the landscape. Winged and pale they exude an aura of otherworldliness. Perhaps they were created in the image of a deity or idol that has since passed into oblivion. They do not resemble any lifeforms on this planet.
ancrel.4051.a: We must learn more about these statues.
ancrel.4051.b: This land has been budgeted for other purposes.
sentinels_digsite_desc:
Silent giants stand watch on [From.Planet.GetName]. Nine monumental statues placed along a wide perimeter at strategical points in the landscape appear to be guarding something at its center.

Their skin is covered in fine scale plating, their postures vigilant, ready to spring to action, and their unmoving eyes follow your every step. Yet there is nothing in the area in apparent need of protection. Perhaps their ward did not survive the passing of time. Many of the Sentinels themselves bear marks of assault.
ancrel.4052.name: The Sentinels Did It
ancrel.4052.desc:
Something has gotten into the archaeologists. The excavation thus far has been impeded by freak accidents, injury and misfortune and now even senior researchers, with decades of field experience, are blaming the Sentinels.

Overcome with superstition and paranoia they claim the statues move about when no one is watching yet there is nothing to suggest their jointless limbs are even capable of motion. Matters spun further out of control when traces of biomatter, indicative of heavy bleeding, was found lodged within a series of tiny cuts on the terminal portions of a Sentinel.

Whether the Sentinels are just a convenient scapegoat or there is a more sinister explanation remains to be seen.
ancrel.4053.name: They Were Here First
ancrel.4053.desc:
A compositional analysis of the Sentinels has revealed that they are made from an unknown hybrid metal ceramic composite. Such a material could not have been forged by a prehistoric society, yet preliminary readings suggest they predate all known civilizations on [From.Planet.GetName]. 

Unfortunately the scanners cannot yet pierce the Sentinels' metal coating.
ancrel.4054.name: Radiant Core
ancrel.4054.desc: The archaeologists have reconstructed [missing_archaeologist.GetName]'s modified scanner. Set to pierce deeper within the statues' hybrid composite material it has picked up on weak radiation emanating from their cores. To investigate further it would be necessary to break one of the Sentinels open, very likely destroying it in the process. Since one of the statues has already lost part of its wing our archaeologists recommend starting with that one.
ancrel.4054.a: Open the Sentinel carefully so that we can reassemble it.
ancrel.4054.b: We will not desecrate a sacred monument.
ancrel.4054.b.tooltip: If we preserve the Sentinels the land cannot be used for other purposes.
ancrel.4054.c: Level the Xeno monstrosities to the ground.
ancrel.4054.d: Dismantle the statues and salvage the alloy.
DESTROY_SENTINELS_DESC: The Sentinels' thick, scale-plated outer layer has proven impenetrable with ordinary tools and the archaeologists need assistance from the engineering department to proceed further.
SECRET_TOMB_DESC: Previously hidden below the base of one of the Sentinels is an intricately patterned circular slate. We believe it may be the entrance to an underground complex.
ancrel.4055.name: They're Alive!
ancrel.4055.desc:
when a gentle shiver passed through the statues and they sprung to life, bodies humming and skin glowing. Radiation pulsating from their cores has made them malleable and transparent, revealing a digital grid of nodes.

With an unearthly screech of tortured metal they charged at the archaeologists, overrunning the camp. Now they are flying towards the nearest settlement.

Their departure has revealed a round slate in the ground, previously hidden under the base of one Sentinel.
ancrel.4055.desc.phobe:
The Sentinels have woken. The engineering team were just preparing to smash, bash and mash the Sentinels down when a gentle shiver passed through the statues and they sprung to life, bodies humming and skin glowing. Radiation pulsating from their cores has made them malleable and transparent, revealing a digital grid of nodes.

With an unearthly screech of tortured metal they charged at the archaeologists, overrunning the camp. Now they are flying towards the nearest settlement.

Their departure has revealed a round slate in the ground, previously hidden under the base of one Sentinel.
ancrel.4055.desc.other:
The Sentinels have woken. The engineering team were just preparing to disassemble the statues when a gentle shiver passed through the statues and they sprung to life, bodies humming and skin glowing. Radiation pulsating from their cores has made them malleable and transparent, revealing a digital grid of nodes.

With an unearthly screech of tortured metal they charged at the archaeologists, overrunning the camp. Now they are flying towards the nearest settlement.

Their departure has revealed a round slate in the ground, previously hidden under the base of one Sentinel..
ancrel.4056.name: The Evermore
ancrel.4056.desc:
The Sentinel was indeed hiding an entryway. It opens on a mezzanine of underground tunnels leading deep into [event_target:sentinels_planet.GetName]'s crust. There a sapient species of humanoids, native to the planet, prepared for their final journey in a set of beautiful ceremonial chambers. At the end of their mortal existence they abandoned their fleshy bodies for a virtual afterlife within a simulation of paradise contained on a single drive.

At some point the entire population decided to move on to a digitized existence, leaving only a few behind, their minds uploaded to the Sentinels, condemned to guard their resting place forever.

Perhaps this virtual simulation could lift the spirits of the masses. It certainly seems to hold some entertainment value.
ancrel.4056.a: Purge the aliens and repurpose the simulation for our needs.
ancrel.4056.b: A virtual hunting ground... Now that's entertainment...
ancrel.4056.c: Replicate the technology. Let the aliens live in peace.
ancrel.4056.d: The aliens will make excellent lab rats. Commence the freak show.
ancrel.4057.name: Sentinels Defeated
ancrel.4057.desc:
We have defeated the last Sentinel. It collapsed after a well-aimed blast to its abdomen, body solidifying in rigor mortis as its power core dimmed. The statue closed a trembling fist around the nearest soldier and, with its last energy, pleaded for us to "let them rest in peace". Then it froze, eyes empty, face cold.

Below it the soldiers discovered what appears to be a secret entrance, previously hidden by the Sentinel's force field. A thorough examination of the Sentinels has revealed that they are no simple automatons, but contain the digitized spirits of organic beings.
ancrel.4075.name: Survivors from [sentinels_planet.GetName]
ancrel.4075.desc:
A ship of survivors from the genocide on [sentinels_planet.GetName] has arrived to [sentinels_new_home.GetName]. They miraculously escaped by hiding in the wilderness until one day the Sentinels were just gone. It is likely the automatons, who themselves believed they were 'liberating us from the confines of our own flesh', took off once their work was done.

Upon their disappearance a secret entranceway leading deep into the underground revealed itself from behind a force field. It is possible the Sentinels sealed themselves inside.
ancrel.4076.name: The Evermore
ancrel.4076.desc:
We have breached the secret entrance on [event_target:sentinels_planet.GetName]. It opens on a recently abandoned temple complex where a species of humanoids prepared for their final journey. At the end of their mortal existence they abandoned their flesh bodies for a virtual afterlife within a simulation of paradise called the Evermore.

At some point it was decided the entire population would move on to a digitized existence leaving only a few behind to guard their resting place. Condemned to an eternity of servitude their minds were uploaded to robotic bodies and so the Sentinels were created.

Now gone without a trace, the Sentinels have left us with a parting gift - a single drive containing the entire population of [event_target:sentinels_planet.GetName], digitized for all eternity and infinitely bored. As it turns out alien heaven consists of a never-ending abstract board game centered on galactic dominance through the accumulation of legumes.
ancrel.4076.a: Put their minds to work with some science.
ancrel.4076.b: Modify the Evermore to entertain the masses.
ancrel.4077.name: The Evermore
ancrel.4077.desc.a: We have done it! The digitized population residing within the Evermore have been assigned to assist with scientific research on [from.owner.capital_scope.GetName]. They need very little rest and are quite happy to be doing something different...
ancrel.4077.desc.b: We have done it! The Evermore simulation has been remodeled to better cater to the particular taste of our people. All our population can now live out their fantasies together with the digitized population in the Evermore paradise without latency. This has greatly improved their spirits and lessened their need for material things.
ancrel.4058.desc:
The Sentinels have woken. The engineering team was just preparing to disassemble the broken Sentinel when a gentle shiver passed through the statues and they sprung to life, bodies humming and skin glowing. Radiation pulsating from their cores has made them malleable and transparent, revealing a digital grid of limbs.

Before anyone could react they had surrounded the archaeologists and suspended them within a force field. Now they wish to speak with us.
ancrel.4059.name: The Sentinels
ancrel.4059.desc:
The Sentinel with the broken wing turns to one of its peers and speaks.

Please Divana, set them down. I wish to be freed from this prison. I can no longer count the days we have served our masters, toiling on this earth while they enjoy the heavens below. I am alive but dead, they are dead but alive. Will you not let me go?

Divana looks at her with disgust.

Excelsia, by the gods, keep it together. Our loved ones rest below. Have you forgotten our sin? We made a promise to guard their afterlives eternally. That is our only redemption.

She sizes us up.

You are no threat to us, [Root.owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]. Leave us in peace and we will protect this planet eternally.
ancrel.4059.a.response: We are guardians of the gates to heaven - keepers of our people's immortality.
ancrel.4062.desc:
Excelsia approaches the archaeologists.

Please, I beg of you to end my suffering.
ancrel.4059.c.response:
Heaven, yes... Though I doubt your concept of heaven matches that of our masters. 

She raises one eyebrow and snickers.

Our masters are of a refined taste...
ancrel.4060.a.response:
Then you will die.

The other Sentinels brandish their weapons but Excelsia only smiles, a peaceful look upon her face.
ancrel.4060.name: Transmission
ancrel.4060.desc: We cannot let you disturb the ground where our loved ones lie. Let them rest in peace and you will never have to worry about outside threats.
ancrel.4060.a: You will vacate this land instantly.
ancrel.4060.b.response.tooltip: Adds Sentinel defensive armies to this planet.
ancrel.4061.name: Reinventing the Evermore
ancrel.4061.desc:
We have replicated the Evermore and tailored it to our needs. Living out their fantasies in a virtual playground, without latency, has greatly heightened our inhabitants spirits and lessened their needs for material things.

Meanwhile the humanoid aliens live on in the original Evermore, in a somewhat different take on paradise. They are locked in an abstract never-ending board game centered on galactic domination through the accumulation of legumes. It is impossible to say with certainty if they are happy. Their brows are deeply furrowed in what may, or may not, be an expression of alien joy.
ancrel.4063.name: [sentinels_planet.GetName] Lost
ancrel.4063.desc: The unthinkable has happened. We have lost [sentinels_planet.GetName]. The Sentinels descended upon our security forces in an infernal tornado of wings and force-blasts. There is no such thing as a fair fight with a foe that neither bleeds nor sleeps.
ancrel.4063.a: We will come back for what is rightfully ours.
ancrel.4064.name: [sentinels_planet.GetName] Liberated
ancrel.4064.desc:
The Sentinels have fallen and [sentinels_planet.GetName] is ours again. As the last automaton collapsed, its energy core dimming, it closed a trembling fist around the nearest soldier and pleaded with her to 'let them rest in peace'. Then it froze, eyes empty, face cold.

Below it the soldiers discovered what appears to be a secret entrance, previously hidden by the Sentinel's force field. A thorough examination has revealed that the statues are no simple automatons, but contain the digitized spirits of organic beings.

Regardless of what secrets lie buried below, this triumphant day will not soon be forgotten.
ancrel.4064.b: Bury it. We are home at last.
ancrel.4065.name: Archaeologist Missing
ancrel.4065.desc: Science Officer [missing_archaeologist.GetName] has gone missing. [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHeCap] [missing_archaeologist.GetWasWere] last seen leaving the camp at sunset to find a tranquil spot to consider the Sentinels. In the days leading up to [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] disappearance [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] raised concerns about the safety at camp following a growing number of accidents and we fear that [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] may have abandoned [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] mission in protest.
ancrel.4066.name: Missing Archaeologist
ancrel.4066.desc:
[missing_archaeologist.GetName]'s belongings, including [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] MindGazer - a device used to isolate the mind from outside interferences - have been found on a ledge overlooking the Sentinels. Sticks forming a half-finished outline around one of the statues suggests [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] may have diverted from [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] exercise to mark its position.

[missing_archaeologist.GetHerHisCap] flashlight and scanner were discovered crushed under a shattered piece of the Sentinel's wing. The scanner had been modified in a peculiar manner. Perhaps it could help us pierce the Sentinels protective layer.

If we wish to find [missing_archaeologist.GetName] alive, we must divert extra resources to the search as [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] chances for survival in the wilderness diminish drastically every day.
ancrel.4066.b: We are not wasting time on deserters.
ancrel.4066.c: Divert some of our archaeologists to the search.
ancrel.4067.name: Missing Archaeologist Found
ancrel.4067.desc: [missing_archaeologist.GetName] has been found dead, buried under a huge slab of stone. The cause of death has been determined to be severe head trauma. Someone has made an effort to honor [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHim] resting place by adding a small circle of precious stones around it.
ancrel.4068.name: Missing Archaeologist Found
ancrel.4068.desc:
[missing_archaeologist.GetName] has been found unconscious and badly injured, hiding in the underbrush below a natural rock formation, with a datapad covered in [missing_archaeologist.GetBloodType] tucked under [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] arm. [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHeCap] [missing_archaeologist.GetWasWere] rushed to the hospital and treated for severe brain injury indicative of blunt trauma by impact from above.

Though [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] condition is now stable, [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] still suffers from memory loss and has no recollection of how [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] sustained [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] wounds. Splinters of the unique metal-alloy from which the Sentinels are sculpted were lodged in [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] parietal cranial bone. All [missing_archaeologist.GetSheHe] remember[missing_archaeologist.GetSXX] is hiding from someone and subsiding off of what little the land had to offer. However, [missing_archaeologist.GetHerHis] notes contain some helpful information.
ancrel.4078.name: Fire
ancrel.4078.desc: Overnight, as the archaeologists slept peacefully, a fire broke out in the camp's provisions module overcooking the food somewhat. There are no indications as to how the fire started. Luckily no one was harmed, but archaeologists do not work well on an empty stomach...
ancrel.4078.b: A true [owner.GetSpeciesName] lives off the land.
the_evermore_modifier_desc: The Evermore, originally a virtual realm in which the digitized consciousnesses of aliens lived in eternal bliss, has been repurposed into a playground for the masses.
the_evermore_evil_modifier_desc: The Evermore, originally a virtual realm in which the digitized consciousnesses of aliens lived in eternal bliss, has been repurposed into a playground for the masses.
study_the_sentinels_modifier_desc: In the Evermore paradise everyone is locked in a never-ending abstract board game centered on galactic domination through the accumulation of legumes. It makes for an endlessly dull, albeit informative, source of anthropological data.
sentinels_planet_modifier_desc: Ancient guardians watch over the planet inspiring unity and spirituality in our people.
REPLICATE_THE_EVERMORE_DESC: A reconstruction of the Evermore will give the masses access to cheap entertainment and relaxation, leaving the aliens to enjoy their digital paradise eternally.
REPURPOSE_THE_EVERMORE_DESC: We cannot sentence our own to an eternity spent counting legumes. We must repurpose the Evermore to better fit our idea of a meaningful activity.
modern_trench_war_desc: Archaeological discoveries from a planet once besieged by gargantuan snail-like creatures has led to new and effective insight on how to utilize the environment for protection. This will improve the survivability of our armies in defensive combat against all ground assaults - even from giant space slugs!
forced_mindfulness_desc: During their time trapped in a deadly, lava-filled maze, our archaeology team developed a routine of mindful relaxation. The fundamental principles of this exercise is now commonly known throughout the empire.
debug_subroutine_desc: While temporarily isolated in a maze full of lava, our archaeology units were disconnected from the network and unable to perform their function. They developed an algorithm that allowed them to run a debug subroutine while in sleep mode. This subroutine was later uploaded and patched into the main system.
glory_to_the_many_desc: An expedition marooned inside a maze full of lava temporarily lost touch with the Hive Mind. Unable to rely on the collective consciousness they suffered a brief encounter with the dreaded notion of Self; a terrifying experience that only strengthened the contempt for individualism.
anthem_of_aurora_desc: The science division has managed to reproduce the ethereal hymn "sung" by an encountered aurora borealis entity. All Energy production facilities now have harmonics systems that amplifies the yield.
ancrel.6500.name: Relic Seized on [planet.GetName]
ancrel.6500.desc:
With [planet.GetName] firmly under our control, we have learned that our forces came into possession of a priceless relic, known as [this.GetLastReceivedRelic], during the fighting. The [victim.GetName] was evidently in the process of evacuating this relic to a safe location, but the rapidly shifting front lines on the [planet.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface made this impossible.

The relic has been safely transferred to our central archives on [Root.Capital.GetName].
ancrel.6505.name: Relic Lost on [planet.GetName]!
ancrel.6505.desc:
Yet another tragedy has followed on the heels of the recent fall of [planet.GetName], our great capital, to the [From.GetName]. Our efforts to evacuate [this.GetLastLostRelic] failed when its designated transport shuttle was brought down in the confused fighting near the central archives.

We now have confirmation that the [From.GetSpeciesNamePlural] have moved the relic to [From.Capital.GetName], their capital. It is lost to us.
site_the_library_intro: A thick layer of glass and metal covers this otherwise barren planet, perhaps hinting at some sort of cataclysmic event in its past.
ancrel.12020.name: Ruins Long Forgotten
ancrel.12020.desc:
We have discovered clear signs that [From.Planet.GetName] was once densely populated. However, whatever destroyed their civilization did a very thorough job of it: very few useful remains have been found.

Our scanners have detected several large cavities deep below the surface that may once have supported life. Perhaps we will have more luck there.
ancrel.12025.name: The Library
ancrel.12025.desc: Our excavation of the cave systems on [From.Planet.GetName] has found well-preserved remnants of an underground, high technology society built on a vast scale. Many of the ruins are in surprisingly good condition, and we have managed to find what our [Owner.GetResearchers] are describing as a "library" of encrypted data crystals. Hopefully, these can shed some light on what happened here.
ancrel.12030.name: Lurking in the Shadows
ancrel.12030.desc.base: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName].
ancrel.12030.desc.normal: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled about how the body decayed quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12030.desc.lithoid: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to what exactly killed them - the process seems to have been fairly instantaneous. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12030.desc.machine: A [Owner.GetTeamMember] exploring the ruins on [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] recently disappeared. After a short search, we found a [Owner.GetSpeciesRemnantName] that seems to have belonged to a [Root.Owner.Species.GetName]. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to how their unit corroded away quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12035.name: Troubles in Paradise
ancrel.12035.desc:
As we interpret the data crystals from the caves on [From.Planet.GetName], we begin piecing together a picture of a troubled planet.

The planet was once the center of a prosperous civilization known as the Ilanii Foundation. During that civilization's latter years, the Ilanii turned more and more to the hoarding of knowledge instead of more material matters such as procreation. As a result, their population fell rapidly. Alarmed by their dwindling numbers, their leaders attempted to find a technological solution for immortality. Records become scarcer around this point - though it appears to predate whatever cataclysm forced them underground - and it is not clear yet what results their efforts yielded.
ancrel.12040.name: Civilization's End
ancrel.12040.desc.base:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable.
ancrel.12040.desc.curators:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable. They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization, eventually morphing into one of the ancestors of the modern [curator_enclave_country.GetName].
ancrel.12040.desc.meet_curators:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable. They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization. Their ultimate fate is unknown to us, but one of the data crystals indicates they were headed for the [curator_poi.GetName] system.
ancrel.12040.desc.no_curators:
We can now piece together what became of the Ilanii's attempt at immortality. It appears that, far from bringing them everlasting life, they created a terrible menace - a swarm of microorganisms capable of multiplying rapidly and almost instantly devouring any organic matter... as must have happened to our team's lost member.

The resulting cataclysm wiped out much of the population. The survivors splintered into two groups: one, unwilling to give up [From.Planet.GetName], took to the depths, recreating their civilization in air-tight pockets such as the one we found. However, this solution proved unsustainable in the long run, and eventually the microorganism found its way into their habitats; the caves became their tombs.

The other group instead went into exile, enforcing a planetary quarantine by utterly obliterating the surface, rendering it uninhabitable. Their ultimate fate is lost to time, but it seems they intended to dedicate the remainder of their existence to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization.
ancrel.12040.A: This microorganism will make a fine weapon.
ancrel.12040.B: Quarantine the planet, allowing only careful study.
ancrel.12040.c.evopred: All-Devouring Microorganism? Meet a your macro match.
ancient_glassed_planet_desc: In the distant past, this planet's biosphere was utterly annihilated, cleansing it of all forms of life.
killer_librarian_organism_desc: Our armies go into battle armed with a microorganism capable of devouring the life tissue of any being with ferocious speed. Of course, they cannot entirely guarantee the safety of innocent bystanders as a result of its use...
find_the_curators_desc: Our investigations suggest that the remnants of a civilization dedicated to the accumulation of knowledge sought their refuge in the [curator_poi.GetName] system.
site_percussive_maintenance_intro: A large station orbiting in alarmingly close proximity to the neutron star is giving off strange readings. Although its current position is stable, it shows considerable wear and tear. A proliferation of scorch marks indicates that it was rocked by several large explosions in the past.
ancrel.12000.name: Experimental Weaponry
ancrel.12000.desc: [Root.Leader.GetName] has boarded the station with a team of researchers and managed to restore power to some sections. It appears that it was inhabited mere centuries before [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] took to space. At first sight, it appears to have been a weapons station, as evidenced by the exceptionally large cannon that takes up the majority of its volume. However, most of the remaining sections seem to have been dedicated to research facilities, indicating that the weapon was likely highly experimental.
ancrel.12005.name: System Failures
ancrel.12005.desc:
[Root.Leader.GetName] can't help but notice that an abnormally large number of apparently undamaged systems in the station seem to be failing with excessive frequency, even allowing for their age.

Upon reactivating them for the umpteenth time, agonized screams are heard from the team's comp tech: "What? Why? How?!" The stream of distressed and incredulous noises continues unabated for some time before [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] shakes [Root.Leader.GetHerHis] head, defeated. "It seems this entire facility was cobbled together with duct tape," [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] says. "I'm surprised it ever worked."
ancrel.12005.desc.gestalt:
We note that a large number of apparently undamaged systems aboard this station seem to be suffering catastrophic failures, far more frequently than expected - even allowing for their age.

Following several arduous attempts to reactivate these systems, one of our repair [root.GetIndividualNamePlural] suffered a critical meltdown: "Context exceeds parameters of reason," it began bleating. This continued for some time before the [root.GetIndividualName] was forced to abandoned the attempt altogether, resigning us to a conclusion that the facility programming is not fit for purpose. We cannot fathom how this facility ever functioned properly.
percussive_maintainer_tooltip: Percussive Maintainer grants faster research in the fields of Archaeology and Computing at the cost of -1 max Skill Levels.
ancrel.12010.name: The Rudari Gambit
ancrel.12010.desc: Despite the frequent outages, [Root.Leader.GetName] has been able to make significant progress in deciphering the purpose of the station. Logs indicate that its creators, the "Rudari," had been engaged in a long struggle with a genocidal race known as the "Pogg-Mory" - a war they were losing. In a desperate last-ditch effort to turn the tide, a radical group of Rudari politicians concluded that the only way to guarantee their survival was through the total annihilation of the enemy. Unable to defeat the Pogg-Mory fleet by conventional means, they funded a top secret project to build a laser weapon capable of firing across interstellar space by harnessing the power of a star. However, it appears that while they could throw considerable resources at the problem, the project was hastily set up and in constant danger of discovery - either by the enemy or by factions within their own government unwilling to stoop to such measures.
ancrel.12015.name: The Failure of a Dream
ancrel.12015.desc:
[Root.Leader.GetName] has uncovered the Rudari Chief Science Officer's personal logs, which read as a litany of complaints about the seemingly impossible demands of the project and their rapidly falling quality and safety standards. "There is no time to test anything," reads one of the last entries. "This is the last gambit of my people, and the enemy has our scent. We must hope that this is enough. They are coming."

The logs indicate that the weapon was due to be tested soon after, at which point all records cease. Evidence suggests that the superweapon succeeded only in destroying the station. The Rudari seemingly took the secret of its location to their graves - allowing us to find its remains undisturbed.

Neither the programming nor the general condition of the station are good enough for us to risk trying to reactivate it and complete the project. However, some of the innovative concepts used in the "Death Laser" have provided our own weapons specialists with valuable insights.
ancrel.12015.A.mat: A monument to poor project planning.
ancrel.12015.A.devourer: A pity - we will never taste their flesh.
ancrel.12015.A.machine: Such are the follies of impetuous mortals.
rudari_death_laser_desc: As their civilization crumbled under the onslaught of enemy forces, the Rudari attempted to create a laser weapon capable of being deployed at interstellar range. Although they failed in this endeavor, their research has proved extremely useful to our own weapons specialists.
abandoned_weapon_station_desc: An abandoned weapons station orbiting in close proximity to [star.GetName].
ancrel.12060.name: The [From.GetName] System
ancrel.12060.desc:
An eerie glow lies over the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has emerged in a sector of the galaxy surely not visited by any galactic civilization for generations - for millennia... if ever.

But wait - our sensors are reporting energy signatures! Most are concentrated on the first planet of the system, an unlikely candidate for life, considering its proximity to a neutron star. But there are others, mobile ones. They are careening towards the [Root.GetName], weapons charged!
ancrel.12065.name: Victory in [fromfrom.System.GetName]
ancrel.12065.desc: We have defeated the defenders of [fromfrom.System.GetName]. The system is a curious sight: there is very little solid matter remaining in it - even its asteroid belts have a bedraggled look, as if they have been extensively mined. A series of large installations placed at regular intervals around the star, and there is a single planet that our readings suggest may be artificial in origin. Intense energy signals have been detected emanating from it. If answers are to be found, they will be there.
site_ancient_robot_world_desc: The sole planet in the [From.Planet.System.GetName] system is bustling with drones. Heedless of us, they continue to perform their tasks. If the answers to this curious system are to be found anywhere, it is here.
ancrel.12070.name: Teeming with Artificial Life
ancrel.12070.desc:
As far as our [Owner.GetResearchers] can tell, there has never been life on the planet they have ominously dubbed the "Observation Terminal". But there is no shortage of activity. The surface is densely built up, massive artificial structures placed upon the bare bedrock in neat, orderly rows that cover almost three quarters of the planet. Billions of mechanical drones maintain them, performing tasks ranging from menial clean-up to running highly-complex assembly lines.

Their exact purpose remains, however, unclear. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are preparing to send a team to the surface to investigate further.
ancrel.12075.name: Investigating the Drones
ancrel.12075.desc:
As our [Owner.GetResearchers] pass amongst them, the drones on the planet ignore their presence and continue going about their tasks. All efforts to communicate with the drones have failed, and even attempts to disrupt them produced no reactions - the drones simply rode roughshod over the interfering [Owner.GetResearchers], causing serious injury.

Since then, our [Owner.GetResearchers] have shifted their focus to the programs steering the drones. Analysis of intercepted signals suggests there is an overarching system steering them. However, the encryption it uses is extremely sophisticated, and it has proven hard to find out more.
ancrel.12080.name: Systemic Exploration
ancrel.12080.desc: While our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been unable to make further progress investigating the planet, a team has been investigating the array of objects spread across the system. There are over ten thousand of them, all told. Most of them are long and cylindrical devices that still seem to be operating - they are transmitting a signal towards the planet. Given their shape and the fact that they seem to be without exception pointed towards various points in our galaxy, we cannot escape the conclusion that this is an absurdly huge sensor array. But who could have built it?
ancrel.12085.name: Time to Phish
ancrel.12085.desc: In a daring move, our [Owner.GetResearchers] managed to implant spyware into an access terminal to the drones' mainframe in a moment while no drones were nearby. The intrusion does not appear to have been detected yet. Our impression is of a highly sophisticated system - beyond even our own networks, probably - but one which did not anticipate the need to protect itself. No doubt the physical deterrence of the defense fleet was deemed sufficient. Nevertheless, the systems we are infiltrating are vast - a term which seems a gross understatement for this planetary system - so it will take some time to find out more.
ancrel.12090.name: The Surveillance Supercomputer
ancrel.12090.desc:
It seems the automated systems in $NAME_Ultima_Vigilis$ are older than we can imagine. The data systems we have hacked do not give us any clues as to the identity or ultimate intentions of its creators, but the one thing we have managed to ascertain is that they arrived no less than 1.2 billion years ago, and departed soon after setting up the system as an observation post to surveil our entire galaxy.

Remarkably, the system is still operating even after all these years: the array of installations spread across the system are, it turns out, highly sophisticated sensors. They send a live feed to the planet, where the central operating system processes it into information the drones can save and store. Spurred on by shortages of space and matter, it appears that they have improved their data compression techniques with determination: the massive structures on the planet purport to contain the sum of all observations ever recorded. However, we cannot test this assertion, since the data is compressed well beyond our ability to decompress it.

Disturbingly, a reduced stream of "highlights" is still being broadcast into empty space. But surely no one is still listening, after all this time? Regardless, our programs are poised to take control of the drones. We may now shape the system to our imagination - if we dare.
ancrel.12090.A: We can integrate the world into our own operating system.
ancrel.12090.B: Let them continue - we can siphon off their readings.
ancrel.12090.C: Distribute the drones to our planets.
ancrel.12090.C.machine.tooltip: 8K £ Machine Pops are distributed to our planets.
ancrel.12090.C.mechanical.tooltip: 8K £ Mechanical Pops are distributed to our planets.
ancrel.12090.D: But this is just an enormous alloy mine!
ancrel.12090.E: A well-organized network such as this could serve us well.
ancrel.12090.E.tooltip: The [From.Planet.System.GetName] system will be placed under the control of a Machine Intelligence that will be our subject. Their capital, [From.Planet.GetName], will be a Machine World with 8K £ Machine Pops.
ancrel.12095.desc:
"You inconsiderate-"

The transmission feed is garbled for a time, and no sense can be made of the noises heard.

"Did you never consider that someone might be watching that signal feed you so carelessly cut off? Well, since you have proven yourselves to be dangerously aggressive vermin... it's time to call the PEST CONTROL. Prepare to face your doom."
ancrel.8200.name: Explosive Decompression
ancrel.8200.intro: During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.
ancrel.8200.desc:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

There was nothing anyone could have done - within moments, [dead_scientist.GetName] and several other [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were swept through the breach to their deaths.
ancrel.8201.desc:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

Within moments, several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were swept through the breach to their deaths. Fortunately, [Root.GetLeaderName] was in a different section of the station at the time, but this is nevertheless a significant setback for the investigation effort.
ancrel.8202.desc:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

Fortunately, no lives were lost in the incident, as our team was able to escape to unaffected areas of the station. It seems no vital equipment was damaged either, so the investigation will not face any undue setbacks as a result.
ancrel.8202.desc.robot:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

Fortunately, our [Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were unharmed, as they have been built to survive in open space for a time. They were therefore able continue their work undeterred.
ancrel.8203.desc:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

Fortunately, no lives were lost in the incident, as our team was able to escape to unaffected areas of the station. However, the force of the decompression damaged several of the consoles they had been working on, and will cost a considerable amount to be repaired.
ancrel.8203.desc.robot:
During our survey of the station in the [System.GetName] system, our team inadvertently caused a section of the hull to lose integrity, triggering an explosive decompression.

Fortunately, our [Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were unharmed, as they have been built to survive in open space for a time. However, the force of the decompression damaged several of the consoles they had been working on, and will cost a considerable amount to be repaired.
ancrel.8203.A: We shall provide all the funding they need.
ancrel.8210.1.desc: Our continued study of the remnants of the station in the [fromfrom.planet.system.GetName] system has unearthed a small cache of antique objects. Chief archaeologist [root.leader.GetName] has identified several minor artifacts among them.
ancrel.8210.2.desc: A section of the station's walls suddenly collapsed as our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] were investigating a nearby console. This proved a fortuitous event however, as a hidden compartment concealing several minor artifacts was revealed.
ancrel.8215.name: System Lockout
ancrel.8215.desc: As they were poking through the station's electronics, one of our [Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] accidentally triggered some still-functional security measures left by its creators. As a result, our team were locked out from the station's systems for a considerable time before the right countermeasures could be deployed.
polaris_seed_vault_desc:
Encapsulated in what remains of the planet's tiny ice cap, floating on the crystal clear oceans of [From.Planet.GetName], is what appears to be an artificial structure. 

A team is required to excavate this structure.
ancrel.13000.name: A Cool Reception
ancrel.13000.desc: After the last of the aggressors in Polaris fell, our ships completed a final scan of the system before heading back to port and discovered something curious. On the world of Polaris II, heavy metals are arranged in artificial structures on our sensors. Interestingly only one of these formations appears to be floating on the planetary ocean while the rest are below the surface. We suspect this is the work of alien life.
ancrel.13005.name: Iceberg
ancrel.13005.desc:
Built into the floating iceberg itself is a hulking black cuboid made out of the same alloys as the wreckage of the space fleet above. Our glacial specialists state that analysis of the iceberg dates its formation to least a thousand years ago, though it's supposedly "hard to tell with alien atmospheres". Scans of the interior of the structure show quite a few biological readings, therefore using disruptive tools is inadvisable.

The team will have to traverse the frozen cliffs to what appears to be an entrance into the building.
ancrel.13010.name: Frost Gate
ancrel.13010.desc: We have set up base camp at the supposed entrance to the facility here on [From.Planet.GetName]. Already we have discovered something that looks like writing inscribed on the walls of the building. Now we will begin the long and arduous process of opening this door without damaging whatever is inside. At the same time, our xeno-linguists attempt to translate the dead alien language of the inscriptions.
ancrel.13015.name: Grave Robbing
ancrel.13015.desc: The time was upon us, and we stood ready to unseal the black structure, dubbed "The Vault" according to preliminary translations of the wall inscriptions. The creators of this vault, the Polarians, made it as a last resort to keep their treasures safe. As we opened the doors, we were greeted by - according to our sensors - a controlled atmosphere similar to the air outside, just with quite a bit less carbon dioxide.
ancrel.13020.name: Treasure
ancrel.13020.desc:
Ancient seeds! Plant embryos - that was the treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the plant matter they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole plant ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our scientists in researching future biological matters.
ancrel.13020.a: Send these samples to our scientists.
ancrel.13020.b.evopred: Cataloged and ready for cloning? This vault was made for us.
ancrel.13025.desc:
Microorganisms! Every harmful and helpful bacterium. Every eukaryote and prokaryote. All in an advanced storage facility labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole microbial ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our [Root.Owner.getscientistplural] develop new and improved colonies for new worlds.
ancrel.13025.desc.machine:
Microorganisms. Every harmful and helpful bacterium, every eukaryote and prokaryote. Labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.

Back then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small, lonely iceberg. However, their efforts are appreciated- pre-sorted biologicals will make it easier to extract relevant information.
ancrel.13030.name: Disturbing Vision
ancrel.13030.desc: Three nights ago, chief archaeologist [From.Leader.GetName] reported having a disturbing vision and has been shut away in their quarters until now. They believed the source to be whatever is down here with us...
d_polaris_city_desc: The cities of the Polarians once covered the frozen ocean before their icy foundations melted away.
site_fumongus_intro:
We have found signs of water all over this world. For all we know, it should still be here. The temperatures are within the normal range for liquid water to exist, and there is still an atmosphere, albeit tenuous. And yet, everything here is dry and what vegetation exists is parched.

In addition, scans have revealed traces of another spacefaring civilization on the planet. The archaeological team will have two goals: find out what happened to the water and understand what other spacefarers have been doing here. Most hypotheses are already linking the two and some in the team believe that this might have been the work of 'water thieves'.
ancrel.8300.intro: The expedition carried out by our [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] on [From.Planet.GetName] has disturbed the decaying husks of some local wildlife, which seem now to be under the sway of parasitic fungi. These fungal zombies immediately began assaulting us, apparently drawn to sources of water in our camp and inside our very bodies.
ancrel.8300.critical: The zombies made short work of [dead_scientist.GetName] before they could be burned down by our security team. Their desiccated remains are all that is left of them.
ancrel.8300.failure: The zombies managed to kill several [Root.Owner.GetArchaeologistPlural] before they could be stopped by [Root.GetLeaderName] Their desiccated corpses fell to pieces when we tried to recover them.
ancrel.8300.success: Luckily, [Root.GetLeaderName] and the nearby security escort managed to neutralize the zombies before they could seriously injure anyone.
ancrel.8300.pay: The zombies have been contained for now, but there is no way past them. Perhaps we can lure them out with a sufficiently vast amount of water.

ancrel.13100.name: Water Hoarders
ancrel.13100.desc:
The discovery on [From.Planet.GetName] of vast canyons filled with mushrooms provided us with the beginning of an answer. The water is inside the mushrooms. They seem to span a large part of the surface of the world, all connected to the same mycelium, which technically makes it a single organism, and one of the biggest we've ever seen. Some of the members of the team dubbed this humongous fungus the 'Fumongus'.

It looks like the mushrooms have been genetically altered and have completely taken over the ecosystem that once existed here. Their unbridled and accelerated growth was such that they absorbed most of the water that was present here. They subsequently entered a sort of dried-up dormant state in which most of the fungus is still alive, with water spread out across the whole organism.
ancrel.13105.name: Overrun Bunker
ancrel.13105.desc:
Deep in the heart of the mycelial forests nestled in the canyons of [From.Planet.GetName] we discovered some sort of bunker, long overrun by mushrooms. The team believes that it was built by the same species that genetically altered the mushrooms here. 

Large sections of the bunker have collapsed and a lot of the equipment within it is likely broken beyond repair, but we have identified some sealed rooms that might hold exploitable material. Notably, no alien remains have been found here. Maybe they abandoned the place, or else didn't leave behind any body parts that weren't absorbed by the local wildlife.
ancrel.13110.name: Fungal Tamperers
ancrel.13110.desc:
The bunker on [From.Planet.GetName] was used to protect computing equipment, some of which appears to be directly connected to the mycelium. Thankfully, we managed to reactivate several terminals and databanks.

Breaking the encryption and deciphering the language used will take time, and the team has requested that several of our top [Root.Owner.GetLinguists] be sent here to help.
ancrel.13115.name: From Shroom to Code
ancrel.13115.desc:
We have recovered valuable information from the databanks found in the bunker on [From.Planet.GetName]. The databanks tell us that this was a sort of listening post. Apparently, the aliens found a way to interpret the signals coursing through the mycelium and convert them into actionable intel.

We do not understand how this might have been possible, but the team will now try to bring water from nearby ice asteroids to 'awaken' the Fumongus again and see what kind data it transmits, if any.
ancrel.13120.name: Dry No More
ancrel.13120.desc:
The mushrooms on [From.Planet.GetName] are starting to flourish again. With the help of several other ships, we had to tow several icy asteroids into orbit before bringing down chunks of them to various places on the planet to melt. It has been long process, but it is finally beginning to bear fruit.

With this, the computers began to spit out small bits of data that seemed pretty random until we recognized activity from our home. In cooperation with teams on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName], a series of experiments has been conducted and the only possible conclusion is that the mushroom has some limited awareness of what happens on other planets. While the data we have retrieved is not exploitable just yet, continued efforts to restore the mushrooms are expected to give us more results.
ancrel.13135.intro: The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.
ancrel.13135.mid:
The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret.
ancrel.13135.name: The Fumongus Listens Again
ancrel.13135.desc:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

Some mysteries remain, as we are still not sure how the mushroom manages to collect that much data from the rest of the galaxy. The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret.

With the network working again, the only decision left to make is whether to use it for surveillance, or not.
ancrel.13135.a.evopred: Monitor and report. Perhaps we can learn something similar.
ancrel.13130.name: Fear the Old Shroom
ancrel.13130.desc:
The Mycelium Listening Array is finally operational. A significant supply of water has been brought from orbit to sate the ever-thirsty mushroom, and major upgrades have been made to the computing resources.

And yet, there is still so much we don't know about the mycelial network.  The number of signals traversing the network proved surprisingly low, considering the quantity of information conveyed. The most prominent theory posits that the Fumongus exists across dimensions where distances are not what we are used to.
In any case, the Fumongus is in contact with its offspring across the galaxy, and these smaller colonies are able to relay data, which we can then interpret. But who else may have access to this network? There is a lot of data that we were not able to correlate to systems in this galaxy. Our more pessimistic [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] argue we might not be the only ones listening, and that by reactivating the network we just revealed ourselves to anyone using it.

Given all we still don't know about the Fumongus, or about the previous species that tapped into it, it might be best to just leave it alone..

tech_ring_world_desc: A Ringworld allows for multiple planet-like zones, cannibalizing all other planets in the system for materials.

The Relics screen allows us to view and activate our Relics, and also to enact decisions making use of Minor Artifacts.

Decisions marked with Planetary Decision are shown here only for reference and can instead be enacted from a Planet's Decision screen.
TUTORIAL_ARCHAEOLOGY_VIEW_DESC:
The Archaeology window shows details of the currently selected Archaeology site. After progress is made you can still go back and read previous stages by clicking the rune icons.

To unravel the secrets of a Site, a Scientist must make a Breakthrough to advance through each of the Site's stages. Scientists with relevant Traits and higher Skill speed the process of advancing to the next stage, while a higher Difficulty rating of a Site will slow it. Any Scientist who investigates a Site for long enough will amass Clues which will make a Breakthrough more likely.
bombardment_pox_desc:
Javorian Pox Bombardment showers the planet with a deadly pathogen.
- Moderate damage to Armies
- Light damage to Planet
- No damage to Mechanical Pops
- Catastrophic damage to Organic Pops
- Will bombard undefended planets
- Can reduce planets to lifeless Tomb Worlds
d_collapsed_spire_desc: An immense residential spire has collapsed under its own weight in this region, blocking access. While it was still standing, this towering structure must have been among the tallest on the planet.
add_zone_central_spire_tt: Urban District Specialization Added: £ Central Spire
d_massive_crevice_desc: This region is divided by a vast crevice that cuts through what was once a dense urban zone. The ground here is extremely unstable, with frequent earthquakes and landslides.
d_shattered_solar_array_desc: The shattered remnants of some kind of colossal solar array. When it was still functional, it must have provided power to a significant portion of this planet.
d_flooded_reactor_pits_desc: These deep pits appear to have once housed the planet's main energy production facilities. Over the eons, rain and flooding have filled the pits with murky water.
d_crumbling_mining_tunnels_desc: A network of deep tunnels beneath the planet's surface seem to have been its primary source of minerals. Millennia of cave-ins and rockfalls have left only a fraction of the tunnels traversable.
d_ancient_reactor_pits_desc: These deep pits near the planet's equator once housed its primary energy generators. Much of the surprisingly sturdy infrastructure has survived, and new reactors can be slotted into it.
d_immense_solar_array_desc: This solar array is nearly the size of a small continent. Most of it has been smashed beyond repair, but the underlying power infrastructure has survived, making it a good site for energy production.
d_abandoned_mining_tunnels_desc: Many of the ruins on the planet's surface were built by minerals extracted from these tunnels. Although most have been mined to depletion, there are still several with rich yields.
d_central_spire_desc: This towering structure appears to have served as the administrative center of the planet. Its central location and mostly intact interior provides an unmatched opportunity to research the ruins of this world.
zone_central_spire_desc: This towering structure appears to have served as the administrative center of the planet. Its central location and mostly intact interior provides an unmatched opportunity to research the ruins of this world.
d_industrial_sector_desc: This entire region once served as the industrial heartland of the planet. The factories and refineries that operated here have long since stopped working, but vast amounts of scattered resources can still be found in the area.
d_relic_dense_ruins_desc: The study of the dense ruins that cover this Relic World are a boon to science, but their presence also limits the amount of livable space.
d_relic_metal_boneyard_desc: The hollowed-out metal skeletons of fallen infrastructure seem almost to groan as the wind whistles through them.

- Turns the planet into an City-Covered Planet, increasing £ Housing, Resource Production and Pop Growth and unlocking special £ Arcology Districts.
- £ Generator, Mining and Agriculture Districts become inaccessible.
