They must have realized they were doomed after seeing the billowing mushroom clouds below, and communication logs shows that the astronauts made several futile and increasingly frantic attempts to contact the surface before they eventually ran out of supplies.

The station is in good condition, and it has afforded our engineers a rare glimpse of the early stages of a planetary space program. They have gained several ideas from the primitive yet ingenious solutions used in the station's design.
colony.162.b.evopred: Fortunate that these remains weren't irradiated.
colony.163.name: Wasteland Radiation
colony.163.desc: The radiation levels in some wasteland regions of [Root.GetName] appear to be greater than our previous scans had indicated. Colonists in several local settlements have complained of poor health, and birth rates are down. We are taking steps to evacuate the affected regions, but these measures will take time.
colony.164.name: Pacifist Movement
colony.164.desc:
The decrepit ruins and desolate wastelands found on [Root.GetName] seem to have prompted many of the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s colonists to adopt some kind of pacifistic philosophy.

Members of this new movement claim that the environment they live in serve as a daily reminder of the senseless horrors of war. They see it as their civic duty to prevent the terrible destruction visited upon [Root.GetName] from occurring on other worlds.
colony.164.b: These wretched cowards shame our nation!
colony.164.c: Excellent. Everyone should give peace a chance.
colony.164.a.tooltip: Up to 400 £ Pops on [Root.GetName] lose any Militaristic ethics and gain the Pacifist ethic
colony.170.name: Orbital Debris
colony.170.desc:
The orbital space around [Root.GetName] is cluttered with debris left behind by the alien civilization that once inhabited the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]. Before they wiped themselves out, their early space programs saw the launch of thousands of primitive satellites and missile launch platforms. Many of these were destroyed by anti-satellite weapons during the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s destructive nuclear war, adding even more space junk to the mix.

Our colony on the surface has developed to a point where this dense field of debris is interfering with its infrastructure. We cannot use satellites and civilian orbital flights are limited to narrow launch windows.
colony.171.name: Freighter Crash
colony.171.desc: A civilian freighter coming in to land on [Root.GetName] was perforated by a dense cloud of fast-moving orbital debris! The flight crew was killed immediately, and the stricken craft tumbled through the atmosphere only to crash-land near one of the colony's main power relays. The resulting explosion resulted in several deaths on the ground, and local infrastructure suffered considerable damage.
colony.171.desc.mach: A worker unit freighter coming in to land on [Root.GetName] was perforated by a dense cloud of fast-moving orbital debris! The flight crew units were destroyed instantly, and the stricken craft tumbled through the atmosphere only to crash-land near one of the colony's main power relays. The resulting explosion resulted in several operation terminations on the ground, and local infrastructure suffered considerable damage.
colony.172.name: Debris Impact
colony.172.desc: A cascade of collisions in the dense layer of debris surrounding [Root.GetName] recently shifted the orbit of a large piece of space junk. The object - which we believe was one of the many orbital missile platforms used in the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s nuclear war - was pulled into the atmosphere, and unfortunately proceeded to impact directly on top of a major settlement. Initial reports indicate heavy casualties.
colony.172.a: We really need to do something about that debris.
colony.173.desc: With the assistance of our Science Ship, colonial authorities on [From.From.GetName] have finished cleaning up the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s orbital space. It has now been made safe for satellites and civilian travel.
colony.174.desc:
With the assistance of our Science Ship, colonial authorities on [From.From.GetName] have finished cleaning up the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s orbital space. It has now been made safe for satellites and civilian travel.

As it turns out, a lot of the debris consisted of valuable minerals from the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface that had been used in satellite construction. We were able to salvage a significant amount, netting a tidy profit in the process.
colony.180.name: Asteroid Sighted
colony.180.desc:
Our deep space tracking arrays on [Root.GetName] have made an alarming discovery - a large asteroid is heading towards the [Root.GetPlanetMoon] on a direct collision course! Should it impact the surface, the consequences would be disastrous.

The asteroid must be destroyed before it is too late!
colony.182.name: Asteroid Destroyed
colony.182.desc:
The asteroid that was approaching [Root.GetName] on a collision course has been destroyed! With their doom averted, our jubilant citizens on the [Root.GetPlanetMoon] have taken to the streets in celebration.

A scan of the remaining fragments has also revealed that the asteroid consisted largely of valuable minerals. We have collected what we could.
colony.182.desc.mach:
The asteroid that was approaching [Root.GetName] on a collision course has been destroyed! No planetside units or structures have been affected by the event, as any inbound debris was small enough to disintegrate on atmospheric entry.

A scan of the remaining fragments has also revealed that the asteroid consisted largely of valuable minerals. We have collected what we could.
colony.183.name: Asteroid Impacts [Root.GetName]
colony.183.desc: We failed to stop the asteroid that was heading for [Root.GetName] in time. It has collided with the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface, causing widespread devastation and untold suffering. Millions are dead.
colony.183.desc.mach: We failed to stop the asteroid that was heading for [Root.GetName] in time. It has collided with the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface, causing widespread devastation and destruction. Millions of machine units have been rendered terminally inoperable.
colony.185.name: World Consumed
colony.185.desc:
We have consumed enough of [Target.GetName] that a chain reaction has begun and destabilized its core.

All drones have been evacuated to [Owner.Capital.GetName].
vultaum_artifact: We have acquired a Vultaum artifact.
precursor.completed.name: Archaeological Project Completed
precursor.1.name: The Vultaum Star Assembly
precursor.1.desc:
We have recovered artifacts from an ancient alien civilization on [From.GetName]! They must have been active in this region of space approximately 12 million years ago, judging by the age of the artifacts.

From what they have been able to piece together, our scientists theorize that these aliens, who called themselves the "Vultaum Star Assembly," were worm-like annelids, roughly 3 to 4 meters in length, that communicated with each other primarily through vibrations carried along their segmented bodies.
precursor.5.name: Vultaum Mining Base
precursor.5.desc: Remnants of a small Vultaum helium-3 mining base have been found at the bottom of a large crater on [From.GetName]. The blast that created the crater seems to have originated from inside the facility itself. Unless Vultaum mining techniques were radically different from our own, an equipment failure or accident cannot account for such a massive explosion.
precursor.6.desc: Miraculously, we managed to salvage parts of a Vultaum data core that had been blown clear of the crater on [From.From.GetName]. Most of the data was corrupt, but our scientists did manage to properly translate the "korga" - the basic Vultaum time unit.
precursor.10.name: Vultaum Observatory
precursor.10.desc:
An ancient Vultaum observatory has been found on the surface of [From.GetName]. The [From.GetStarName] system is fairly distant from the region of space where the Vultaum originated, and this facility appears to have been primarily used for the observation of their own stars.

We have gone over the observatory's surviving data, but there are no clues as to exactly what the Vultaum were searching for in their observations.
precursor.11.desc: The archaeological dig on [From.From.GetName] has uncovered a small mural in one of the observatory's dust-covered smaller chambers. It seems to depict several different constellations, possibly as they would appear if viewed from the Vultaum homeworld. Our astronomers have not been able to identify the individual stars.
precursor.15.name: Vultaum Colony
precursor.15.desc: The partial remains of a collapsed Vultaum space elevator have been discovered by the [Root.GetName] in one of the equatorial regions on [From.GetName]. It seems the elevator was intentionally severed at its counterweight beyond geostationary orbit, collapsing the massive cable on top of several major urban centers along the equator. Judging by the ruins, the resulting death toll must have been in the millions.
precursor.16.desc: Our archaeologists on [From.From.GetName] have managed to recover the partial remains of a star chart next to a broken segment of elevator cable. It was apparently used by captains in the Vultaum merchant marine, and it shows several of their most lucrative interstellar trade routes.
precursor.20.desc:
Several large, perfectly circular lakes on the surface of [From.GetName] were caused by a series of massive antimatter explosions several million years ago. This [From.GetPlanetMoon] was inhabited by the Vultaum at that point, and the craters are all clustered in the region that housed their largest planetary settlements.

Orbital bombardment has been ruled out by the science staff on the [Root.GetName], leading us to believe that these explosions were triggered by someone or something on the ground.
precursor.21.desc: The archaeologists on [From.From.GetName] have managed to recover an intact memory core from a terminal inside a crumbling medical facility. It contained some interesting statistics, such as the average natural Vultaum lifespan (roughly 270 years) and a list of their most common diseases.
precursor.25.desc:
A thorough scan of [From.GetName] has revealed a vast, artificially-constructed network of tunnels beneath the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface. Most of the tunnels have collapsed, and the crew of the [Root.GetName] believe they represent only a small portion of what was once a much larger subterranean Vultaum colony.

The main underground caverns were intentionally collapsed, crushing the Vultaum cities and their inhabitants under several million tons of rock.
precursor.26.desc: The archaeological dig on [From.From.GetName] has unearthed some remarkable fossilized Vultaum remains from one of the collapsed chambers closest to the surface. This has given our scientists a much clearer picture of what the Vultaum actually looked like.
precursor.30.name: Vultaum Gas Giant Facility
precursor.30.desc: We have detected the partial remains of a gas mining station in orbit around [From.GetName] which appears Vultaum in origin. Its station-keeping thrusters were deliberately fired millions of years ago in an attempt to push the station directly into the gas giant, but a collision with an unknown object prevented this from happening.
precursor.31.desc: A mostly intact Vultaum space suit that previous looters had somehow overlooked has been recovered by our archaeologists. This four meter long, tube-like construct has given our scientists new insights into what kind of environments the Vultaum preferred.
precursor.35.name: Vultaum Trade Post
precursor.35.desc: [From.GetName] was home to a small Vultaum outpost where they traded with several neighboring civilizations. At some point the trade post appears to have been converted into a religious mission, where the Vultaum attempted to convert visiting alien merchants to their philosophy. Trade ceased shortly afterward, and the [From.GetPlanetMoon] was eventually abandoned.
precursor.36.desc: Archaeologists on [From.From.GetName] have salvaged a small Vultaum digital pamphlet. It seems the missionaries at this outpost passed pamphlets like this on to visiting merchants. Most of the data is corrupt, but there are several references to "the great lie" and "the shackles of virtual reality."
precursor.40.name: Vultaum Satellite
precursor.40.desc:
A small Vultaum satellite was found in orbit of [From.GetName]. It had been set up to continuously repeat a message until its power source drained millions of years ago. We salvaged its transmitter array but could only recover a small portion of the transmission.

The main purpose of this satellite was apparently to preach the dominant Vultaum philosophy to neighboring civilizations. Its message speaks of the need to "disconnect" and to "embrace true existence," whatever that means.
precursor.41.desc: After careful analysis of the Vultaum transmitter array, our archaeologists and data engineers have concluded that the machinery does not contain any technologies of value to us. The project has greatly improved our understanding of the primary Vultaum programming language, however. This will hopefully make it easier to decipher their data in the future.
precursor.45.name: Vultaum Splinter Colony
precursor.45.desc: [From.GetName] was the site of a small Vultaum colony that is unique for two reasons - the [From.GetStarName] system is not within what used to be Vultaum space, and the ruins are several centuries younger than anything else left by their civilization. The colony seems to have been settled by some kind of splinter group that rejected their society's dominant philosophy.
precursor.46.desc: Several artifacts excavated at the archaeological dig site on [From.From.GetName] are covered in writing that firmly rejects the Vultaum philosophical idea that "life itself is a lie." One of them appears to be a memorial of sorts to the Vultaum race as a whole. This would confirm our theory that this splinter colony existed for some time after the collapse of the rest of the Star Assembly.
precursor.50.name: Vultaum Virtual Reality Center
precursor.50.desc: Vultaum engineers at some point built a massive orbital complex near [From.GetName] dedicated to computer research. Strangely, they seem to have ignored the normally popular field of artificial intelligence to focus exclusively on virtual realities and massive computer simulations. Most of the complex has been ruined by weapons fire and micrometeoroids, but what remains is in remarkable condition given the station's age.
precursor.51.desc:
The archaeologists investigating the Vultaum orbital complex above [From.From.GetName] have stumbled upon an interesting find. They managed to recover a partial copy of what was apparently a fairly popular multi-user virtual reality game enjoyed by billions of Vultaum across their empire.

Although the game takes place in a fictional and highly satirized version of their contemporary society, it has proved an invaluable source of information on both their language and customs.
precursor.55.name: Vultaum Asteroid Mining Base
precursor.55.desc: [From.GetName] is covered in impact craters from asteroid collisions, but one stands out - it appears to have been created through the detonation of some kind of antimatter device. There is evidence elsewhere on the asteroid's surface indicating that it was heavily mined by the Vultaum at some point roughly 12 million years ago. The large crater we found was presumably the location of their mining outpost.
precursor.56.desc: A closer examination of the destroyed Vultaum mining base on [From.From.GetName] has uncovered some of their abandoned mining equipment in a surviving tunnel. It was uniquely designed for use with their worm-like anatomy, and appears to have been operated primarily through the body vibrations they used to communicate.
precursor.100.name: Vultaum Home System Located
precursor.100.desc: After intense study of our recovered Vultaum artifacts, scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName] have managed to deduce the exact galactic coordinates of Vultaumar - the home system of the ancient Vultaum civilization! We should launch an expedition to this system before someone else beats us to it.
precursor.101.name: The Vultaum Homeworld
precursor.101.desc:
The shattered remnants of the Vultaum homeworld reveal that it underwent a massive extinction event 12 million years ago, caused by the detonation of some kind of antimatter device. From the ruins that remain on the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface, we have learned that Vultaum society experienced a radical ideological shift a century before their extinction.

Their new philosophy posited that the entire universe was an artificial reality which all sapient beings had been unwittingly plugged into for the amusement of some higher power. The Vultaum undertook increasingly radical attempts to forcefully "disconnect" themselves from this simulation, most of which involved mass suicide.

They finally concluded that only the simultaneous disconnection of billions of individuals would destabilize the system enough to grant them freedom. At an agreed upon hour, Vultaum everywhere killed themselves by any means available. Those who refused to take part in this mass suicide were too few to repopulate the species, and so the Vultaum faded into obscurity and eventual extinction.
precursor.102.name: Vultaum Homeworld Discovered
precursor.102.desc.a: The shattered homeworld of the ancient Vultaum has been found, but it has clearly been visited by someone else recently. Nothing of value remains to be found on the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon].
precursor.102.desc.b: According to our survey data, this broken world once served as the homeworld of an ancient civilization known as the "Vultaum." There are signs that other spacefarers visited here recently... nothing of value remains to be found on the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon].
precursor.500.name: The Yuht Empire
precursor.500.desc:
We have recovered artifacts from an ancient alien civilization on [From.GetName]! Our scientists think they inhabited this region of stars roughly six million years ago, based on the age of the artifacts. The aliens called themselves the "Yuht" and appear to have been very large and flat arthropod analogues.

It seems a single individual could reach a length of nearly a hundred meters as an adult, and it was apparently exceedingly rare for more than two or three Yuht to travel aboard the same starship.
precursor.505.name: Yuht Hatchery World
precursor.505.desc: [From.GetName] was subjected to extensive orbital bombardment at some point in the distant past, during which the biosphere suffered catastrophic damage. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] appears to have been home to a small outpost built by the ancient Yuht, but why that would warrant the devastation of an entire world is a mystery.
precursor.506.desc:
After extensive studies of [From.From.GetName], we now know that the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] served as one of several "hatchery worlds" in the Yuht Empire. Their Ministry of Breeding prepared worlds by sterilizing them of predators and other potentially harmful elements before planting eggs on the surface.

The Yuht hatchlings were then left on their own in this relatively safe environment for several centuries until they developed a level of near-sapience. Only then were they collected and carefully introduced into society.
precursor.510.name: Yuht Listening Post
precursor.510.desc: We have discovered several massive listening arrays on [From.GetName]. These arrays are millions of years old and we believe they were originally built by the Yuht, though it appears at least one other alien civilization repurposed them at some point in the last 500,000 years for their own needs. The colossal receiving dishes are beyond repair, but some terminals are still intact.
precursor.511.desc:
Our archaeologists on [From.From.GetName] have learned that the listening arrays built there were used to scan space for any signs of intelligent alien life - something the Yuht had never once encountered.

After managing to partially restore power to a computer terminal, the archaeologists acquired a data disc with log files from the sensor array stretching over centuries. These logs suggest that this section of the galaxy was indeed devoid of sapient life at the time of the Yuht Empire.
precursor.515.name: Yuht Colony
precursor.515.desc:
The ruins of several dozen massive Yuht arcologies can be found in the southern hemisphere of [From.GetName], indicating that this [From.GetPlanetMoon] was one of their major colonies.

Inside one of the crumbling buildings our ground team discovered the remains of what appears to be a museum exhibiting "famous alien frauds." These are various artifacts collected by Yuht from throughout their empire, claimed to prove the existence of sapient alien life. In each case, the museum has debunked the artifacts as frauds.
precursor.516.desc: Most of the artifacts exhibited by the Yuht museums on [From.From.GetName] are missing, but our archaeologists managed to recover one of these supposed frauds. It seems to be an instrument used for measuring cosmic radiation, but the archaeologists have confirmed that it predates the Yuht by several million years. Contrary to the opinion of the Yuht museum, this would indeed seem to be an authentic alien artifact.
precursor.520.desc:
Signs of Yuht development can be found all across [From.GetName], and the [From.GetPlanetMoon] must have experienced limited terraforming at some point. One region in the northern hemisphere is some kind of massive graveyard. No Yuht settlements can be found nearby, but there are many monuments marking burial sites.

With a low birthrate and an average lifespan close to a thousand years, each Yuht death was treated as a significant event and much emphasis was placed on burial ceremonies.
precursor.521.desc: The archaeological digs on [From.From.GetName] have revealed that most of the graves were looted in the millions of years since they were first dug, likely as a result of the Yuht custom of burying their dead with jewelry and other extravagant gifts. In a pile of things discarded by the looters, the archaeologists found a large doll resembling an adult Yuht. They speculate that it may have served as a good luck charm or memento of some kind.
precursor.525.desc:
A massive ground war was fought on [From.GetName] between the Yuht and a second species that we know little of. This campaign took place in the final years of the Yuht Empire, and though it occurred millions of years ago, wreckage of ruined war machines can still be found.

Although the [From.GetPlanetMoon] was an important Yuht colony, their cities and outlying settlements were never rebuilt after the fighting ceased, which would seem to indicate that they ultimately lost the campaign.
precursor.526.desc: After combing through several of the ancient battlefields on [From.From.GetName], our archaeologists recovered what appears to be a Yuht battle harness. Several large-caliber cannons were still attached to it, and the archaeologists theorize that Yuht soldiers, given the massive size of their bodies, fought as what can essentially be described as large mobile fortresses.
precursor.530.name: Yuht Satellite
precursor.530.desc:
A Yuht satellite was placed in orbit around [From.GetName] to commemorate the moment of first contact between their empire and the Jabbardeeni, a contemporary civilization. This event occurred right here in the [From.GetStarName] system, and had a profound impact on all levels of Yuht society.

For over a million years they had thought themselves alone in the galaxy, and the Yuht reacted with both awe and horror upon the discovery of sapient alien life. The [Root.GetName] has recovered the satellite, which now awaits a full analysis.
precursor.531.desc: After analyzing the satellite we recovered above [From.From.GetName], our archaeologists found an ingrained, highly stylized picture of what appears to be a Yuht cruiser and a much smaller Jabbardeeni scout in close formation during the first contact event. This has given us some notion of what their starships looked like.
precursor.535.name: Yuht Cruiser
precursor.535.desc: The remains of a Yuht cruiser have been found in orbit around [From.GetName]. It seems to have fallen victim to weapons fire, but given the extreme age of the hulk it is difficult to be certain. There is no indication that the ship was ever equipped with an FTL drive - it must have traveled between stars at sublight speeds.
precursor.536.desc:
The archaeologists investigating the derelict Yuht cruiser above [From.From.GetName] have transmitted their report. There are two large cryo chambers in the cruiser's mid-section, designed to house one Yuht each in suspended animation. Given the massive size of Yuht individuals, this was apparently their standard crew complement on vessels of this size.

No Yuht remains were found anywhere on the ship, but the archaeologists managed to recover logs from a computer that monitored the life signs and medical condition of the crew. It has provided valuable data on Yuht physiology.
precursor.540.name: Yuht Colony Ship
precursor.540.desc:
The partial remains of an ancient Yuht starship have been found in high orbit over [From.GetName]. An initial analysis conducted by the [Root.GetName] indicate that the vessel may have served as a colony ship.

Even cruiser-sized Yuht ships were typically crewed by only one or two individuals given the immense size of their bodies, but this hulk has more than a dozen cryo-pods attached, each containing withered exoskeletons from what must have been Yuht colonists.
precursor.541.desc: Most of the remains of the derelict Yuht colony ship that orbits [From.From.GetName] are in poor condition, but our archaeologists managed to recover the vessel's sublight engines. The Yuht never breached the light barrier, depending instead on cryo technology and thousand year long natural life-spans to spread their empire across the stars.
precursor.545.name: Yuht Asteroid Dwelling
precursor.545.desc: This asteroid appears to have served as the home of a single Yuht individual. Deep scans show a series of connected caves in the asteroid's interior that follow a pattern similar to the rooms seen in ancient Yuht dwellings that have been discovered elsewhere. To learn more we will have to dispatch an away team to investigate the cave system.
precursor.546.desc: After investigating the Yuht dwelling on asteroid [From.From.GetName], we have learned that it was the home of the famous philosopher-hermit "Yakliir." She was evidently a figure of some renown in their culture, and references to her have been found in several different Yuht sources. Yakliir's remains were found by the dwelling's main airlock, where she perished waiting for a scheduled supply shuttle that never arrived.
precursor.600.name: Yuht Home System Located
precursor.600.desc: After intense study of our recovered Yuht artifacts, scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName] have managed to deduce the exact galactic coordinates of Yuhtaan - the home system of the ancient Yuht civilization! We should launch an expedition to this system before someone else beats us to it.
precursor.601.name: The Yuht Homeworld
precursor.601.desc:
We have confirmed that [FromFrom.GetName] was the original homeworld of the Yuht. The [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] suffered extensive orbital bombardment roughly four million years ago. Twisted metal skeletons are all that remain of the massive arcologies that once covered the surface.

From what we can piece together, it seems the Yuht spent the better part of a million years searching local space in vain for signs of intelligent alien life. When they finally encountered the Jabbardeeni, a young race that had only recently achieved interstellar travel, their alien psychology was a tremendous shock.

The Yuht leadership reached a consensus: the Jabbardeeni had to be eradicated before they grew too powerful. A massive surprise attack was launched, which was beaten back at great cost for both sides. Despite their young age, the Jabbardeeni were already experimenting with technologies the Yuht had never considered, and eventually they gained the upper hand. After less than a decade of warfare, the two million year old Yuht Empire was utterly destroyed.
precursor.602.name: Yuht Homeworld Discovered
precursor.602.desc.a: We have discovered the ancient homeworld of the Yuht, but alas, someone else must have recently paid a visit to this world. The [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] has been stripped clean of anything of value.
precursor.602.desc.b: Our survey of [FromFrom.GetName] has revealed that the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] was once the homeworld of an ancient species known as the "Yuht." This system was recently visited by other interstellar travelers, however, and they appear to have picked the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] clean of anything of value.
precursor.1000.name: The First League
precursor.1000.desc:
We have recovered artifacts from an ancient alien civilization on [From.GetName]! If what we have learned from these artifacts is correct, this civilization was some sort of confederation that consisted of many different alien races. They called themselves the "First League" and appear to have co-existed in relative peace some two million years ago.

Though the [From.GetStarName] system lies in the region of space that seems to have made up the core of their territory, a partial map found among the artifacts indicates that this First League may have covered a significant portion of our galaxy before its eventual collapse.
precursor.1005.name: League Naval Base
precursor.1005.desc: The wreckage of what must have been a major First League naval base has been detected in orbit around [From.GetName]. We know the League maintained a massive fleet called the "Grand Navy" to combat piracy and safeguard member nations from external aggressors - this particular outpost appears to have provided berthing for one of their rimward patrol fleets.
precursor.1006.desc: Our archaeological mission to the First League naval base has concluded. We recovered the emblem of the 28th Outer Rim Patrol Fleet, a mid-sized task force charged with the defense of trade routes leading to League associate nations along the galactic rim. The base orbiting [From.From.GetName] was apparently their home port.
precursor.1010.name: League Cruiser
precursor.1010.desc: The bow section of an ancient First League cruiser has been discovered orbiting [From.GetName]. There is insufficient debris nearby to account for the rest of the ship, but what little remains is in very poor condition. The hull has been riddled with holes from what appears to be large mass driver projectiles.
precursor.1011.desc: The archaeological expedition to the First League cruiser orbiting [From.From.GetName] has returned. Little of use could be found on the ruined vessel, but the archaeologists did manage to recover its crew manifest. The First League called upon all of its member worlds to staff the Grand Navy, their joint starfleet, and through the manifest we have learned that the crew of this particular cruiser was made up of individuals from twelve different species.
precursor.1015.name: The Khamdai Homeworld
precursor.1015.desc: The survey of [From.GetName] has revealed that the [From.GetPlanetMoon] was the homeworld of the insectoid Khamdai, one of the founding members of the ancient First League. Massive hive-like cities once covered most of the surface, but we have learned that the Khamdai banned all construction in a large circular region extending across more than a third of the southern hemisphere. This area served as both a mating ground and nature reserve.
precursor.1016.desc:
Our archaeological expedition to [From.From.GetName] has learned much about the now-extinct Khamdai. They were a warrior culture that fought several wars against many of the other First League founders soon after their first starships breached the light barrier.

After meeting with defeat, the Khamdai became an enthusiastic supporter of the First League's founding and many of their finest warriors would go on to serve as shock troops against the League's enemies. We have recovered a perfectly preserved "magil-sha," a ceremonial sickle used by Khamdai members of the First League Honor Guard.
precursor.1020.name: The Chassago Homeworld
precursor.1020.desc: This world is the ancient homeworld of the serpentine Chassago, one of the founding members of the First League. The vast majority of their cities were located underground and [From.GetName] is riddled with tunnel networks, of which most have collapsed in the two million years since the Chassago went extinct. Probes from the [Root.GetName] have identified the probable locations of several subterranean cities.
precursor.1021.desc:
The excavation of the subterranean Chassago cities on [From.From.GetName] is well underway, and we have already learned much about this ancient species. They were reptilian, with elongated and legless bodies that could be twenty meters or longer in adult individuals.

All surviving accounts indicate that the Chassago were expert traders, and their trade barges were often the first point of contact between non-affiliated races and the First League. It is doubtful whether it could have expanded as rapidly as it did without the benefit of the extensive Chassago trade network that already existed before its foundation.
precursor.1025.name: The Migir-Yan Homeworld
precursor.1025.desc:
The diminutive but fast-breeding Migir-Yan were one of the founding members of the ancient First League, and [From.GetName] was their homeworld. The population was clustered into hundreds of massive arcologies spread out across the surface, each capable of supporting several hundred million individuals.

These arcologies were connected by a network of skyways, and the Migir-Yan were evidently content to leave the rest of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s wilderness untouched.
precursor.1026.desc:
Fossilized remains of the extinct Migir-Yan have been recovered by our archaeologists on [From.From.GetName], allowing us to paint a clearer picture of what this species looked like. Unusually small, with most individuals being no taller than 0.6 meters, these mammalian rodent analogues were herbivores.

Migir-Yan family units often consisted of close to a thousand individuals, and an individual's station in society depended almost exclusively on their social skills. The Migir-Yan diplomatic corps is believed to have been the driving force behind the creation of the First League.
precursor.1030.name: The V'ropak Homeworld
precursor.1030.desc:
[From.GetName] was the homeworld of the avian V'ropak, a species that was among the founding members of the ancient First League. These flightless bird analogues walked on long, spindly legs and fossilized remains suggest that their females could reach heights of up to four meters, while males were slightly smaller.

All of their cities were built inside hollowed out mesas. Scans indicate that some of these mesas were artificially constructed, presumably by the V'ropak themselves after they ran out of natural candidates to build new cities within.
precursor.1031.desc: When the First League was at the zenith of its power, the V'ropak were renowned as the best scientists in the galaxy. Their research innovations drove the League's initial expansion phase, and more than one species was brought into the fold by promises of access to V'ropak technology. Unfortunately, none of this technology remains to be found among the ruins of [From.From.GetName] today.
precursor.1035.name: League Science Base
precursor.1035.desc: A surface scan of [From.GetName] has identified the remnants of an ancient installation on the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface. Most of the facility was wiped out in a massive explosion some two million years ago, but a few outlying buildings more or less survived the blast. All evidence recovered so far points towards this having been some sort of research base built by the First League.
precursor.1036.desc:
The archaeological expedition we sent to [From.From.GetName] has returned. Very little remained of the First League research base they were sent to investigate, but judging by its isolated location, we suspect that the research conducted there was of a dangerous nature - possibly involving dimensional travel or advanced bio-weapons.

A recovered data disc from the "Academy of Sciences" has offered some insights into how the scientific community of the First League was organized.
precursor.1040.name: Joint League Colony
precursor.1040.desc: Ruins of a First League colony have been unearthed on [From.GetName]. The colony appears to have been a social experiment conducted in the League's waning years - the initial population consisted of an equal number of colonists from all of the League's member species. It was abandoned less than fifty years after its founding.
precursor.1041.desc:
Our archaeologists have learned more about the lost colony on [From.From.GetName]. At its founding, the First League was already on the verge of collapse and the colony was meant to serve as a propaganda tool - a model world where all League members were represented and worked together in harmony.

This effort appears to have backfired, as there is evidence of significant infighting between the colonists, including a large massacre that occurred just before the colony was abandoned.
precursor.1045.name: League Trade Center
precursor.1045.desc: Two million years ago, [From.GetName] served as a major trading hub for the member nations of the First League. Large portions of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface was covered in towering cities, and we have identified the ruins of at least twelve major spaceports in the northern hemisphere alone. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] was gradually abandoned over a period of several centuries, presumably as a result of shifting trade routes and the collapse of the First League.
precursor.1046.desc: It is unclear which species first settled this world - bones and fossilized remains from all known First League member species have been found on the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] in nearly equal amounts. Our archaeologists have also secured remains from half a dozen races that weren't official members, but who seem to have enjoyed special trading privileges in First League space.
precursor.1050.name: Battle Wreckage
precursor.1050.desc: A great battle between the Grand Navy of the First League and another fleet took place not far from here some two million years ago. The gravity well of [From.GetName] has since captured much of the debris left by this engagement, and the wreckage of several massive hulks can be found on the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface.
precursor.1051.desc:
Our archaeologists have successfully excavated several starship hulls on the surface of [From.From.GetName], relics from the massive space battle that took place in this system two million years ago. The forces involved were the 2nd and 3rd Fleets of the First League Grand Navy, fighting to contain an incursion by the combined fleets of the Rikim, a nomadic warrior species from the galactic rim.

What began as a minor skirmish quickly escalated into a running fleet battle involving hundreds of ships on both sides. It is impossible to tell which side won.
precursor.1055.name: League Prison Complex
precursor.1055.desc:
The ruins of a large prison complex have been discovered on [From.GetName]. This hostile world seems to have served as some kind of maximum-security penal colony in the First League. As a federal facility, the prison housed convicted felons from across all of League space.

Surviving records indicate most of the prisoners were guilty of piracy, terrorism and other crimes of "extraordinary nature." Fossilized remains from some prisoners can still be found where the cells used to be.
precursor.1056.desc:
The archaeological mission to [From.From.GetName] has uncovered evidence of what appears to be a failed escape attempt some distance south of the prison complex. A toppled utility vehicle from the prison was found behind a small cliff, and several kilometers beyond that the remains of several prisoners in stolen pressure suits were huddled together.

They seem to have died of asphyxiation when the oxygen supply in their suits ran out. For whatever reason, the prison authorities evidently saw no reason to collect the bodies.
precursor.1060.name: Protected [Owner.GetPreFTLUpper] World
precursor.1060.desc:
[From.GetName] was inhabited by an early Bronze Age civilization some two million years ago. Interestingly, the [Root.GetName] has also found evidence of hidden observation posts on the [From.GetPlanetMoon] that were built by the First League. It would appear that they studied the [Owner.GetPreFTLLower] aliens while making an effort to avoid cultural contamination.

Most of the observation posts were destroyed by advanced energy weapons, and we have found nothing yet to explain why the [Owner.GetPreFTLLower] civilization never advanced beyond the Bronze Age.
precursor.1061.desc:
From our archaeological findings on [From.From.GetName], we have learned that the First League maintained a clear policy not to interfere in the development of pre-space civilizations. Hidden observation posts like the ones we found on this [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] were maintained on at least seven worlds throughout League space.

This particular civilization appears to have met its end when a band of slavers invaded during the power vacuum that resulted from the First League's collapse.
precursor.1065.name: Orbital Blockade
precursor.1065.desc:
[From.GetName] lies deep inside what was considered First League space two million years ago, and it appears to have been either a major colony or the homeworld of a species described as "non-compliant" in surviving League records.

The two parties appear to have been engaged in some kind of trade war, and the League's Grand Navy maintained extensive blockades of the [From.GetPlanetMoon] on at least two separate occasions. Orbital debris indicate that the blockades were violently challenged several times.
precursor.1066.desc: A team of archaeologists found the wreckage of a First League destroyer on the surface of [From.From.GetName]. It must have been part of the orbital blockade, and seems to have gone down when the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s native aliens detonated a hidden antimatter device on a captured blockade runner. The archaeologists managed to retrieve a partial copy of the destroyer's databanks, providing us with a list of all First League vessels that took part in the blockade.
precursor.1070.name: Smuggler Asteroid
precursor.1070.desc: This asteroid appears to have served as a lawless port for the various criminal organizations that were active in the territory of the First League. Smugglers, pirates, mercenaries and other lowlifes from every League member species gathered here to offload illicit cargo, broker new deals or just relax in one of the asteroid's many cantinas.
precursor.1071.desc: The archaeological mission to asteroid [From.From.GetName] has revealed much about the criminal underworld active throughout the First League two million years ago. As member nations opened borders to one another, crime flourished alongside trade. Smuggling and piracy appears to have been serious problems that occupied a large portion of the sizable League fleet.
precursor.1100.name: First League Home System Located
precursor.1100.desc: After intense study of our recovered First League artifacts, scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName] have managed to deduce the exact galactic coordinates of Fen Habbanis - the home system of the great First League! We should launch an expedition to this system before someone else beats us to it.
precursor.1101.name: The First League Headquarters
precursor.1101.desc:
[FromFrom.GetName] was the administrative center of the First League throughout most of its existence, and served as the seat of their Great Senate. The [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] was densely populated, with a planet-wide city covering most of the surface. Food had to be imported from other member worlds to support the untold billions living in this enormous metropolis.

When the League collapsed, these food shipments ceased virtually overnight. Those with the means departed for other worlds, but most of the population remained behind. Mass starvation and anarchy followed as the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] was carved up between warlords and criminal organizations.

The population continued to dwindle for a few centuries until the planet had been reduced to little more than a lifeless ghost world - a final epitaph of the First League.
precursor.1102.name: First League Capital Found
precursor.1102.desc.a: We have finally discovered the capital of the ancient First League. Unfortunately, we are too late. Someone else has been here recently, and anything of value is long gone.
precursor.1102.desc.b: Our recent survey of [FromFrom.GetName] has revealed that this world served as the administrative capital of some kind of ancient interstellar alliance known as the "First League." Other explorers have visited here recently, and unfortunately they picked the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] clean of any valuable artifacts before they left.
precursor.1500.name: The Irassian Concordat
precursor.1500.desc:
We have recovered artifacts from an ancient alien civilization on [From.GetName]! From what we have translated so far of their language, we have learned that these aliens called themselves the "Irassian Concordat." They were an interstellar power that held sway over this region of the galaxy a little over a million years ago.

They appear to have been six-limbed mammalians, and there are several references to some sort of plague called the "Javorian Pox" which swept across their empire with devastating results, possibly leading to their extinction.
precursor.1505.name: Quarantined World
precursor.1505.desc: [From.GetName] was once a large Irassian colony, showing signs of both industrial development and terraforming. As on other Irassian worlds, the fossilized remains tell a harrowing tale - the population rapidly succumbed to the Javorian Pox, and there appears to have been widespread panic in all of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s major settlements. There is also an unusually large amount of debris in orbit, possibly the remnants of a battle.
precursor.1506.desc: We have analyzed the orbital debris, and our archaeologists conclude that [From.From.GetName] was subjected to a military blockade before and during the Irassian colony's demise. The Irassian fleet had strict orders to quarantine the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] in a vain attempt to contain the Javorian Pox. At least a dozen civilian ships made an attempt to break the blockade, and despite the heavy fighting it appears some were successful.
precursor.1510.name: Purified World
precursor.1510.desc:
It is immediately apparent that [From.GetName], an ancient Irassian colony, has been the victim of extensive orbital bombardment. Large craters are still visible from space where the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s major population centers used to be roughly 1.2 million years ago.

The handful of survivors from the initial bombardment appear to have succumbed shortly afterwards to the Javorian Pox that was then ravaging most Irassian worlds.
precursor.1511.desc: Our archaeological expedition has recovered a communications log from the ruins of a listening post on [From.From.GetName]. It shows the contents of a transmission between the commander of an Irassian fleet in orbit, and their naval headquarters on Irassia. The commander questions orders to "purge" the colony of all life to prevent the spreading of the pox. Although the log ends before the issue is resolved, the orders were evidently carried out.
precursor.1515.name: The Joggra Homeworld
precursor.1515.desc:
This [From.GetPlanetMoon] was the homeworld of the Joggra, a subjugated client species of the Irassian Concordat. A molluscoid species that was on the verge of achieving space flight when the Irassians discovered them, the Joggra were conquered after a lengthy military campaign that devastated many of their cities.

There is evidence on the surface that a sizeable Irassian military garrison was stationed there for decades afterwards, suggesting that the Joggra were not content to remain under the Irassian yoke.
precursor.1516.desc:
Remnants of a Joggran subspace message have been found on [From.From.GetName], which appears to have been transmitted to the homeworlds of the Irassian Concordat's other client species:

"The time to strike at the tyrants is now. Our agents have learned that the Javorian Pox only affects the weak Irassians, but any species can act as a carrier for the disease. Every effort must be made to infiltrate their worlds, their space stations, their ships, even their *unintelligible*!

At long last, the Irassians have met a foe that cannot be brought low by their vaunted starfleet. By the *unintelligible*, this opportunity must not be squandered!"
precursor.1520.name: The Ti'Derg Homeworld
precursor.1520.desc:
[From.GetName] was the homeworld of the Ti'Derg roughly 1.2 million years ago, a client species of the Irassian Concordat. They were winged arthropoids, and recovered fossils suggest they were capable of at least limited flight - what little we have seen of their surviving architecture supports this theory.

Unfortunately, there are few remains of this civilization, as the [From.GetPlanetMoon] seems to have been subjected to a massive orbital bombardment.
precursor.1521.desc:
Our study of the alien ruins on [From.From.GetName] has offered us new insights into the final moments of the Irassian Concordat. The Irassians believed that the Ti'Derg were part of a plot together with several of the Concordat's other client species to deliberately spread the Javorian Pox to Irassian worlds.

Whether this was true or not we will likely never know, but the Irassian fleet felt the evidence was compelling enough to incinerate the entire [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] from orbit.
precursor.1525.name: Dead Colony
precursor.1525.desc:
[From.GetName] shows every sign of having been a thriving Irassian colony world up until approximately 1,200,000 years ago. Given their age, the ruins found so far on the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface are in fairly good condition. There are no signs of orbital bombardment or armed conflict.

The Irassian colonists appear to have succumbed to the Javorian Pox, after which the aggressive native flora reclaimed the lifeless cities and hid them under a dense layer of vegetation.
precursor.1526.desc:
After clearing away the vegetation from one of the ancient Irassian settlements on [From.From.GetName] and setting up energy field generators to keep predators at bay, our archaeologists conducted a thorough excavation of the ruins. We now have a much better understanding of what daily life in Irassian society was like.

Among the most valuable finds is a digital atlas, apparently used to teach Irassian children about their empire. It also contains detailed and disparaging descriptions of all of the Concordat's subjugated client species.
precursor.1530.name: Irassian Mining Base
precursor.1530.desc: A series of deep boreholes on the surface of [From.GetName] are all that remain of the Irassian mining operation that was active on this world some 1.2 million years ago. The [Root.GetName] has conducted a thorough surface scan, but we have yet to find the remains of any actual mining facilities.
precursor.1531.desc: After investigating the boreholes on [From.From.GetName], our archaeologists found the fossilized remains of over a hundred Irassian miners at the bottom of one of them. They appear to be more victims of the Javorian Pox that brought about the fall of the Irassian Concordat. In a futile attempt to keep the disease from spreading, their comrades dumped the bodies down one of the boreholes before the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] was evacuated.
precursor.1535.name: Irassian Colony
precursor.1535.desc: [From.GetName] was a young Irassian colony that had only just been founded at the time of their extinction. We have found the sparse ruins of a single settlement and a rudimentary spaceport in the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s northern hemisphere. Judging by the fossilized remains, this world appears to have been among the first to be hit by the Javorian Pox that ravaged Irassian space.
precursor.1536.desc:
Our archaeologists on [From.From.GetName] have made a startling discovery. All evidence points conclusively towards this unassuming [From.From.GetPlanetMoon] having been the origin of the Javorian Pox!

A rare form of native bacteria invaded the Irassian colony due to a manufacturing flaw in a quarantine seal, and from there it spread to the air filters of a visiting merchant ship. Since the pox spread at such an unprecedented rate, it is doubtful whether the Irassians themselves ever had time to learn of its origin.
precursor.1540.name: Derelict Irassian Ship
precursor.1540.desc: A derelict Irassian cruiser has been left forgotten for over a million years in close orbit around [From.GetName]. The slowly spinning vessel shows no obvious signs of weapon damage, and all escape pods remain accounted for. As would be expected, no power signatures can be detected from within its hull.
precursor.1541.desc: The inside of the Irassian cruiser found orbiting [From.From.GetName] contains the dead remains of its full crew complement. Most of them perished as a result of the Javorian Pox that would later render the Irassians extinct, but some of the crew were gunned down by marine guards while trying to reach the escape pods. According to recovered log files, the captain issued strict orders to quarantine the ship after the outbreak became apparent.
precursor.1545.name: Disease Control
precursor.1545.desc:
Debris from what must have been a massive orbital installation has been discovered above [From.GetName]. Artifacts recovered amongst the debris have confirmed that this space station served as the headquarters of the Irassian Concordat's Authority of Disease Control some 1.2 million years ago.

The Irassians were far more susceptible to alien diseases than most known species, and the budget of their public health institute nearly rivaled that of their military. Despite this, surviving records show that their entire species perished from the Javorian Pox.
precursor.1546.desc:
We have recovered the remnants of several research logs from the debris field above [From.From.GetName]. Their final entries are all focused on finding a cure for the Javorian Pox that was sweeping across the Irassian Concordat, and they grow increasingly desperate as the situation worsened.

The last entry reveals that the pox had spread in an uncontrolled fashion on the space station itself. An attachment details all of their failed attempts to produce a cure in the vain hope that the data would be useful to future generations of Irassian scientists.
precursor.1550.name: Asteroid Listening Post
precursor.1550.desc: A small Irassian military listening post has been built into a hollowed-out portion of this asteroid's interior. It is equipped with an array of powerful sensors that seem to be aimed towards neighboring systems. None of them are functional, and the asteroid appears to have been gone over and looted at least once by another party.
precursor.1551.desc: We have learned that the Irassians used the listening post on asteroid [From.From.GetName] to spy and plan attacks on neighboring civilizations during the expansionist phase of their empire. These attacks met with dramatic success, and the Irassians soon became the dominant power in this section of the galaxy. By the time they were decimated by the Javorian Pox, this listening post had long since been abandoned by the Irassian military.
precursor.1555.name: Gas Giant Science Station
precursor.1555.desc: Orbital wreckage that once belonged to a sizable Irassian research station have been found above [From.GetName]. Exactly what the Irassians were researching here remains unclear, but their instruments appear to have been aimed towards the gas giant itself.
precursor.1556.desc:
An analysis of the Irassian orbital wreckage discovered above [From.From.GetName] has yielded few answers, but we have some idea of what their scientists were studying in their research station. Recovered logs make references to some kind of artificial object floating deep inside the gas giant's crushing atmosphere.

The [Root.GetName] has found no trace of such an object despite repeated atmospheric scans, so either the Irassians finally managed to retrieve it or someone else did in the countless years since their demise.
precursor.1600.name: Irassian Home System Located
precursor.1600.desc: After intense study of our recovered Irassian artifacts, scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName] have managed to deduce the exact galactic coordinates of Irass - the home system of the ancient Irassian civilization! We should launch an expedition to this system before someone else beats us to it.
precursor.1601.name: The Irassian Homeworld
precursor.1601.desc:
Irassia - the former homeworld of the Irassian Concordat. Someone has relatively recently (within the last 2,000 years) gone through the trouble of systematically bombarding every square meter of the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon]'s surface from orbit - possibly a misguided attempt to keep the Javorian Pox from resurfacing.

Despite this, the surface is still covered in the fossilized remains of the billions of Irassians who succumbed to the plague in the final years of their empire. By the time it had spread to their homeworld, most of the worlds in the Irassian Concordat had already fallen, and their alien vassals were in open revolt.

Judging by ancient satellite logs recovered from orbit, the mood among the population on the Irassian homeworld was largely resigned by this point. The widespread panic that accompanied the first outbreaks of the pox on the colonies was largely absent, as most had come to accept the fact that the end was drawing near.
precursor.1602.name: Irassian Homeworld Found
precursor.1602.desc.a: This is Irassia, or at least what remains of the once proud capital of the Irassian Concordat. If any artifacts survived the destruction of the Irassian homeworld, someone else has already made off with them - there are clear signs that someone visited here recently.
precursor.1602.desc.b: This world once supported a lush biosphere, until it was erased by a massive orbital bombardment. The survey indicates that the [FromFrom.GetPlanetMoon] was the capital of an ancient civilization known as the "Irassian Concordat." We have learned little else, since other explorers have already made off with everything of value.
precursor.2000.name: The Cybrex
precursor.2000.desc:
We have recovered artifacts from an ancient alien civilization on [From.GetName]! Incredibly, this civilization, which apparently referred to itself as the "Cybrex," seems to have been made up of machines that were linked together in some sort of collective consciousness. The age of the artifacts indicate they were active some 600,000 years ago - in this portion of the galaxy at least - but we have learned nothing of their exact origins.

According to a partial data fragment that our scientists managed to extract from one of the artifacts, the Cybrex at some point launched a crusade to destroy all sapient organic life in the galaxy for reasons unknown.
precursor.2005.name: Kuur Homeworld
precursor.2005.desc: [From.GetName] was the homeworld of the ancient Kuur, an alien civilization wiped out by the Cybrex roughly 600,000 years ago. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] has been thoroughly strip-mined by the machines, and a few scattered ruins are all that remain of the Kuur civilization. The rest has been grounded into dust.
precursor.2006.desc:
We have learned that [From.From.GetName] was the point of origin of the Cybrex. Some kind of sapient machine was created by the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s original inhabitants, the Kuur. Although the details of how it happened are unknown to us, this eventually resulted in the birth of a massive communal machine consciousness - the Cybrex.

At some point they turned on the Kuur, butchering the population of their homeworld in a brief but destructive war that all but destroyed the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s biosphere. The systematic elimination of Kuur colonies in neighboring systems followed, until their civilization had ceased to be.
precursor.2010.name: Indimak Homeworld
precursor.2010.desc:
[From.GetName] was originally the homeworld of the Indimak, another victim of the relentless expansion of the Cybrex. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] was bombarded from orbit until the Indimak offered their surrender. Cybrex warforms then descended to the surface, initiating a program to exterminate the Indimak population that would last for three years.

Along with seven billion Indimak, this also resulted in the destruction of an estimated 97% of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s biota.
precursor.2011.desc:
The biosphere of [From.From.GetName] has only now started recovering from the Cybrex invasion 600,000 years ago. We have found the overgrown ruins of a Cybrex factory, where Indimak slaves were forced to assist in the demise of their own species by building war machines. When their extermination program was reaching completion, the Cybrex "disassembled" the remaining slave workers and dismantled the factories.

Although they initially maintained a significant mining operation on the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon], the Cybrex appear to have later withdrawn from the entire system for unknown reasons.
precursor.2015.name: Broken Cybrex Warforms
precursor.2015.desc: The broken remains of two Cybrex warforms have been discovered in orbit around [From.GetName]. They appear to have been destroyed in battle, but no debris from their adversary has been found. Either they were badly outmatched, or there is more to this engagement than it seems.
precursor.2016.desc:
After studying the wreckage of the two Cybrex warforms over [From.From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has concluded that they were most likely destroyed while fighting each other. This theory explains the lack of non-Cybrex debris, and it fits the damage patterns found on the wrecks.

Why the two Cybrex vessels turned on each other remains a mystery, however. After they were immobilized, both warforms triggered some kind of self-destruct mechanism that fried their neural processors.
precursor.2020.name: Cybrex Invasion
precursor.2020.desc: A massive ground war took place on [From.From.From.GetName] when the Cybrex invaded the [From.From.From.GetPlanetMoon] more than 600,000 years ago. The name of the alien species that fought against them has not survived the passage of time, but they seem to have put up stiff resistance. Broken Cybrex war machines can be found all over the [From.From.From.GetPlanetMoon], and debris from their invasion fleet still drifts in orbit.
precursor.2021.desc:
After their initial invasion of [From.From.GetName] stalemated due to the unexpected tenacity of the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]'s defenders, the Cybrex seem to have withdrawn back into orbit to reconsider their options.

Their solution to the problem was to maneuver two large asteroids on a collision course with the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon]. The impacts destroyed most of the industries and infrastructure the Cybrex had calculated on subverting for their own use, but this was deemed a necessary sacrifice to break the stalemate.
precursor.2025.name: Cybrex Ruins
precursor.2025.desc: [From.GetName] shows signs of having once been a heavily developed Cybrex world. With their typical efficiency, the machines have thoroughly strip-mined the [From.GetPlanetMoon] and ruins from massive factory complexes can be found in both hemispheres. Curiously, a large rectangular area near the equator appears to have been left largely untouched.
precursor.2026.desc:
In a surprising departure from their previous behavior, the Cybrex seem to have established a large reservation on [From.From.GetName] where sapient organics were allowed to live completely undisturbed.

Although they were closely monitored, the Cybrex left the inhabitants to develop on their own, even when a destructive civil war between the organics left the reservation largely depopulated. After several centuries the Cybrex suddenly abandoned the [From.From.GetPlanetMoon], and the reservation's remaining population gradually died out.
precursor.2030.name: Cybrex Listening Post
precursor.2030.desc: [From.GetName] is in fact an artificially constructed object, carefully concealed with a thin layer of rock to make it appear as an asteroid. The hollow interior houses an ancient Cybrex listening post, which was used to spy on space traffic within the system. It has long since ceased functioning.
precursor.2031.desc:
A closer study of asteroid [From.From.GetName] - in reality a hidden Cybrex listening post - has produced some interesting results. For whatever reason, the asteroid was left behind when the rest of the Cybrex vanished from the galaxy. It remained functional for at least 50,000 years after their disappearance, despite increasingly erratic behavior from its administrative AI.

After more than five trillion failed attempts to connect with the Cybrex subspace hub, the AI appears to have suicided by short-circuiting all of the asteroid's systems.
precursor.2035.name: Cybrex Refinery
precursor.2035.desc: Ancient debris from some kind of massive Cybrex refinery complex has been found in orbit around the gas giant [From.GetName]. Lingering energy traces suggest that it was destroyed by some kind of antimatter weapon.
precursor.2036.desc:
Evidence has been found indicating that the Cybrex were mining helium-3 from [From.From.GetName], using their orbital complex to refine the gas before distributing it as fuel to their roving space fleets.

Interestingly, the energy signature of the antimatter weapon that destroyed the facility is distinctly Cybrex in origin. Why would they destroy their own refinery?
precursor.2040.name: Battle Debris
precursor.2040.desc: A colossal space battle occurred in high orbit of [From.GetName] some 600,000 years ago, with ships from at least five different fleets participating. One of the fleets belonged to the Cybrex, although the vast majority of orbital debris seems to come from the other participants.
precursor.2041.desc:
After analyzing the debris left behind from the ancient battle fought above [From.From.GetName], we have learned that four alien empires contemporary with the Cybrex pooled their forces together in a desperate attempt to halt the advancing fleets of the machine consciousness.

Judging by the small amounts of Cybrex debris that was produced by the battle, they were not successful.
precursor.2045.name: Ancient Cybrex Base
precursor.2045.desc: The hostile and unforgiving world of [From.GetName] was home to what once appears to have been a large Cybrex base. Nothing remains of it now aside from scattered debris and a large crater. We will have to investigate the site of the base more closely if we are to learn more.
precursor.2046.desc:
We have found debris on [From.From.GetName] from a large ship that does not appear to have been of Cybrex origin in the crater that was once the site of their base. Our archaeologists speculate that the ship belonged to one of the organic civilizations under Cybrex attack. If so, it may have been sent to collide with the base on some kind of suicide run.

No other explanation for the destruction of the base has been found.
precursor.2050.name: Organic Remains
precursor.2050.desc: The ancient, frozen remains of almost a thousand aliens have been found in the vicinity of [From.GetName]. They come from over a dozen different species and preliminary dating puts the corpses at roughly 600,000 years old... around the same time as the Cybrex machine consciousness ravaged this part of the galaxy.
precursor.2051.desc:
The dead aliens we found above [From.From.GetName] all died from vacuum exposure, and each individual had the barcode the Cybrex were known to laser onto the skin of organic captives. It seems like the Cybrex executed these aliens by "spacing" them, perhaps after having finished interrogations or to keep them from escaping during some kind of rescue operation.

We may never know the truth.
precursor.2055.name: Cybrex Research Station
precursor.2055.desc: A single, badly scorched module is all that is left of a Cybrex research station that once orbited [From.GetName] hundreds of thousands of years ago. The vacuum-exposed inside of the module is filled with the dead remains of creatures that are part machine and part organic.
precursor.2056.desc:
An analysis of the Cybrex research module we found above [From.From.GetName] has revealed that the machine consciousness was experimenting with cybernetic life forms. Hundreds of unfortunate prisoners were transported to this facility for the purpose of having their limbs and organs replaced with various mechanical contraptions.

The exact objective of these tests remains unclear - there is no evidence that the Cybrex ever made use of cybernetic units outside of this lab.
precursor.2100.name: Cybrex Home System Located
precursor.2100.desc: After intense study of our recovered Cybrex artifacts, scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName] have managed to deduce the exact galactic coordinates of a system the ancient machines referred to as "Cybrex Prime" - possibly where their civilization retreated after their abortive attempt to exterminate all sapient organic life! We should launch an expedition to this system before someone else beats us to it.
precursor.2101.name: The Cybrex Central Nexus
precursor.2101.desc:
It would seem that the Cybrex re-evaluated their galactic crusade against organic life at some point during its seventeenth year. Whether this change was prompted by losses on the battlefield or an ideological shift in their networked consensus we may never know, but for whatever reason the Cybrex decided to halt their campaign.

They began a slow withdrawal that lasted for nearly a century, until they eventually vanished completely. We now know that they retreated to this system, where they had constructed a massive ring world designed to house their entire civilization.

They isolated themselves here for several millennia, until an independent explorer chanced upon their system and spread its location to the rest of the galaxy. The news that the dreaded Cybrex had been found again prompted several neighboring powers to organize a massive military expedition, which bombarded the Cybrex ring world into rubble.

Strangely, the Cybrex seem to have offered no resistance whatsoever.
precursor.2102.name: Cybrex Ring World Found
precursor.2102.desc.a: This colossal ring world was clearly built by the Cybrex, and must be where they retreated after their failed crusade. Sadly, others have recently visited here, and it looks like they were quite thorough - nothing of value remains.
precursor.2102.desc.b: Our survey of this intriguing ring world has revealed that it was constructed by some kind of machine civilization known as the "Cybrex"... but unfortunately, we have been able to learn little else. Other explorers have already scoured this system of anything valuable.
precursor.2200.name: Living Metal
precursor.2200.desc:
As Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports [RogueLeader.GetHerHis] findings about the immense ring world in the [From.GetStarName] system [RogueLeader.GetSheHe] can barely contain [RogueLeader.GetHerHis] awe. The immensity of the rings are beyond our comprehension, the time required to construct even one of the sections are far beyond us.

The scans reveal a rare new resource we've never encountered before, a living metal, which is abundant on the rings. This material might be one of the reasons the ring's creators could construct it in the first place. Research this technology might bring us closer to their knowledge.
precursor.301.name: Precursor Discovery
precursor.301.a.desc: Intercepted communications from a group of independent prospectors indicate that they recently found something relating to an ancient Precursor civilization on [precursor_planet.GetName]. Superstition compelled them to leave the [precursor_planet.GetPlanetMoon] alone, so whatever they discovered must still be there.
precursor.301.b.desc: Several merchant ships passing in the vicinity of [precursor_planet.GetName] have independently of each other reported anomalous readings coming from the direction of the [precursor_planet.GetPlanetMoon]. After studying these readings, experts on [Root.Capital.GetName] believe they may be indicative of ancient Precursor activity.
precursor.301.c.desc: Authorities on [Root.Capital.GetName] recently exposed a large smuggling ring, and many arrests have been made. In an attempt to bargain for leniency, one of the smuggler captains gave us the coordinates of a [precursor_planet.GetPlanetMoon] that supposedly contains remnants of an ancient Precursor civilization.
precursor.301.d.desc: Several recruits from our ground forces recently made a HALO insertion onto the surface of [precursor_planet.GetName] as part of a survival training exercise. When the recruits were picked up again after two months, one of them reported several findings indicating that an ancient Precursor civilization had a presence on this world long ago.
precursor.301.e.desc: Diagnostic Array Theta has registered a possible irregularity on [precursor_planet.GetName]. No [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] units are known to be operating in the vicinity of this uninhabited astronomical body, but a preliminary analysis indicates that it may have been visited by a Precursor civilization at some point in the distant past.
precursor.301.f.desc: Patrol [root.GetIndividualNamePlural] performing a routine surface sweep of [precursor_planet.GetName] have alerted us to an irregularity within our controlled space. Signs of possible activity consistent with a Precursor civilization have been sighted.
precursor.302.name: Vultaum Artifact Recovered
precursor.303.name: Yuht Artifact Recovered
precursor.304.name: First League Artifact Recovered
precursor.305.name: Irassian Artifact Recovered
precursor.306.name: Cybrex Artifact Recovered
precursor.302.a.desc: A thorough investigation of [precursor_planet.GetName] has unearthed evidence of a past [Root.Owner.GetPrecursorCiv] presence. An away team from the [Root.GetName] has managed to bring a relatively well-preserved artifact back to the ship, which should hopefully increase our knowledge of this ancient civilization.
precursor.302.b.desc: Retrieval units operating out of the [Root.GetName] have successfully recovered an artifact from [precursor_planet.GetName] whose origins can be traced back to the [Root.Owner.GetPrecursorCiv] Precursor civilization. Our databanks are currently being updated with the new information we have gained through the study of this item.
precursor.320.desc: Analysis of the minor artifacts suggests that there may be a Precursor connection on or near [precursor_planet.GetName].
VULTAUM_ARTIFACT_FOUND_DESC: We have learned that there may have been Precursor activity on [precursor_planet.GetName] at some point in the galactic past. The sphere of influence of the ancient Vultaum Star Assembly is known to have extended to this region of space, making this world a promising lead in our ongoing efforts to learn more about their civilization.
YUHT_ARTIFACT_FOUND_DESC: We have learned that there may have been Precursor activity on [precursor_planet.GetName] at some point in the galactic past. The sphere of influence of the ancient Yuht Empire is known to have extended to this region of space, making this world a promising lead in our ongoing efforts to learn more about their civilization.
LEAGUE_ARTIFACT_FOUND_DESC: We have learned that there may have been Precursor activity on [precursor_planet.GetName] at some point in the galactic past. The sphere of influence of the ancient First League is known to have extended to this region of space, making this world a promising lead in our ongoing efforts to learn more about their civilization.
IRASSIAN_ARTIFACT_FOUND_DESC: We have learned that there may have been Precursor activity on [precursor_planet.GetName] at some point in the galactic past. The sphere of influence of the ancient Irassian Concordat is known to have extended to this region of space, making this world a promising lead in our ongoing efforts to learn more about their civilization.
CYBREX_ARTIFACT_FOUND_DESC: We have learned that there may have been Precursor activity on [precursor_planet.GetName] at some point in the galactic past. The sphere of influence of the ancient Cybrex is known to have extended to this region of space, making this world a promising lead in our ongoing efforts to learn more about their civilization.
new_precursor_project: A new archaeological special project is available on [precursor_planet.GetName].
precursor.310.name: Private Collector
precursor.310.desc: A private collector on [collector_home.GetName] has somehow come into ownership of an ancient Precursor artifact believed to be [Root.GetPrecursorCiv] in origin. Despite government pressure, the collector has so far been reluctant to part with it.
buy_precursor_artifact: Buy the artifact for an exorbitant sum.
seize_precursor_artifact: Declare the artifact to be state property and have it seized by the local authorities.
leave_precursor_artifact: Leave the artifact in the collector's care.
precursor.311.desc:
Greetings from [artifact_seller.Capital.GetName]. There is a matter my government wishes to discuss.

We understand that your archaeologists have been studying the ancient [Root.GetPrecursorCiv] civilization for quite some time. Understandable, since their territory once covered a large part of what today constitutes the [Root.GetName].

As it happens, their territory also extended into what is now the [artifact_seller.GetName], and [artifact_seller.GetSpeciesAdj] archaeologists have recovered a number of unique artifacts. If you are interested, we would be willing to sell you one of these artifacts.
precursor.311.a.reply: Excellent. We will make arrangements to transport the artifact to [Root.Capital.GetName] at once.
precursor.311.b.reply: You drive a hard bargain, but we would expect nothing less from [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]. We accept your offer.
precursor.311.c: Surrender that artifact now or suffer the consequences.
precursor.312.desc: The [artifact_seller.GetName] does not give in to threats. You have made new enemies this day, [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural]!
precursor.313.desc: I... we... the [artifact_seller.GetName] will of course gladly donate the artifact to the [Root.GetName], in the interest of fostering amicable relations between our two star nations.
purchase_artifact: We purchase a Precursor artifact from the [artifact_seller.GetName].
coerce_artifact: We attempt to coerce the [artifact_seller.GetName] into giving us their Precursor artifact.
precursor.314.desc:
Greetings, [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] friends.

A recent [artifact_giver.GetSpeciesAdj] archaeological expedition on one of our planets uncovered several artifacts believed to have originated in the ancient [Root.GetPrecursorCiv] Precursor civilization.
