diplomatic.16.desc: Your scientist, [encroaching_research_leader.GetName], has been paying undue attention to stars in constellations our people hold sacred. We cannot allow anyone to operate in our territory who does not pay proper respect to our faith and its legends.
diplomatic.16.a: This must be some form of misunderstanding.
diplomatic.17.name: Heretical Discovery in [From.GetName]
diplomatic.17.desc:
Conducting research in foreign-controlled space requires tact, something we sometimes overlook in recruiting our scientists. This became apparent when [encroaching_research_leader.GetName] recently ran into trouble studying some of the stars in sacred [From.GetAdj] constellations. Locals objected to a clinical examination of the subject and hassled [encroaching_research_leader.GetHimHer] until [From.GetRulerTitle] [From.GetRulerName] made a statement sanctioning the research.

[encroaching_research_leader.GetName], apparently spiteful over the protest, appears to have taken the time to actually find material suggesting that some of the [From.GetAdj] legends surrounding the stars may be wildly inconsistent with their real age and development. This is likely to cause further outrage if published.
diplomatic.17.a: [encroaching_research_leader.GetIsAreCap] [encroaching_research_leader.GetSheHe] deliberately trying to cause a scandal? Fire [encroaching_research_leader.GetHimHer].
diplomatic.17.b: Things like these happen in the course of research.
diplomatic.18.name: [encroaching_research_leader.GetName] Publishes Heresy
diplomatic.18.desc:
Despite our trust in the best intentions of the [From.GetName] researcher who has been studying our ancient constellations, [encroaching_research_leader.GetSheHe] [encroaching_research_leader.GetHasHave] managed to upset our people by re-evaluating the stars' age and arguing that the development of their brightness and visibility conflicts with our legends about the constellations.

The people who originally objected to the project are arguing that this was done deliberately out of malice by the scientist after they requested an end to the studies. The [From.GetAdj] government has decided to gloss over the issue and refused to take action to prevent the anger and pain the report is likely to cause among our people.
diplomatic.18.a: We should never have trusted them to respect us.
diplomatic.19.name: Exotic Woodwind
diplomatic.19.desc:
Music has taken many forms among the beings we have encountered since leaving [Root.GetHomeWorldName], and the methods and preferences continue to baffle us. Sometimes alien music is inaudible to us, while at other times, the waves are strong enough to destroy our capacity for hearing. Coming across music that we love more than its creators is a rare occasion indeed.

Such a rare occasion has occurred recently on [music_listening_planet.GetName]. Located close to the [music_origin_country.GetAdj] border, radio stations playing music from the other side have grown immensely in popularity. It appears some instrument from [music_origin_country.GetHomeWorldName] is not just pleasant, but appears to cause [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] bodies to resonate, causing a relaxing feeling in the [Root.GetSpeciesOrganName]. Whatever this instrument is, it's unlike any of our own.
diplomatic.19.a: An excellent time to learn more about their culture.
diplomatic.19.b: Let us be careful and study this instrument.
diplomatic.20.name: Instrumental Biology
diplomatic.20.desc: Having taken a closer look at the alien music, we have discovered that it is made by a wind instrument made from one of the native plants native on their homeworld. The unusual internal structure of the plant is completely different from anything on [Root.GetHomeWorldName], even on molecular level. The effect of air passing through the plant on [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] bodies has advanced our understanding of floral biology on alien worlds.
diplomatic.20.a: Who knows what we can find?
diplomatic.21.name: [neighbor_contesting_colony.GetName] Objects to Expansion
diplomatic.21.desc: Your new colony on [Root.GetName] is located very close to our borders. We would prefer it if you withdrew from this frontier, to avoid future conflicts over where our border should be drawn.
diplomatic.21.b: The colony is part of our future. It stays.
diplomatic.1000.name: Fleet Maneuvers
diplomatic.1000.desc:
Commander [exercise_admiral.GetName] has drawn up plans for a major fleet exercise that will involve a substantial portion of our navy. The location [exercise_admiral.GetSheHe] [exercise_admiral.GetHasHave] chosen for these maneuvers is the [exercise_system.GetName] system, which is close to the border of the [exercise_neighbor.GetName].

The [exercise_neighbor.GetSpeciesNamePlural] may see this as a major provocation, but if we cancel the exercise our military will consider it a sign of weakness. After all, [exercise_system.GetName] lies within our space - the [exercise_neighbor.GetName] has no right to tell us what we can or cannot do in our own backyard.
diplomatic.1000.a: Carry out the maneuvers as planned.
FLEET_MANEUVERS_1_PROJECT_DESC:
Major fleet maneuvers have been planned in the [exercise_system.GetName] system, close to the border of the [exercise_neighbor.GetName]. The purpose of this exercise is to simulate a hostile probe by significant [exercise_neighbor.GetSpeciesName] forces into our space, as a possible prelude to an invasion.

The exercise will begin once all of the allocated forces have reached the initial staging area in orbit of [exercise_location.GetName].
FLEET_MANEUVERS_2_PROJECT_DESC:
Major fleet maneuvers have been planned in the [exercise_system.GetName] system, close to the border of the [exercise_neighbor.GetName]. The purpose of this exercise is to simulate a hostile probe by significant [exercise_neighbor.GetSpeciesName] forces into our space, as a possible prelude to an invasion.

The exercise will begin once all of the allocated forces have reached the initial staging area in orbit of [exercise_location.GetName].
FLEET_MANEUVERS_3_PROJECT_DESC:
Major fleet maneuvers have been planned in the [exercise_system.GetName] system, close to the border of the [exercise_neighbor.GetName]. The purpose of this exercise is to simulate a hostile probe by significant [exercise_neighbor.GetSpeciesName] forces into our space, as a possible prelude to an invasion.

The exercise will begin once all of the allocated forces have reached the initial staging area in orbit of [exercise_location.GetName].
diplomatic.1001.name: Fleet Maneuvers Canceled
diplomatic.1001.desc: The plans to hold a major fleet exercise have been canceled. Continuous delays in moving the allocated forces into position means that to proceed now would seriously impair the readiness level of the entire fleet.
diplomatic.1002.desc: As the [Root.GetName] is now involved in a shooting war, the major fleet exercise we had planned has been canceled. Our naval crews will have to gain experience on the field of battle instead.
diplomatic.1006.name: Naval Activity in [exercise_system.GetName]
diplomatic.1006.desc: We have received intelligence reports of significant fleet movements within the [From.Owner.GetName]. They seem to be centered on the [exercise_system.GetName] system - suspiciously close to our border. What are the [From.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] up to?
diplomatic.1011.name: Fleet Maneuvers: Collisions
diplomatic.1011.desc: The complex maneuvers devised by Commander [exercise_admiral.GetName] have resulted in several minor collisions during the naval drills currently being held in the [exercise_system.GetName] system. Crew casualties were minimal and none of the involved ships suffered critical damage, but they will require some yard work upon the conclusion of the exercise.
diplomatic.1011.a: At least no ships were lost.
exercise_collision_tooltip: Several of our ships have sustained damage from collisions.
diplomatic.1012.name: Fleet Maneuvers: Ships Lost
diplomatic.1012.desc: The [destroyed_ship_1.GetName] and the [destroyed_ship_2.GetName] were both tragically lost with all hands when the two starships collided during a high-speed maneuver that was part of the ongoing [exercise_system.GetName] naval drills. Next of kin have been notified.
exercise_ships_lost: Two of our ships have been lost due to an accidental collision.
diplomatic.1013.name: Fleet Maneuvers: Promising Officer
diplomatic.1013.desc: Captain [exercise_officer.GetName] of the [officer_ship.GetName] has shown a great deal of promise during the ongoing fleet exercises in the [exercise_system.GetName] system. The young officer has displayed initiative along with considerable leadership abilities, and the Admiralty has seen fit to immediately promote [exercise_officer.GetHerHim] to flag rank.
diplomatic.1013.a: The fleet is always in need of capable commanders.
diplomatic.1014.name: Fleet Maneuvers: Public Interest
diplomatic.1014.desc: The ongoing naval drills in the [exercise_system.GetName] system have attracted considerable media attention on [Root.Capital.GetName] and the colonies. Unclassified holo recordings showing some of the more dramatic maneuvers have made the public enamored with the valiant defenders of the [Root.GetName] serving in the fleet. Volunteers are flocking to our naval recruitment stations!
diplomatic.1020.name: Intelligence on [From.Owner.GetSpeciesName] Maneuvers
diplomatic.1020.desc:
Our intelligence assets have gathered more information on the increased [From.Owner.GetSpeciesName] naval activity in the [exercise_system.GetName] system. The [From.Owner.GetName] seems to have gathered a large fleet there to conduct some kind of massive naval exercise on an unprecedented scale.

As of yet there are no signs that this exercise will translate into direct military operations against the [Root.GetName], its proximity to our border can only be seen as a deliberate provocation! How should we respond?
exercise_diplomatic_protest: We make our displeasure at these exercises known to the [From.Owner.GetName].
diplomatic.1021.desc:
The [From.GetName] objects in the strongest possible terms to the provocative military exercise currently being held in the [exercise_system.GetName] system by [Root.GetSpeciesName] naval units.

To stage fleet maneuvers on such an unprecedented scale so close to our borders can only be construed as a thinly veiled threat. Our own forces have been placed on maximum alert, and our fleet commanders have been instructed to respond to any border violations with overwhelming force.
diplomatic.1021.a: Tell the [From.GetSpeciesNamePlural] to stay out of our affairs!
diplomatic.1021.b: We can't afford an incident... cancel the exercise.
diplomatic.1021.c: Our diplomats will smooth things over.
exercise_diplomatic_hardline: We make a hard-line diplomatic response to their obnoxious little protest.
exercise_diplomatic_canceled: We cancel our ongoing fleet maneuvers to improve relations with the [From.GetName]. The military will not be pleased.
exercise_diplomatic_conciliatory: We make a conciliatory response to lessen the diplomatic damage, but the exercise continues.
diplomatic.1022.desc:
We have received your poorly phrased objection to the military exercises our glorious naval forces are currently conducting in the [exercise_system.GetName] system. Since that system, as you are no doubt aware, lies well within the sovereign territory of the [From.GetName], we do not see how what transpires there could possibly be any of your business.

The [Root.GetName] would do well not to send us any more such provocative and reckless diplomatic correspondence in the future.

This transmission ends now.
diplomatic.1023.desc:
In light of the objections voiced by the [Root.GetName] to our naval maneuvers in the [exercise_system.GetName] system, the [From.GetName] has decided to terminate all ongoing exercises in the interest of fostering better relations between our two star nations.

It is our sincere hope that this action will help to defuse interstellar tensions while proving beyond doubt the [From.GetSpeciesName] commitment towards a lasting galactic peace.
diplomatic.1023.a: Perhaps they are earnest in their quest for peace...
diplomatic.1024.desc:
The [From.GetName] deeply regrets any misunderstandings our ongoing military exercises in the [exercise_system.GetName] system might have caused.

These naval drills were planned well in advance, and the location was chosen at random by our commanders. In no way should this be construed as some kind of threat or provocation directed at the [Root.GetName].
diplomatic.1025.name: Maneuvers Concluded
diplomatic.1025.desc: The fleet maneuvers conducted by the [exercise_fleet.GetName] in the [exercise_system.GetName] system have been concluded. Commander [exercise_admiral.GetName] reports that we have learned much from this exercise, in large part due to its immense scale. Despite any potential diplomatic repercussions, the military benefits, at least, have been substantial.
diplomatic.1026.name: [From.Owner.GetSpeciesName] Maneuvers Concluded
diplomatic.1026.desc: Judging by the sudden drop in coded [From.Owner.GetSpeciesName] military transmissions coming from the [exercise_system.GetName] system, the naval exercise that was being held there by the [From.Owner.GetName] has finally come to an end.
precursor_1_desc: Their knowledge was vast, their theories complex. But did their search for ultimate truth lead to enlightenment, or oblivion?
precursor_2_desc: They roamed the stars, always searching, ever expanding. Now, only their ruins remain, whispering of unforeseen consequences.
precursor_3_desc: Unity is fragile. What force shattered a once flourishing federation whose influence spanned entire sectors?
precursor_4_desc: Even the mightiest civilizations fall to unseen foes. Did arrogance blind them, or did ignorance seal their fate?
precursor_5_desc: For a time, nothing could stand against them, until something shattered their resolve. What brought their crusade to an end?
precursor_baol_1_desc: They cultivated entire worlds, shaping ecosystems with care. But even the deepest roots can be torn from the ground.
precursor_zroni_1_desc: The mind is limitless. Their thoughts carried them across the stars, reshaping existence. But even those who see beyond do not always see alike.
precursor_inetian_desc: Prosperity breeds ambition, and ambition invites ruin. What force unraveled their web remains unknown, but profit alone was not enough to save them.
precursor_adakkaria_desc: They rode the tides of the cosmos, never bound, never still. But even wanderers cannot roam forever.
AST_WAVELENGTHS_1_DESC: The asteroid [Root.GetName] is emitting some form of radiation in controlled bursts. Is someone - something - trying to communicate with us?
AST_DEBRIS_FIELD_1_DESC: Sensors report a number of possible points of interest within the dense debris field surrounding [Root.GetName].
HBL_LUSH_PLANET_1_DESC: [Root.GetName] is exceptionally green, and preliminary scans indicate that there might be several articles of interest on the surface.
UHB_ANCIENT_RUINS_1_DESC: Impressive structures litter [Root.GetName]'s surface, practically begging for some archaeological work.
UHB_MOLTEN_CHART_DESC: A weak distress signal originates from the superheated surface of [Root.GetName].
GEN_PLAYGROUND_DESC: Impressive structures litter a small area on the surface of [Root.GetName], practically begging for some archaeological work.
AST_SHRINE_1_DESC: [Root.GetName] has been partially hollowed out and carved with exquisite precision. There is something familiar about the lines and curves etched into the rock...
HBL_MUSIC_1_DESC: There is a pattern of unusual sonic activity on [Root.GetName].
GAS_ZRO_ICE_DESC: It seems [Root.GetName] is lacking the hydrogen and helium to be classified as a proper gas giant and is, in fact, an ice giant.
AST_ILLICIT_DARK_DESC: [Root.GetName] periodically spews an alarmingly eclectic mix of particles and radiation into the void.
TOX_PURPLE_RAIN_DESC: [Root.GetName]'s toxic biosphere gives the planet a unique color scheme.
FROZ_BASE_DESC: Sensors pick up unexpected activity from an isolated point on [Root.GetName]'s frozen surface.
FROZ_BASE2_DESC: Sensors pick up unexpected activity from an isolated point on [Root.GetName]'s arctic surface.
TROP_PETS_DESC: Irregular patterns of movement have been detected within the dense tropical undergrowth of [Root.GetName].
BARR_BASE_DESC: A cursory scan of the planet's surface reveals a weak signal pulsing into the darkness of space.
PROJ_MOON_DESC: According to preliminary scans, [Root.GetName] is exhibiting several strange properties and gives readings that are not at all in line with what one would expect from a planet of this type...
SEA_DESC: Vaguely-defined shapes swirl with the currents in [Root.GetName]'s vast oceans.
MOLTEN_BASE_DESC: Sensors pick up rhythmic movement on the hellish surface of [Root.GetName].
LEVELED_DESC: [Root.GetName] seems to exhibit one, and only one, interesting geological feature...
DIMENSIONAL_POCKET_DESC: The debris field which [Root.GetName] is part of roils and swirls under the influence of unknown forces.
HAB_CORN_DESC: Optical scans indicate that the surface of [Root.GetName] is unusually verdant in places.
HAB_MAT_DESC: Backscattering spectrometry sensors indicate the presence of valuable substances in the planet's crust.
ATM_ANOMALY_DESC: Atmospheric readings from [Root.GetName] do not match simulated projections.
FRBR_GRIMACING_DESC: Repeated scans of [Root.GetName]'s surface give inconsistent sensor readings, almost as if the planet itself was in a constant state of upheaval.
FROZ_ILLUMINATED_DESC: Inexplicable optical phenomena play across the surface of [Root.GetName], clearly visible from space.
GAS_CLOUDY_DESC: The atmospheric patterns of [Root.GetName] are highly atypical for a gas giant of modest size.
GAIA_MOVE_DESC: As a Gaia-class planet, [Root.GetName] is expected to teem with life...
FROZ_BOX_DESC: Scans indicate the presence of a foreign, alien-made object on one of [Root.GetName]'s many frozen mountain tops.
CONT_SIGNS_DESC:
[Root.GetName]'s surface appears heavily pockmarked, which is not unusual.

What is unusual is the regular shape of the scars, irregularly distributed. This is unlikely to be the result of meteorite impacts.
AST_CRATER_DESC: [Root.GetName] is home to a number of exquisite impact craters. However, something breaks the visual uniformity in one of the larger craters...
BAR_COLONY_DESC: Optical sensors isolate a cluster of shapes on the barren surface of [Root.GetName] that could be buildings.
TOX_MAT_DESC: Backscattering spectrometry sensors indicate the presence of valuable substances beneath [Root.GetName]'s noxious clouds.
AST_CLUSTER_DESC: An unusually deliberate, geometric configuration of minerals drifts through the debris belt by [Root.GetName], and is possibly of alien origin.
GAEA_CHECKERED_DESC: Visual scans of [Root.GetName]'s surface reveal a grid pattern seemingly covering the entire planet.
GEN_ABANDONED_SHIP_DESC:
A cursory scan of [Root.GetName] yields surprising results.

Something seems to be scanning us back...
GEN_DESERT_DESC: The atmosphere of [Root.GetName] is extremely thin, and yet something not unlike wind seems to agitate the seas of sand that make up its surface.
TOX_STRUCTURES_DESC: Somewhere beneath [Root.GetName]'s unctuous clouds, unnatural structures silhouette themselves against the toxic surface.
TROP_WOODS_DESC: The surface of [Root.GetName] is dominated by particularly impressive-looking trees.
HOLE_RADIATION_DESC: Sensors pick up unusual readings in the vicinity of [Root.GetName] - readings that are hard to explain being this close to a black hole.
UHB_BUOY_DESC: A wavering signal haunts [Root.GetName], though it does not seem to originate from the planet's surface.
GAIA_RECORD_DESC: [Root.GetName]'s verdant plains are quiet, save for a weak but steady beacon signal.
CRYSTAL_MANUFACTORY_DESC: An old, seemingly abandoned structure looms over [Root.GetName], an otherwise unremarkable asteroid.
anomaly.75.name: Rock Brain
anomaly.75.desc: A scan of the particularly massive asteroid [From.GetName] yields fascinating results. The rock's core is shot through with a network of conductive crystals carrying a weak electric charge. The crew on the [Root.GetName] recognize this matrix as a primitive neural lattice and believe the celestial body to be thinking in some capacity, if not fully sapient. They seek permission to excavate the core and transport it to the nearest orbital station for closer study.
anomaly.75.b: Make do with what you can study from the surface.
anomaly.75.b.tooltip:
Adds the Rock Brain modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ +8
anomaly.75.c: It is not so unlike us. Let us talk.
anomaly.75.c.tooltip: Order [Root.GetName] to attach surface probes to [From.GetName] and decode its alleged neural activity
anomaly.76.desc:
[rock_scientist.GetName] here. It was a challenge, but I think we've managed to parse the readings into something like... not language perhaps, but concepts. Ideas. And we can feed something similar back to the asteroid, to maybe communicate.

We'll display some of the <filtered output>, and I'll do my best to give a more "complete interpretation" of the raw data.
anomaly.76.a: On second thought, this seems ill-advised.
anomaly.76.a.tooltip: Abort any attempts at contacting [rock_brain.GetName] directly, and study it from afar
anomaly.77.desc:
<new> <thoughts>. <reason>. <reason> <perplexing>.


"To provide some context, [rock_brain.GetName] has no sensory organs in the traditional sense. It is perceiving our input as its own thoughts. To an extent."
anomaly.77.a: <Do you understand that we are not you?>
anomaly.77.a.response:
<thought>-<different> <reconciliation>-<same> <divergence>-<different>.


"It is unconvinced that we are anything but a cerebral blip, but it has entertained such cognitive ghosts in the past. We are a fleeting diversion."
anomaly.77.b: <How long have you been drifting in orbit of [rock_sun.GetName]?>
anomaly.77.b.response:
<not>... <previous> <not>. <not>.


"[rock_brain.GetName] does not recognize nor even perceive the existence of the star [rock_sun.GetName]. It also lacks a concept of time, outside of a limited grasp of the successive occurrence of thought."
anomaly.77.c: "Are we getting anything useful out of this?"
anomaly.77.c.response:
<...>


"Oh yes, this exchange is evolving our fuzzy decoder nets at an incredible rate. I am amazed this is working as well as it is, but I am picking up some alarming readings..."
anomaly.78.desc:
<quer--. <query>


"As I feared. Our probes are bleeding [rock_brain.GetName] of the energy that drives its cognition. [rock_brain.GetName] is not a perfectly closed system so this would have happened eventually - though in tens of thousands of years, rather than now..."
anomaly.78.a: <Is there anything we can do to help you?>
anomaly.78.a.response:
<am>.


"It says it's fine, but it's not fine. We have tried feeding some energy back into the neural lattice but that only produces noisier brain waves, not stronger ones. We've already crossed the threshold, what little energy remains will soon peter out no matter what we do. It has no means of detecting its cognition slowing down, nor any reason to predict that this spells its end. Nor any idea about what it means to die..."
anomaly.78.b1.response:
<perceive>-<within> <repeat>. <[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]>.


"It will think of us again, or it is now, again, embodying us through its thoughts? I'm afraid the signal is fading rapidly. We are also not sure what to make of "[rock_fallen_empire.GetRealName]" - it appears to be the closest to traditional language we've gotten from [rock_brain.GetName], but its meaning remains obscure. Maybe our interpretation algorithms are simply breaking down as the subject's neural lattice fails."
anomaly.78.b2.response:
<perceive>-<within> <repeat>.


"It will think of us again. Rather, it is now once again embodying us through its thoughts? I'm afraid the signal is fading rapidly - or maybe our interpretation algorithms are simply breaking down as the subject's neural lattice fails."
anomaly.79.desc: [rock_brain.GetName] is silent. All attempts by Science Officer [rock_scientist.GetName] to recharge the mineral lattice within the asteroid have failed; whatever spark of sapience once animated its rough-hewn neurons is gone, but we have learned much from this distant evolutionary cousin.
anomaly.79.a: Was it the last of its kind, or the first?
anomaly.80.name: Rock Migraine
anomaly.80.desc:
The core of [From.From.GetName], once coaxed from beneath the crust of the asteroid, does not respond well to the vacuum of space. The [Root.GetName]'s instruments read a sudden energy spike moments before the rocky lump gently, but decisively, fractures.

Large chunks of the conductive mineral are salvaged, but whatever spectral charge animated them is now gone.
anomaly.80.a: The crystals are still valuable in their own right.
anomaly.81.desc:
Our necromancers have scored new traces across the asteroid's delicate mineral seams, crude invocations hewn in stone and suffused with a pulsing current. Yet, the consciousness that was [rock_brain.GetName] remains lost to us.

It is something different now, suspended in a sinister dream - fitted with directional thrusters and awaiting our command.
anomaly.85.name: Gossiping Planets
anomaly.85.desc: Irregular electromagnetic bursts from [From.GetName] and its neighboring planets intrigue the crew of the [Root.GetName]. Further study reveals that the bursts are coded communications, though the contents are fairly banal. The electromagnetic activity suddenly ceases, as if in response to the eavesdropping, but not before the [Root.GetName] has cataloged the self-reported statuses of [From.GetName] and every other planet in the system.
anomaly.85.a: Use the data to further research long-range communications.
anomaly.85.b: Map the status data to every planet in the system.
anomaly.90.name: Grasping Vines
anomaly.90.desc:
The dense grasses of [From.GetName] respond to the [Root.GetName]'s exploratory probes by disassembling them in a spectacularly violent manner. As sinewy vines reach for the ship far above, the relative lack of animal life on the planet starts making sense.

A Special Project has been issued for further study of the planet's plant life.
anomaly.91.name: Grassy Militia
anomaly.91.desc:
Careful examination reveals that the violent behavior of the vines and grasses of [From.From.GetName] is no dumb self-defense reflex.

The plants have a complex internal social order. Depending on geographical region, different phyla assume a number of different tasks, the most important one seemingly being staving off native herbivores and would-be invaders from the skies.
anomaly.91.a.tooltip:
Adds the Cunning Flora modifier to [From.From.GetName]:
£ +6
anomaly.95.name: Important to Someone Else
anomaly.95.desc: An aluminum plaque is found drifting among the detritus around [From.GetName], its anodized surface standing out from the metal debris surrounding it. It depicts two ridiculous-looking mammalian figures and some rather tasteless geometric shapes.
anomaly.95.a: It might make a good coaster for my drink.
anomaly.95.c: I'm sure someone would be willing to pay for it.
anomaly.95.b.tooltip: Adds the coordinates of the Sol system to the Situation Log.
anomaly.96.name: Terra Firma
anomaly.96.desc.neutral:
The directions inferred from the inscribed plaque were largely accurate.

This is the system of Sol, with the plaque apparently originating from the planet our astronomers have labeled Sol III.
anomaly.96.desc.phobe: We have found the alleged source of the tacky metal scrap we recovered. The system of Sol is a pinprick in space centered on a pitiful yellow dwarf, a backwater completely eclipsed by the splendor of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.96.desc.phile: We have finally reached the system of Sol, a destination some being went to great pains to communicate through a very primitive medium. The plaque's point of origin is seemingly the third rock from the sun, which should be a continental planet.
anomaly.96.a.phobe: Make a statement. Jettison the plaque into their sun.
anomaly.96.a.phile: You shouted into the void, and we came.
anomaly.100.name: Catching up with a Pioneer
anomaly.100.desc: An aluminum plate, anodized gold, is recovered from the surface of [From.GetName]. Everyone aboard the [Root.GetName] recognize it long before analysis and database cross-referencing confirm its origins.
anomaly.105.name: Old-Timey Tunes
anomaly.105.desc: A golden disc strikes the forward viewport of the [Root.GetName] as it is surveying the weak gravitational field of [From.GetName]. The object is recovered, and cursory analysis indicates that the minuscule grooves on the disc's surface might be encoded audio and video data, authored by some alien civilization.
anomaly.105.a: It might make a good coaster for a very big drink.
anomaly.105.c: Xeno-audiophiles would pay a lot for this.
anomaly.105.b.tooltip: Adds the Sol system coordinates to the Situation Log.
anomaly.106.name: Terra Firma
anomaly.106.desc.neutral:
The directions inferred from the audiovisual record were largely accurate.

This is the system of Sol, with the disc apparently originating from the planet our astronomers have labeled Sol III.
anomaly.106.desc.phobe: We have found the alleged source of the tacky disc we recovered. The system of Sol is a pinprick in space centered on a pitiful yellow dwarf, a backwater completely eclipsed by the splendor of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.106.desc.phile: We have finally reached the system of Sol, a destination some being went to great pains to communicate through a very primitive medium. The disc's point of origin is seemingly the third rock from the sun, which should be a continental planet.
anomaly.106.a.phobe: Make a statement. Jettison the record into their sun.
anomaly.106.a.phile: You shouted into the void, and we came.
anomaly.110.name: Voices From the Past
anomaly.110.desc:
In an abandoned fortress on the surface of [From.GetName], evidently the stronghold of some long-dead race of [Owner.GetPreFTLLowerPlural], a golden disc rests on a pedestal beneath a thick covering of spore-dust.

First designated to be stowed away as an alien artifact of minor, possibly xeno-religious significance, an archival computer soon identifies it as the golden phonograph record originally launched with the Voyager probe.
anomaly.115.name: Cell Cells
anomaly.115.desc: [From.GetName] is partially hollow. Within its interior spaces sprawls a dense honeycomb structure crafted of some unknown alloy, housing containers of alien genetic material. By all appearances this is an archive of life, the genetic record of some earlier civilization come and gone. Most of the DNA is hopelessly degraded, but there is still much to learn here.
anomaly.120.name: Eddic, Monolithic
anomaly.120.desc:
[From.GetName] is uninhabited and indeed uninhabitable, but not unvisited. Its surface is littered with tall cenotaphs carved from some mineral not native to the planet; evidently placed here by some artistically-inclined spacefaring race. The monoliths' flowing lines deftly chart a history so fantastical it must surely be fictional.

Surely.
anomaly.120.b.tooltip: Make digital reproductions of the monoliths widely available in our Empire.
anomaly.121.desc:
The annotated reproductions of the monolithic imagery found on [From.From.GetName] prove immensely popular in the [Root.GetName].

Many citizens state that the fantastical annals have completely changed how they feel about aliens.
anomaly.125.name: Unsolicited Mapping
anomaly.125.desc: Intercepting the distress signal, the [Root.GetName] sends a probe down to the volatile surface of [From.GetName]. It seems an unregistered freighter recently crashed on the planet; whatever it was carrying has been reduced an ashen sludge, but some data from the navigation computer can be recovered and survey data for this system reconstructed.
anomaly.130.name: Gravity Crush
anomaly.130.desc:
The [Root.GetName]'s survey of the asteroid is temporarily halted as a probe is caught by an errant gravitational anomaly.

The probe manages to transmit some data before it is brutally crushed by the extreme forces - forces that completely dissipate soon after.
anomaly.130.a: At least no one got hurt.
anomaly.135.name: Abandoned Amusement Park
anomaly.135.desc:
The structures on [From.GetName] are not as old as we first believed. It is a playground or amusement park of some sort. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] notes that many of the contraptions are highly complex creations that we can learn much from and that, from the builders' alien point of view, this might have been a cutting-edge sensor array or even a gigantic art installation.

Regardless, to us [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural], it looks mostly like a place where you would take your young and let them amuse themselves.
anomaly.140.name: Familiar Shrine
anomaly.140.desc:
Most of the asteroid has been laser-chiseled with great precision into the likeness of a small [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] temple: a shrine to the Untold, great destroyer-deity of several old [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] faiths.

The temple has been tumbling through the quiet of space for longer than we have been capable of space-flight - a finding which disturbs more than a few of our researchers.

Despite the unsettling nature of this discovery, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has suggested we search for more objects matching the characteristics of this space temple. [Root.leader.GetHeSheCap] [Root.leader.GetHasHave] prepared a list of likely candidates in nearby star systems.
anomaly.140.a: Perhaps it would be best if we did not.
anomaly.140.c: We will not suffer this heresy.
anomaly.140.c.tooltip: Order the [Root.GetName] to raze the shrine.
anomaly.142.name: Old Gods: Approaching the Benefactress
anomaly.142.desc: The [Root.GetName] has entered the [Root.GetStarName] system. Its crew reports the star is indeed orbited by another object not dissimilar to the shrine of the Untold.
anomaly.143.name: Old Gods: Approaching the Undaunted
anomaly.143.desc: The [Root.GetName] has entered the [Root.GetStarName] system, where its crew report another object in orbit bearing strong resemblance to a shrine to the Untold.
anomaly.144.name: Old Gods: Approaching the Percipient
anomaly.144.desc: Expecting perhaps for a more difficult search when scanning for the shrine to the Percipient, the crew of [Root.GetName] were not ready to see it obviously signposted when entering [Root.GetStarName]. Artificial mineral patterns have been carved around on stellar bodies in the systems pointing to a central location.
anomaly.145.name: What Music They Make
anomaly.145.desc:
The animals of [From.GetName] - predator and prey alike - gather together as night falls and... sing.

The howls, clicks, chirps, roars and hisses seem discordant at first, but underneath lies a recognizable melody. The crew of the [Root.GetName] suggest it's even rather pleasant to hear.

We believe an external influence must have interfered in order to develop this non-sapient choir. We cannot fathom as to why, however we may be able to figure out how they did it.
anomaly.150.name: Below Zro
anomaly.150.desc: [From.GetName] is not only an ice giant, but an ice giant made up of highly unusual solids. There are pockets of Zro trapped in the within reach of the upper levels of the planet's atmosphere.
anomaly.155.name: Illicit Matter
anomaly.155.desc:
The [Root.GetName] finds a disturbing tangle of technology hidden in a deep crater on the asteroid's surface.

Evidently someone has - by rather simplistic means - managed to stabilize a one-way wormhole. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] suggests that the asteroid is an exit point. The other end opens up somewhere in uncharted space some light-years away from a black hole, and small quantities of dark matter are leaking - being siphoned - through the wormhole.

Whoever set this up seems to have abandoned the operation.
anomaly.160.name: Purple Rain
anomaly.160.desc:
Images capturing [From.GetName]'s mesmerizing purple-colored rain, taken by the [Root.GetName]'s surface exploration probes, somehow find their way into the hands of the cultural elite on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

While the discovery is of no scientific value, the evocative imagery of the colorful precipitation sparks a minor renaissance in the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] art world, the positive effects of which shall be felt for years to come.
anomaly.165.name: Old Gods: Shrine to the Benefactress
anomaly.165.desc:
Deciphering the pictograms in the Benefactress' shrine went more smoothly than anticipated. The linguists assigned to the project describe these texts as somehow familiar: "clicking" easily for them, despite the grammar's age and complexity.

They note, however, these written messages allude to some truly obscure themes and contexts. We cannot fully understand their messages until they are combined with other texts associated with this quadrumvirate godhead.
anomaly.166.name: Old Gods: Shrine to the Undaunted
anomaly.166.desc: After days of careful, and at times excruciating effort, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has retrieved the Doctrine of the Undaunted: a humble textile scroll coated with a sturdy plastic polymer. The scroll has been brought back to the [Root.GetName] for further analysis.
anomaly.167.name: Old Gods: Shrine to the Percipient
anomaly.167.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has reported back from the Percipient's shrine.

Its walls are inlaid with logographic script, heavily distorted by layers of a protective lacquer. Initial attempts to decipher this text failed; its grammar is too distinct from other linguistic groups we've encountered. The crew of the [Root.GetName] tried removing the protective lacquer for a clearer view, but to no avail.

The mission was about to be declared a failure when - on the cusp of an irritated outburst - [Root.GetLeaderName] suddenly began to perceive discrete lines of coherent text.

It did not take the crew long to utilize these insights as a codex. Soon they had the ceiling, walls and floor imaged in a spiral pattern: part of a broader picture which we believe may be completed using texts from the other shrines.
anomaly.168.name: Old Gods: Revelation
anomaly.168.desc:
The complete doctrine of the gods - for that is how we believe the recovered texts should be regarded - is as revelatory to us as it is devastating to the fantasies upon which our ancient religions were founded.

When placed within a [Root.GetSpeciesAdj]-centered context, these texts make it clear that we were meant for greatness, guided by the strong hand of a religious leader. We are destined for godhood, but our past is littered with unfulfilled prophecies and sin born of ignorance. Redemption is ephemeral.
anomaly.168.a.tooltip: Knowledge is power. Secret knowledge is secret power.
anomaly.168.c: But what can we learn from this?
anomaly.168.d: We walk in the footsteps of the Divine!
anomaly.170.name: The Exile
anomaly.170.desc:
The readings originate from a small research outpost - which the [Root.Owner.GetName] has no records of establishing or indeed authorizing - on the surface of [FromFrom.GetName]. It is staffed by one [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] scientist, a fairly talented and industrious one if their research on [FromFrom.GetName] is anything to go by. There is a problem with regards to their identity however; we have been unable to match them against official state records, and they refuse to identify themselves save for stating that they are "an exile."

They have expressed an interest in returning to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] and serving the [Root.Owner.GetName] directly, on the condition that the [Root.GetName] immediately depart [FromFrom.GetName] and no [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] ships ever return there.
anomaly.170.a: Out of the question. Search every nook and cranny of that outpost.
anomaly.170.a.tooltip: Detain The Exile and ransack the unauthorized research outpost.
anomaly.170.b: The [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] welcomes the exile back into the fold.
anomaly.170.b.tooltip: The Exile, a Level 3 £ Scientist, joins our empire.
the_exile_background: [Root.GetName] was found in a Research Outpost on the [Root.GetHomeWorldBiome] [Root.GetBackgroundPlanet].
anomaly.171.name: Cold and Empty
anomaly.171.desc:
There is nothing unusual about the research outpost itself. It is little but a temporary shelter erected against the savage elements, allowing surface-level planetary study for a limited time before it wears down and conditions become untenable.

The outpost on [From.From.From.GetName] is nearing the end of its lifespan, but the planet's intense chill has yet to critically degrade the impermanent structure. The equipment - functional, cheap, intended to be abandoned - is well-used, and the local databanks are filled with detailed but ultimately mundane accounts of the planet as well as the simple experiments that were carried out in its harsh environment.

Curiously, no closer examination seems to have been made of the mineral outcropping the outpost's foundations rest on; scans by the [Root.GetName] indicate that the geological formation, a mountain mostly buried under ice, may be partially hollow. More alarmingly, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the sole inhabitant of the outpost, the mysterious "exile," has gone missing and is nowhere to be found.
anomaly.172.name: Down Below
anomaly.172.desc:
There is something unusual about the research outpost on [From.From.From.GetName]. The structure itself is commonplace enough - a temporary shelter erected against the harsh elements, allowing surface-level planetary study for a limited time before it wears down and conditions become untenable - but it is situated on top of a rocky formation poking through the sea of ice that covers the planet.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] found an intricate system of caves and narrow passages leading into this mountain, accessible from inside the research outpost.

In one of the larger cavern-halls, they found the desiccated remains of the outpost's original staff. This contingent of [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] researchers had originally been dispatched elsewhere, but evidently diverted to this uninhabited and hostile planet to set up shop.

Of course, the self-proclaimed "exile" is now nowhere to be found. The [Root.GetName] has launched one of its escape pods, transporting the bodies of the deceased back to [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].
anomaly.175.name: Salty
anomaly.175.desc:
Science ship [Root.GetName] could find no source for the strange readings we detected on [From.From.GetName], which appear to be mere sensor echoes. Nevertheless, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] - a self-proclaimed gourmet chef and history buff - claims to have made a significant discovery there.

A mineral deposit found in several vast patches of surface ice appears closely related to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Stellar Salt: once an essential ingredient in many traditional [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] dishes, long thought depleted on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].

Culinary historians have long suspected that this mineral condiment was not native to our homeworld, and the Science Officer's discovery on [From.From.GetName] lends some credence to this theory. Whether or not the salt actually tastes like the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Stellar Salt of old is ultimately of little consequence: the mere idea of reviving traditional foodstuffs with such closely-matched ingredients is bound to excite our economy and our palates.
anomaly.180.name: Nimkip
anomaly.180.desc:
[From.From.GetName] is populated by tiny, colorful lifeforms that straddle the divide between flora and fauna. They lack any serious evolutionary potential, but their group coordination and great strength relative to their size is impressive.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has taken a shine to them, admitting a particular soft spot for "the red ones."
anomaly.180.b: The [Root.Owner.GetName] will not suffer these creatures to live.
anomaly.180.b.tooltip: A swift extermination campaign carried out by the crew of the [Root.GetName] will ensure that this cutesy alien menace can never rise to threaten the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.180.c: We need to remain a passive observer.
anomaly.180.e.tooltip: The nutrients from these cutesy aliens will feed our [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesSpawnNamePlural].
anomaly.185.name: Limbo
anomaly.185.desc:
The signal originates from the remains of an antenna-like structure. Exploratory probes were dispatched from the [Root.GetName] to the surface to investigate the matter more closely.

What Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] found was a cavernous vault that, while easily pried open, was evidently the last safehouse and refuge of some long-dead race of aliens. While reasonably technologically advanced, it seems they never reached for the stars and perished to some planet-wide natural disaster. The vault is immense, housing thousands upon thousands of black boxes that the [Root.GetName] has determined to be data storage devices.

A Special Project has been prepared to decode their contents.
anomaly.190.name: Moon Projection
anomaly.190.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that they do not trust the sensor readings they've gathered aboard the [Root.GetName], not one bit of it. They are especially suspicious of [From.From.GetName]'s moon, and have outlined a Special Project for further investigation.

Consult the Situation Log for details.
anomaly.191.name: Moon Projected
anomaly.191.desc:
There is a device on the moon, and it is mystifying. At its core lies a ternary computer, seemingly tasked with endlessly calculating new permutations based on a core set of planetary readings. These values are then passed to a powerful comm array, which modulates the data before blasting it at the surface of its parent planet. The raw signal appears nonsensical at a casual glance, but the careful modulation ensures that it becomes nearly indistinguishable from legitimate sensor readings once the signal is reflected from the parent planet's surface and filtered through its atmosphere.

The purpose of this set-up is difficult to deduce, but provides a good opportunity to study alien engineering techniques.
anomaly.191.a.tooltip:
Adds the Projecting Moon modifier to the moon:
£ +6
anomaly.195.name: Misty Shores
anomaly.195.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that large, flexible geometric grids made up of some plastic polymer - clearly artificial in nature - have been placed in the seas of [From.From.GetName].

Visible from orbit, they seem to serve no purpose other than, possibly, an aesthetic one.
anomaly.200.name: Geothermal
anomaly.200.desc:
The measured pounding observed from orbit is the motion of immense and ancient geothermal extractors, breathing their last. Built and then abandoned at some point in the distant past, the vast batteries of disintegrating machinery have been pumping up superheated fluids from the planet's core ever since.

Their storage capacitors are all broken or leaking, but some energy can still be siphoned from them.
anomaly.205.name: Completely Leveled
anomaly.205.desc:
A thorough geological survey of [From.From.GetName] by the [Root.GetName] reveals nothing of interest.

In fact, it is extraordinarily uninteresting - its only defining feature is its lack of defining features. There are depressions and elevations, yes, but on the whole the surface of [From.From.GetName] can be regarded as unnaturally flat. Likewise, the native flora and fauna are strikingly docile and unworthy of attention.
anomaly.205.a.tooltip: All £ Tile Blockers have been cleared from [From.From.GetName].
anomaly.210.name: Dimensional Pocket
anomaly.210.desc:
The [Root.GetName] never made it all the way to [From.From.From.GetName] to study the anomalies surrounding it. The ship, along with Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] and crew, blinked out of existence as it was navigating the debris field.

And then reappeared minutes later.

[Root.GetLeaderName] reports that they found themselves, briefly, in some extra-dimensional space. External viewports revealed that they were surrounded by countless ships of alien design, suspended in a seemingly endless void. Before the crew could get their bearings, the vision abruptly faded and they found themselves back in regular space.

However, roughly half of the crew are missing - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that they may have been selectively trapped, by some unknowable mechanism, in that strange space.
anomaly.211.name: Dimensional Drift
anomaly.211.desc:
The missing members of the [Root.GetName]'s crew, thought lost to the dimensional rift, have reappeared.

They hailed us from aboard an unknown vessel, not entirely dissimilar to our own science ships, idling close to where the [Root.GetName] originally experienced the dimensional disturbance. They claim to remember nothing of their time outside our dimension, aside from a vague awareness of having been away for some time.

They wish for nothing but to return to service under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], and intend to surrender their ship to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities.
anomaly.211.desc.bio:
The missing crew of the [Root.GetName], long presumed lost to the dimensional rift, have inexplicably reappeared.

They hailed us from aboard an unfamiliar organic construct, its form eerily similar to our own science vessels, yet subtly... off. The way it moves, the way it pulses, it follows no known genetic blueprint, as though it were a reflection of our ships seen through a warped, alien mind. It drifted silently near the coordinates where the [Root.GetName] first encountered the disturbance, waiting.

The crew remembers nothing of their time beyond. Only a vague sensation of absence, of having been somewhere else, for far longer than time should allow. And yet, they are unchanged. Or so they claim.

They wish to return to service under Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], and they offer their strange, silent vessel to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities without hesitation. But as we receive their transmission, a deep and unfamiliar resonance hums through the comms. The ship, though still, feels as though it is listening.
anomaly.211.b: The safety of the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] people hinges on their destruction.
anomaly.211.c: The safety of the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] hinges on their destruction.
anomaly.215.name: Cornucopicturesque
anomaly.215.desc:
[From.From.GetName]'s surface is dotted with irregular patches of intense greenery.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is not yet ready to explain the mechanics behind the soil's localized hyperfertility, but asserts that much of the native flora is suitable for [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] consumption with only minimal processing needed.
anomaly.215.desc.serv:
[From.From.GetName]'s surface is dotted with irregular patches of intense greenery.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is not yet ready to explain the mechanics behind the soil's localized hyperfertility, but asserts that much of the native flora is suitable for [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] Bio-Trophy consumption with only minimal processing needed.
anomaly.215.a.tooltip:
Adds the Cornucopia modifier to [From.GetName]:
Additional Food
anomaly.220.name: Mineralistic
anomaly.220.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has provided us with a detailed report on [From.GetName]'s geological riches. Apparently the planet's unique tectonic history has served to concentrate many minerals of interest to the [Root.GetName] near the surface.
anomaly.220.a.tooltip:
Adds the Raw Materials modifier to [From.GetName]:
Additional Minerals
anomaly.225.name: Swirling Shadows
anomaly.225.desc:
Immense, ragged planes of shadow drift across [From.GetName]'s face.

They are cast not by clouds but by sheets of organic material drifting through the upper layers of the atmosphere, hinged - or rather jointed - to allow for a small degree of articulation.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is as yet unwilling to say whether these things are flora or fauna, or what possible purpose, if any, their elaborate shadow-casting might serve.
anomaly.225.a.tooltip:
Adds the Shadow Play modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ +4
anomaly.230.name: Grimacing
anomaly.230.desc.v1:
The very geological structure of [From.GetName] is indeed in flux, driven by what Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] assures us is a tectonic process as fascinating as it is esoteric. What is of more interest to the [Root.Owner.GetName] is that we may be able to strategically halt the planet's ceaseless, chaotic self-transformation. In short, a near-instant terraforming of the planet into something slightly - if not entirely - more habitable, is theoretically possible.

[Root.GetLeaderName] estimates that an additional 200 Energy Credits will be needed to power a thorough mapping of planetary activity and determine the validity of what the Science Officer has termed "a surgical terraforming strike." Of course, we can always choose to terraform it using existing technologies at a later date.
anomaly.230.desc.v2:
The very geological structure of [From.GetName] is indeed in flux, driven by what Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] assures us is a tectonic process as fascinating as it is esoteric. What is of more interest to the [Root.Owner.GetName] is that we may be able to strategically halt the planet's ceaseless, chaotic self-transformation. In short, a near-instant stabilization of the planet into something slightly - if not entirely - more habitable, is theoretically possible.

[Root.GetLeaderName] estimates that an additional 200 Energy Credits will be needed to power a thorough mapping of planetary activity and determine the validity of what the Science Officer has termed "a surgical terraforming strike." Actual terraforming lies beyond our grasp at present, so this is an exciting opportunity.
anomaly.230.b.tooltip: Spend Energy Credits to attempt to stabilize the planet in a more favorable state, with roughly a 50% chance of success.
anomaly.230.c: We have no credits to spend on vague hypotheses.
anomaly.231.name: Tactical Terraforming
anomaly.231.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that [From.From.GetName] can indeed be terraformed! A narrow window of opportunity is expected to open shortly, as the planet enters a particularly unstable phase of its cycle lasting a couple of months. [Root.GetLeaderName] believes that miniaturized explosive charges delivered to the planet's crust and strategic irradiation of the atmosphere during this time will halt [From.From.GetName]'s tumultuous changes and stabilize it in a form somewhat more suitable for sustaining life.

A Special Project has been issued, but we do not have much time.
anomaly.232.name: Tactical Terraforming Failed
anomaly.232.desc: The crew of the [Root.GetName] are disappointed to report that the window of opportunity for terraforming [From.From.GetName] has closed, despite their best efforts to identify it in time. Another opportunity is unlikely to arise for another few centuries.
anomaly.233.name: Tactical Terraforming Successful
anomaly.233.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is proud to report that [From.From.GetName] can now be re-classified as an Arid rather than Barren planet. This grand experiment has greatly enriched the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] sciences.
anomaly.233.desc.mach: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is proud to report that [From.From.GetName] can now be re-classified as a Machine planet rather than Barren planet. This grand experiment has greatly enriched the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] sciences.
anomaly.235.name: Lightshow
anomaly.235.desc.v1:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the luminous waves coursing through the ice that blankets [From.GetName] are of alien origin.

Some ancient battle has deposited scattered wreckage from an alien fighter on the frozen planet, and only the exposed core of its main weapons remains intact. It seems this alien race used lasers similar to the ones currently in use by [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] fleets, and the fizzling innards periodically discharge low-powered beams into the ice of [From.GetName]. The planet's harsh climate prevents the lasers from actually melting the ice, allowing the chilly matrix to act as a brilliant prism.
anomaly.235.desc.v2:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the luminous waves coursing through the ice that blankets [From.GetName] are of alien origin.

Some ancient battle has deposited scattered wreckage from an alien fighter on the frozen planet, and only the exposed core of its main weapons remains intact. It seems this alien race used lasers somewhat more advanced than the ones currently in use by [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] fleets, and the fizzling innards periodically discharge low-powered lasers into the ice of [From.GetName]. The planet's harsh climate prevents the lasers from actually melting the ice, allowing the chilly matrix to act as a brilliant prism.
anomaly.240.name: Deceptive Giant
anomaly.240.desc:
What we had assumed was an abnormally small gas giant is, in fact, not.

Beneath a deceptive cover of thick dust swirling in the upper atmosphere lies a regular planet. A barren planet, but a planet nonetheless.

This has proven quite embarrassing to the astronomical community on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName].
anomaly.240.a.tooltip: [From.GetName]: Revealed to be a Barren planet.
anomaly.245.name: Eden Overrun
anomaly.245.desc:
[From.GetName] is indeed teeming with life.

Dangerous life.

While ripe for colonization, the crew of the [Root.GetName] warn that we are likely to run into problems with the local wildlife.
anomaly.250.name: A Whiff of Something
anomaly.250.desc:
The [Root.GetName] has recovered an elongated metal box from the surface of [From.GetName]. Clusters of small perforations on five sides lead Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] to believe it is not a container, but some sort of aerosol dispersal device. Initial tests seem to confirm their suspicions as trace aromatics still emanate from the object.

A Special Project has been issued to confirm whether this might be an information-carrying device constructed by some alien race communicating primarily through the secretion and reception of atmosphere-borne chemical compounds; smells.
anomaly.251.name: A Whiff of Something
anomaly.251.desc:
The box is indeed a document, of a sort. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] admits that they had been hoping for a historical record or some other kind of codex significant to whatever culture left it behind, but they were disappointed.

The true nature of the aromatic box seems to be a collection of fairly short narratives which, going by the rapid changes in odor towards the end of each sequence, are intended to surprise or be interpreted as comedic. The techniques used to store and reproduce specific smells is of some interest, but the tales it tells are not.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] are left with the uncomfortable feeling that they have unwittingly become intimately familiar with what certain gaseous byproducts of alien digestion smell like. However, [Root.GetLeaderName] is unwilling to speculate as to why the box was dumped on this frozen hellscape of a planet.
anomaly.255.name: Apocalypse Past
anomaly.255.desc:
[From.GetName] was once home to a race of reasonably intelligent beings who destroyed themselves when they were seemingly only decades away from space flight. The planet has recovered from what must have been immense acts of senseless destruction, but it still bears very visible scars.

One of the few remaining ruins on the surface holds a reasonably well-preserved stone monolith inscribed with a message, quickly decoded by [Root.GetLeaderName]. It is a warning, from the last of the extinct species to whoever they believed would arise after their passing. It was the development of an "ultimate weapon" that was their downfall; some quirk in the psychology of this species evidently rendered deterrence through mutually assured destruction impossible.

Survivors, before dying of unknown causes soon after, hid this weaponry deep underground as destroying them was difficult, and left this message dissuade us from going looking for them.
anomaly.256.name: An Interesting Find
anomaly.256.desc:
It seems the people of this planet were experimenting only with what we would consider to be fairly basic weapons technologies.

The havoc they wrought is more a testament to their incredible, genocidal tenacity than it is to the power of their weaponry.
anomaly.256.b: None of this is of any use to the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.257.name: A Brutal Find
anomaly.257.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] remarks that the previous inhabitants of this place were right to hide these weapons, recovered from a cave beneath the ruins, away. They build on the same basic principles as weapons already in use in the [Root.Owner.GetName], but are far more advanced. These technologies are sure to be a boon to the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] military machine.
anomaly.257.a: What? We already possess this technology.
anomaly.258.name: Empty-handed
anomaly.258.desc: The search proves fruitless. Whatever these mystical weapons were, they are now gone.
anomaly.260.name: Mineral Factorial
anomaly.260.desc:
The [Root.GetName] has found an alien structure on [From.GetName]. It seems to be the only one of its kind on the planet - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that all other xenoarchitectural traces may have been moved off-world, with this sole building left behind for reasons unknown.

It is a processing plant working the planet's abundant mineral resources, and preliminary scans by the [Root.GetName] indicate that it can be reactivated with relative ease.
anomaly.265.name: Alien Drag Racing
anomaly.265.desc:
The crater on [From.GetName] exhibits long, irregular marks imprinted into the relatively soft upper layers of the asteroid. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has recovered some interesting unexpected wreckage from the edges of the depression; wheeled vehicles, seemingly personal transports rather than research craft.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] speculate that the crater may once have been used for sport, with some alien species pitting their personal locomotion devices against each other in tests of mechanical strength or speed in near-zero-G.
anomaly.265.a.tooltip:
Adds the Skid Marks modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ +6
anomaly.270.name: Fender Bender
anomaly.270.desc:
While the crater in question was most likely the result of a regular meteorite impact, the complex patterns in the resulting depression originated at a later time.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] argues that these surface-level patterns are not the result of an impact but a collision, one between asteroid [From.GetName] and some unspecified orbital installation or ship of alien make.
anomaly.270.a.tooltip:
Adds the Circuits in the Dust modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ +3
anomaly.275.name: Abandoned Thrusting
anomaly.275.desc:
In the center of a particularly large crater on [From.GetName] lies a cluster of metal shapes, doubtlessly of alien origin.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is convinced that they are massive, planetoid-mountable propulsion devices, intended to push [From.GetName] from its orbit for purposes and destinations unknown. The [Root.GetName] is on standby, its crew ready to begin disassembly and analysis of the alleged propulsion systems with the hopes of improving our own thruster technology.
anomaly.280.name: Colonial Failure
anomaly.280.desc:
There was an alien colony on [From.GetName] once, or at least an early attempt at one. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the effort was obviously premature, the ramshackle structures never standing a chance against the hostile climate of [From.GetName].

Not wanting to leave empty-handed, the [Root.GetName] has recovered a defunct atmospheric filtration unit that may be of some interest.
anomaly.280.a: We can learn from their mistakes.
anomaly.280.c: The [Root.Owner.GetName] would never make such mistakes.
anomaly.285.name: Unusual Tectonics
anomaly.285.desc:
What the [Root.GetName] found on [From.GetName] were not buildings, but surprisingly regular mineral outcroppings. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] asserts that these angular blocks of rock are the product of interactions between tectonic plates, their shapes the result of the unusual tectonophysics inherent in the planet's crust.

The perfect angularity of these thrust faults implies a possibility of aliens tampering with [From.GetName]'s crust at some point in the past.
anomaly.285.a.tooltip:
Adds the Unusual Tectonics modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ +2
£ +2
anomaly.290.name: Rock Potential
anomaly.290.desc:
[From.GetName] is exceptionally rich in minerals.

Minerals that are, unfortunately, of no use to us. However, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] believes the many elements in the crust of [From.GetName] can be transformed into potentially more useful forms through positron bombardment.

The [Root.GetName] has requests that the [Root.Owner.GetName] set aside 1000 Energy Credits for the purposes of this project.
anomaly.290.b: Very well, ready the positron charges.
anomaly.292.desc: The crew of the [Root.GetName] are pleased to report that the experiment was a success, and a significant number of dense mineral veins on [From.From.GetName] have been transmuted into usable resources.
anomaly.295.name: Up is Down
anomaly.295.desc:
As the [Root.GetName] passed through the asteroid belt on its way to [From.GetName], Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reported that the ship experienced a number of sudden gravitational shifts. Ever curious, [Root.GetLeaderName] dispatched a number of probes to scan the debris field to discern the cause.

It turns out that the culprit is a number of gravity generators of old, alien make. Sputtering on dying energy sources and with their polarities inverted, they occasionally spew reverse-gravity into the void, though not with enough force to cause any serious harm. Not anymore.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] theorizes that the generators once provided artificial gravity for a large asteroid in the belt, but some malfunction eventually tore the rock apart.
anomaly.3000.name: Careless Pawing
anomaly.3000.desc:
According to a report from the crew of the [Root.GetName], their mission was a failure. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] allegedly took manual control of the probe sent to retrieve a sample from the cluster, resulting in a collision between drone and mineral cluster that, while mild, resulted in the mineral cluster breaking apart completely.

The crew is careful to note that the experience has left Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] somewhat shaken, and the mineral shards should still be of some value.
anomaly.3000.a: Its parts are equal to the sum of its parts.
anomaly.3005.name: Gilded Cage
anomaly.3005.desc:
The mineral construct is, for lack of a better term, a room.

Made out of the same type of minerals in common use in the [Root.Owner.GetName], the construct is a hollow icosidodecahedron. Resonance scans indicate that it is mostly hollow, and was likely inhabited at some point in time. Unlike its pristine exterior, the interior is in complete disarray, possibly the result of an intentional act of sabotage.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that this makes it difficult to learn anything of value from the construct's insides, but stresses that the engineering techniques involved in creating the outer shell, eminently capable of withstanding the stresses of deep space, must have been tremendously advanced.
anomaly.3010.name: Crystal Codex
anomaly.3010.desc:
The mineral cluster is a holographic record, multi-sided, many-edged, and translucent. It remains secure in the [Root.GetName]'s tractor beam, but our experts will need some time to decode its contents.

A Special Project has been issued to expedite this process.
anomaly.3010.a: Nothing good would come of it.
anomaly.3012.desc: The holographic data documents the terms and conditions for a trilateral trade treaty between three major alien powers that once dominated this quadrant of the galaxy. Context eludes us and the details are meaningless, but Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] feels that this find will prove invaluable to improving our own ability to communicate with alien forces.
anomaly.3015.name: Alien Barracks
anomaly.3015.desc:
The silhouettes discernible from orbit are indeed buildings, and closer inspection reveal them to be of an obvious martial nature. While abandoned for some time - though very recently on a galactic timescale - Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] believes that secrets of alien tactics may yet be exhumed from beneath the dust that covers the decaying barracks and looted armories.

A Special Project may be issued to study the remains.
anomaly.3015.b.pacifist: That this outpost is dead and buried speaks volumes.
anomaly.3017.name: Alien Barracks
anomaly.3017.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName]'s thorough xeno-historical analysis of the military installation on [From.From.GetName] has yielded few tangible results. The base was constructed before the planet turned completely barren, but it is unclear if its current inhospitality is the result of armed conflict or some more peaceful or even natural process.

What can be deduced of their strategies and tactics in armed conflict does not seem to have been far in advance of our own.

On the upside, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] claims to have drawn much inspiration from the alien remnants.
anomaly.3020.name: Checkered
anomaly.3020.desc:
The unique topology of [From.GetName] neatly divides the planet into innumerable distinct biomes, micro-climates that interact only in subtle ways seemingly engineered to sustain neighboring climes. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] strongly suspects advanced terraforming techniques at work, but few clues remain regarding the process itself.

Its effects, however, remain plainly visible to [Root.GetLeaderName] and the [Root.GetName]'s crew.
anomaly.3025.name: Ancient Automata
anomaly.3025.desc:
One of the major areas of extreme verdancy on [From.GetName] is centered on an overgrown alien structure. Initially thought ruined, closer observations by the [Root.GetName] reveal that the building has mostly survived the crushing embrace of the planet's flora.

A Special Project has been issued to find a way into the structure.
anomaly.3027.desc:
The overgrown structure - an alien mineral processing plant - on [From.From.GetName] was, prior to its abandonment in the distant past, mostly automated. Husks of artificial workers litter the floor, their organic components - for their bodies were largely of a biological nature, held upright by polymer endoskeletons - long since rotted away.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] speculates that it is the organic remains of these automatons that, soon liquefied and drained into the ground, provided an intense boost to soil nutrition and allowed the native flora to grow both abundant and resilient.

The plant can be reactivated but the automatons, fascinating as they may be to [Root.GetLeaderName], will never walk its halls again.
anomaly.3030.name: Hard Shoulder
anomaly.3030.desc:
There is a ship idling on the plains of [From.GetName], its sensors reacting to the [Root.GetName] in orbit around the planet.

The [Root.GetName]'s crew have been unable to confirm exactly when the craft was abandoned - for it is abandoned - or who left it there, or where they are now. According to Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], remotely activating the lightly armed ship would be trivial, should we wish to add it to our fleets.
anomaly.3030.a: No one will miss it, surely.
anomaly.3030.b.phobe: We don't know whence it came or where it is going. Dismantle it.
anomaly.3035.name: Taking Stock
anomaly.3035.desc.carefree:
The desert [From.GetPlanetMoon] [From.GetName] turned out to be rather unremarkable.

While the crew monitored silent instruments, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] was idly eyeing the [Root.GetName]'s energy reserves. According to their report the [Root.GetName] was issued less than the standard amount of energy when it last left port, but is more likely that [Root.GetLeaderName]'s carefree approach to resource management is to blame for the deficit.

Regardless, the ship does need additional Energy Credits.
anomaly.3035.desc.meticulous:
The desert [From.GetPlanetMoon] [From.GetName] turned out to be rather unremarkable.

While the crew monitored silent instruments, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] was conscientiously taking inventory of the [Root.GetName]'s energy reserves. According to their report the [Root.GetName] was issued more than the standard amount of energy when it last left port, probably due to some clerical error.

[Root.Leader.GetName] has volunteered to return the excess to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] authorities.
anomaly.3040.name: Pirate Exiles
anomaly.3040.desc:
What was thought to be a cluster of minerals are the metal hulls of two alien corvettes, stealthily drifting through the asteroid belt.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] established contact, and the two ships are crewed by alleged former pirates, now cast out from their robber-clan. They have heard whispers that [Root.Owner.GetRulerTitle] [Root.Owner.GetRulerName] of the [Root.Owner.GetName] is a champion of the people, and seek asylum.
anomaly.3040.desc.fallback:
What was thought to be a cluster of minerals are the metal hulls of two alien corvettes, stealthily drifting through the asteroid belt.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] established contact, and the two ships are crewed by alleged former pirates, now cast out from their robber-clan. Curiously, they believe that we will be well-disposed towards them, and are seeking asylum.
anomaly.3040.a.tooltip: Enlist the exiled pirates and gain two Corvette-class ships.
anomaly.3040.b: We do not need their services. Take what they have but their lives.
anomaly.3040.c: The [Root.Owner.GetName] will not suffer the existence of their kind.
anomaly.3040.d: We must deny their asylum claim.
anomaly.3050.name: Grinding Lattice
anomaly.3050.desc:
[From.GetName] is crisscrossed by overlapping mineral-composite bands that are elevated above the harsh surface by tall, flexible pylons. Constantly agitated by atmospheric winds, these pylons sway and the overlapping bands rub together to produce sonic waves at what are - to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] - inaudible frequencies.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports some difficulty in isolating this audio from the natural background noise of the planet, but notes that the mineral bands could - should we so choose - be broken down and efficiently recycled by the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.3050.a: Isolate and study the alien sounds.
anomaly.3050.b: Make preparations for salvaging the mineral bands.
anomaly.3055.name: Wooden Hegemony
anomaly.3055.desc:
[From.GetName] is a tropical planet with a thriving biosphere. A close analysis of surface flora reveals an unexpected lack of diversity, as one particular family of tall trees dominate the ecosystem.

Though not harmful in and of themselves, their monocultural hegemony appears to have a detrimental effect on the survivability of the planet's small animals, and it would be difficult to efficiently cultivate food crops on the surface should colonization ever be attempted.

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName], a xeno-biologist of some repute, has put together a plan for re-balancing this alien biosphere.
anomaly.3055.a.tooltip:
Adds the Unbalanced Ecosystem modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ -20%
anomaly.3055.b.tooltip:
Adds the Unbalanced Ecosystem modifier to [From.GetName]:
£ -20%
anomaly.3056.desc: Balance has been restored - or perhaps achieved for the first time - as large swathes of the dominant perennials have been rendered infertile by targeted radiation emissions from the [Root.GetName]. Additional specimens have been reduced to ash to further hasten the arrival of a truer equilibrium.
anomaly.3057.desc:
The inelegant elimination of wide swathes of the dominant trees on [From.From.GetName] have had unintended consequences.

The small animals that previously suffered under the perennial tyranny of the trees are growing both more plentiful and more aggressive - some would say savage. The isolated ashen fields that used to be home to lush forests now play host to heated territory battles.
anomaly.3057.a: Perhaps we should have known better than to meddle.
anomaly.3060.name: Head in the Sand
anomaly.3060.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the waves seen rippling across the sandy seas of [From.GetName] are, bizarrely enough, the result of active ship thrusters.

An alien vessel lies buried in the sand nose-down, its sputtering propulsion systems weakly agitating the dunes above. It appears to have been down there for some time, slowly driving itself deeper into the desert dunes. The [Root.GetName] lacks the means to excavate the struggling ship, and [Root.GetLeaderName] recommends sending a military vessel to [From.GetName] to unearth it.
anomaly.3060.b: We will not take the obvious bait.
anomaly.3060.c: If there are any organics left they will be terminated.
anomaly.3061.desc:
The [Root.GetFleetName] eventually succeeds in raising the submerged alien vessel.

It is empty. Almost stripped bare, in fact.

Its crew must have abandoned ship before it was left to burrow into the particulate surface of [From.From.GetName], and they took most of the ship's non-critical internals with them. The engineers of the [Root.GetFleetName] have managed to essentially hotwire the vessel, and have replenished its dwindling energy stores.
anomaly.3061.a: A fresh commission for the [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] fleet.
anomaly.3062.desc: The [Root.GetFleetName]'s high-tensile wires eventually managed to raise the submerged alien vessel, only to be met by the recognizable whirring of weapons systems powering up!
anomaly.3063.desc:
The salvage attempt failed. The high-tensile tethers that the [Root.GetFleetName] had wrapped around the burrowing ship effortlessly sliced through the vessel's corroded hull as raising was attempted.

The individual pieces were then relatively easy to retrieve, but the whole thing is reduced to scrap.
anomaly.3065.name: Illicit Communications
anomaly.3065.desc:
A cobbled-together comms repeater has been inexpertly strapped to [From.GetName].

Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is confident that this is part of a relay network for pirate communications. Initial analysis indicates that the messages relayed are not of a particularly strategically sensitive nature, but rather private inter-ship communications between individual crewmembers.
anomaly.3065.a: Perhaps we can learn something about life in deep space.
anomaly.3065.b: Perhaps we can learn something useful about life in deep space.
anomaly.3070.name: Down the Drain
anomaly.3070.desc:
The readings originate from a small metal pod; Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has determined it to be a lifeboat of ancient and alien make.
