The Crystalline Entities are capable of violently discharging at specific target, and unfortunately seem to prefer to do so rather than let foreign entities pass by unscathed.
story.205.desc.spiri:
The Crystalline Entities - the name itself a compromise between rival factions of xeno-biologists and xeno-geologists on [Root.Capital.GetName] - exist beyond such base concepts as life, and death. Some of the less imaginative purveyors of wisdom on [Root.Capital.GetName] call them "silicate-animate matter," claiming that the specimens, while unusual, are still subject to the same supposed unfeeling natural laws that some claim govern us all.

At any rate, the Crystalline Entities are solitary, majestic beings. Each individual Crystal Sovereign is rarely accompanied by more than two subservient entities, a Sentinel and a smaller Crystal Cohort. The Entities do not mate, nor do any of them appear older or younger than others - they are all sprung from some immaculate, past eon. The shifts in hue between individual Sovereigns that have been observed seem to be related to their latent internal charge - which can be violently unleashed - and it appears as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal.
story.205.desc.gesta:
The Crystalline Entities are probably alive.

A perhaps more descriptive name for them is "silicate-animate matter," as they have little in common with biological or traditionally artificial life.

The Entities do not seem to mate, and we have yet to observe any Crystals that are recognizably older or younger than others. Contrary to an early hypothesis, the shifts in hue between individual Crystalline Entities seem to be related not to their age but to their latent internal charge - which can be violently unleashed - and it appear as if though sporadic fluctuations in this charge alter the refractive properties of the Crystal.
story.205.a: This knowledge will surely be a great boon to the sciences.
story.205.a.tooltip:
Adds the Prismatic Lenses modifier to our Empire:
£ +10%
story.205.b: We will find some use for this information.
story.205.b.tooltip:
Adds the Crystal Sonar modifier to our Empire:
Spend £ 30 Energy to Instantly Survey any Crystalline Entity system when entered.
story.210.name: Crystalline Entity Shattered
story.210.desc.milit:
The Crystalline Entities - a new designation better reflecting their apparent status as silicate yet animate matter - are tough and aggressive adversaries.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. This is fortunate, as our fleets will need to engage with several more specimens if we are to learn anything about these enigmatic prisms. What we do know is that changes, in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power that drives their weapon-like discharge, are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities in different colors, and should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.
story.210.desc.mater:
The Crystalline Entities - re-designated as such once it became clear they have more in common with animals than precious minerals - are aggressive and outright hostile to [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. Additionally, changes in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power - that drives their weapon-like discharge - are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities in different colors, and should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

We are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more about them. Despite our inability to easily exploit them as a natural resource, the [Root.GetName] is, of course, unwilling to just walk away empty-handed.
story.210.desc:
The Crystalline Entities - informally re-named after it became obvious that the crystals' behavior is actual behavior and not some obscure mineralogical process - are aggressive and outright hostile to [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. As peaceful interaction seems impossible at present, we are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more about them.
story.210.desc.gesta:
The Crystalline Entities are aggressive and outright hostile to us and our ships. Perhaps they perceive our fleets as Metallic Entities, to be ousted from Crystal territory by any means necessary.

Our engagements have allowed us to pinpoint structural weaknesses that should, theoretically, be shared among all individual Crystalline Entities. Additionally, changes in levels of apparent aggression and the internal generation of power - which drives their weapon-like discharge - are accompanied by shifts in how the crystals break light.

In essence, it is likely that [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships will eventually encounter Crystalline Entities of different colors, and we should be prepared for differences in behavior and combat capabilities.

As peaceful interaction seems impossible at present, we are left with little choice but to continue to engage the Crystalline Entities in direct combat if we wish to learn more.
story.215.name: Crystalline Entities Crushed
story.215.desc.milit:
The fleets of the [Root.GetName] leave crushed crystal in their wake wherever they go.

The Crystalline Entities' true nature is likely to forever remain a mystery to us, but what does it matter?

[Root.GetSpeciesAdj] forces are now exceptionally skilled at annihilating the prisms, and we have, over the course of the campaign, found ways to tune up our weaponry.
story.215.desc.mater:
After the destruction of several crystal specimens and collection of thousands of samples, [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] engineers have finally devised a cost-effective process for refining the remains of Crystalline Entities into usable materials.

Whether this will actually offset the cost of engaging with the crystals and their weaponized emissions remains to be seen, but it is a victory for industry nonetheless.
story.215.desc:
Despite frequent clashes, the Crystalline Entities remain as enigmatic as ever. They do not seem to mate, and it is difficult to imagine some kind of vast, spacer geode naturally producing the things.

We have found some uses for the shards of destroyed Crystalline Entities, but fear that some things, such as the truth of their actual nature, simply are fundamentally unknowable.
story.215.desc.gesta:
Despite frequent clashes, the Crystalline Entities remain as enigmatic as ever. They do not seem to mate, and it is difficult to imagine some kind of vast, spacer geode naturally producing the things.

We have found some uses for the shards of destroyed Crystalline Entities but fear that some things, such as the truth of their actual nature, simply are fundamentally unknowable.
story.215.b.mater: We must make the most out of what the universe brings.
story.215.b.mater.tooltip: Gives access to the Greater Crystal Bounty empire Edict.
story.215.c.tooltip: Gives access to the Crystal Bounty empire Edict.
story.219.name: Crystal Sonar
story.219.desc:
The [From.GetFleetName] has encountered Crystalline Entities in the [From.From.GetName] system.

Using some stored Energy, our ships can generate an intense but harmless high-frequency blast to fire at the Crystalline Entities. The Entities act as prisms and resonators, breaking up the pulse and scattering it across the star system, and the waves reflected from planetary bodies are picked up by our ship sensors.

The whole system surveyed, in an instant.
story.219.a.tooltip: Spend £ -30 Energy Credits to instantly Survey the [From.From.GetName] system.
story.219.c: We do not have the resources to spare.
story.220.name: Crystal Ball
story.220.desc.hostile:
The [Root.GetName] reports a significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. There is little to indicate whether this is an ancestral home of the creatures, but never before have this many crystalline entities been observed in one system at once.

Initial readings point to the unusual crystal construct in the system being of some interest, should we be able to... disassemble it.
story.220.desc.nonhostile:
The [Root.GetName] reports a significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. Evidently some kind of den - or at least a hub of crystalline activity, such as it is - [From.GetName] is home to a crystal construct unlike any previously encountered.

This construct exhibits several properties associated with the crystalline entities, but greatly exaggerated.
story.220.desc.gesta:
We see significant crystalline presence in the [From.GetName] system. Evidently some kind of den - or at least a hub of crystalline activity, such as it is - [From.GetName] is home to a crystal construct unlike any previously encountered.

This construct exhibits several properties associated with the crystalline entities, but greatly exaggerated.
story.221.name: Scried
story.221.desc:
A xenoscience department on [Root.Capital.GetName] reports that they have concluded their remote study of the crystalline construct.

Again, the sheer lack of observable behavior exhibited by these entities makes it difficult to draw any solid conclusions. However, their physiological properties continue to intrigue. The study of the construct has allowed our xenobiologists, in close cooperation with our materials engineers, to begin to emulate the advanced reconstructive properties observed in the crystalline construct.
story.221.desc.gesta:
We have concluded our remote study of the crystalline construct.

The sheer lack of observable behavior exhibited by these entities makes it difficult to draw any solid conclusions. However, their physiological properties continue to intrigue, and we can now begin to emulate the advanced reconstructive properties observed in the crystalline construct.
story.223.name: Scrying Interrupted
story.223.desc: A xenoscience department on [Root.Capital.GetName] reports that the crystalline construct observed in a distant system has been destroyed, and remote study is no longer possible.
story.223.desc.gesta: The crystalline construct observed in a distant system has been destroyed, and remote study is no longer possible.
story.223.a.tooltip: The Crystalline Construct Special Project is canceled.
story.301.name: Ancient Mining Drones
story.301.desc.pacif:
Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment.

The drones seem to lack any diplomatic comms protocols - at least any decipherable by the [Root.Owner.GetName] - and react with hostility to [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] ships entering the system.

Their presence in the [Root.System.GetName] system is intriguing, and we should attempt to learn more about them.
story.301.desc.mater:
Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment. Their purpose is obvious enough - mining - but who it is that tasked them is not immediately apparent. What is obvious is that no shipment of minerals has been retrieved from this system in hundreds, if not thousands of years.

They may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch by the [Root.Owner.GetName].
story.301.desc:
Reports of deep-space drones in certain systems have been investigated. The drones appear to be the workers and custodians of an autonomous orbital mining operation, established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves, judging by the state of the processing equipment. The drones possess powerful mining lasers and make obviously threatening, if not outright hostile, overtures toward [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] vessels when approached.

They may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch by the [Root.Owner.GetName].
story.301.desc.gesta:
The deep-space drones we have encountered appear to be the workers and custodians of autonomous orbital mining operations. Judging by the state of the processing equipment, these sites were established millennia ago and then soon abandoned by all but the drones themselves. The drones possess powerful mining lasers and make obviously threatening, if not outright hostile, overtures toward us when approached.

They may only be old drones, but they should be kept under close watch.
story.301.b: Let us see what they are made of - take them apart.
story.305.name: Mining Drone Work Ethic
story.305.desc.pacif:
When not posturing with their mining lasers aimed at [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] ships, the drones appear steadfast and dumbly hard-working, hacking away at mineral-poor asteroids for want of something better to do.

What is more interesting is that the drones are not completely silent, contrary to earlier assumptions. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.
story.305.desc.mater:
The drones are remarkably efficient at squeezing ever-diminishing returns from rocks [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] miners would have soon discarded, deemed exhausted of all worthwhile mineral content. Our top engineers are working on adapting the drones' methodology for use in the [Root.GetName]'s Mining Networks and Stations which should improve efficiency, effectively lessening energy expenditure.

Of lesser import is the fact that the drones are not completely silent, contrary to previous assumptions. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.
story.305.desc:
The drones and their tireless, endless work of extracting ever-diminishing resources from their local planetoids make for a somewhat dull, but nevertheless informative subject of study. In fact, Mining Networks on [Root.Capital.GetName] could stand to learn a thing or two about maximizing mineral extraction rates while conserving energy.

Additionally, we have found that the drones are not completely silent. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. If there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery for another time.
story.305.desc.gesta:
The drones and their tireless, endless work of extracting ever-diminishing resources from their local planetoids make for a somewhat dull, but nevertheless informative subject of study. In fact, we could stand to learn a thing or two about maximizing mineral extraction rates while conserving energy.

Additionally, we have found that the drones are not completely silent. They emit signal pings, though extremely infrequently and at a wavelength hard to isolate from background noise. Whether there is anyone left to receive these pings may be a mystery better left for another time.
story.305.b: Let us find out how they evaluate mining sites.
story.310.name: Mining Drone Disassembly
story.310.desc.mater:
The mining drones were destroyed in a heated battle with [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] vessels. As luck would have it, their energy cells are by far the sturdiest component used in their construction, and some were recovered by our ships. The technology behind these cells is beyond us at present, but initial tests show we are quite capable of converting their output to Energy Credits.

As the final energy cell bled out, the engineers handling the test noticed a dip in background radiation. It would appear that the drones are not silent, but have been sporadically broadcasting on unusual frequencies since we first encountered them, possibly ever since they were first deployed. It is unlikely that there is anyone left to receive these transmissions.

At any rate, the drones could prove to be a potent but limited source of energy, should we be able to find and disable them efficiently enough.

story.310.a.tooltip: Gives access to the Drone Bounty empire Edict.
story.320.name: Deposits Surveyed
story.320.desc: All high-mineral deposits discovered by the reverse-engineered Ancient Mining Drone evaluation algorithms have been surveyed.
story.330.name: Ancient Mineral Processing Hub
story.330.desc: The [Root.GetName] has encountered a significant Ancient Mining Drone presence in the [From.GetName] system. It appears to be a major mining and mineral processing hub, perhaps the last of its kind in the galaxy.
story.330.desc.gesta: We have encountered a significant Ancient Mining Drone presence in the [From.GetName] system. It appears to be a major mining and mineral processing hub, perhaps the last of its kind in the galaxy.
story.330.b: Let us see what we can learn from it.
story.331.name: Processing Observed
story.331.desc: Leaving the ancient mining drone mineral processing hub undisturbed was, ultimately, a wise decision. By observing its monotonous rhythms over an extended period of time, we have been able to identify several systemic techniques in its automated handling of raw materials that surpass our own.
story.331.desc.gesta: Leaving the ancient mining drone mineral processing hub undisturbed was, ultimately, a wise decision. By observing its monotonous rhythms over an extended period of time, we have been able to identify several systemic techniques in its automated handling of raw materials that surpass our own.
story.331.a: Then we make these techniques ours.
story.333.name: Mining Drone Base Destroyed
story.333.desc: We have received reports that the mineral processing hub observed in the [location_planet.GetStarName] system has been destroyed. Its significant stores of raw and processed minerals were jettisoned and have made planetfall on [location_planet.GetName] in the local asteroid belt.
story.333.desc.gesta: The mineral processing hub we observed in the [location_planet.GetStarName] system has been destroyed. Its significant stores of raw and processed minerals were jettisoned and have made planetfall on [location_planet.GetName] in the local asteroid belt.
story.333.a.tooltip:
The Automated Processing Hub Special Project is canceled.
[location_planet.GetName] is now richer in minerals.
story.401.name: Void Clouds
story.401.desc.spiri:
"A cloud," reads the awed report, collated from multiple sources. "Like a cloud of luminous star-stuff, billowing in the dark." The report goes on to refer to the phenomenon, somewhat poetically, as a "void cloud."

It is evident to the priesthoods of the [Root.Owner.GetName] that these clouds are heralds animated by some higher will. Exactly who or what this will belongs is the subject of heated debate, and is likely to remain so for the foreseeable future. Until such time as the Void Cloud's true nature can be ascertained, it would perhaps be prudent to treat the immense power evident in its roiling motion with some caution.
story.401.desc:
An investigation into a peculiar cluster of debris and space-dust previously dubbed [This.ContactCountry.GetName] has yielded surprising results; it is a particulate cloud bristling with a powerful charge of unknown origin that has no business exhibiting simple reflexive actions, let alone movements with purpose.

And yet it does.

There is something undeniably ominous about the hazy subject of the relayed video feeds. Perhaps there are things in the universe we should not tangle with.
story.401.desc.gesta:
Our investigation into the peculiar cluster of debris and space-dust with the designation [This.ContactCountry.GetName] has yielded surprising results: it is a particulate cloud bristling with a powerful charge of unknown origin. It has no business exhibiting simple reflexive actions, let alone movements with purpose.

And yet it does.

There is something undeniably ominous about the hazy subject of the relayed video feeds. Perhaps there are things in the universe we should not tangle with.
story.401.a.spiri: Conduit for the divine or not, it must be studied.
story.401.b.spiri: We leave the matter in the capable hands of our commanders.
story.401.c: Let us watch, but not interfere with it.
story.401.d: We leave the matter in the capable hands of our commanders.
story.405.name: Void Unclouded
story.405.desc.spiri:
The Void Clouds are stewards of the cosmos. Once [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] astronomers knew what to look for, they found traces of the Void Clouds everywhere.

Formed at the dawn of creation, they stood watch as stars were lit and young planets formed. Now they drift, quasi-conscious agglomerations of inanimate matter from the earliest hours of time itself, afloat between dying stars and breaking worlds.

They are a constant reminder that we are but all small parts of something greater.
story.405.desc:
The Void Clouds are, as far as [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] researchers can tell, among the oldest entities in the universe. They seem to have originated just a scant few billion years after matter as we know it first appeared, the tremendous forces of the young cosmos making something out of nothing. They would have been stars once, but were not.

Explaining their apparent animal intelligence is more difficult, but the answer might lie in the abnormally strong electromagnetic fields that keep them together - another product of their primordial beginnings. It is not inconceivable that, given enough time, the circulation of its strange stardust and gravitic fields aligned in a flexible approximation of neural pathways.

Moreover, the Clouds seem to be receiving impulses from one another, if not outright communicating, lightyears apart. Quantum entanglement is suspected to play a role in this phenomenon.
story.405.desc.gesta:
The Void Clouds may be among the oldest entities in the universe. They seem to have originated just a scant few billion years after matter as we know it first appeared, the tremendous forces of the young cosmos making something out of nothing. They would have been stars once, but were not.

Explaining their apparent animal intelligence is more difficult, but the answer might lie in the abnormally strong electromagnetic fields that keep them together - another product of their primordial beginnings. It is not inconceivable that, given enough time, the circulation of its strange stardust and gravitic fields aligned in a flexible approximation of neural pathways or computational circuits.

Moreover, the Clouds seem to be receiving impulses from one another, if not outright communicating, lightyears apart. Quantum entanglement is suspected to play a role in this phenomenon.
story.405.a.spiri.tooltip:
Adds the Grand Design modifier to your Empire:
£ Happiness +5%
story.405.b: They will not stand in our way.
story.405.b.tooltip:
Adds the Cloudbuster modifier to our Empire:
Damage to Void Clouds: +10%
story.405.c.tooltip: Adds a list of likely Void Cloud systems to the Situation Log.
story.410.name: Dark Clouds
story.410.desc.spiri:
Brought down by the [From.GetName], the Void Cloud did not die easy.

Just before the Void Cloud's electromagnetic field finally collapsed - sending its star-stuff spiraling through the system - many crewmembers engaged in the battle reported a sudden sense of dread, of coming doom.

Perhaps we have sinned.
story.410.desc:
Victory over the Void Cloud was hard-won.

While we suffered heavy casualties, the fact remains that the [Root.GetName] has overcome one of the galaxy's most terrifying enigmas.
story.410.desc.gesta:
Victory over the Void Cloud was hard-won.

While we suffered heavy casualties, the fact remains that we have overcome one of the galaxy's most terrifying enigmas.
story.410.a.spiri: How could we atone, not knowing who we have wronged?
story.501.name: Tiyanki
story.501.desc.spiri:
The Diviners name the beings, floating through the dark, "Tiyanki." They are a sacred and peaceful spaceborne life form that roams from system to system, feeding on gases common to the upper layers of many gas giants, and rarely showing any signs of hostility.

We are to keep at a respectful distance.
story.501.desc:
The spaceborne lifeforms - which the [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] Head of Society Research has come to refer to as "Tiyanki" - are docile creatures. Capable of accessing some lower dimension of subspace, they roam from system to system with remarkable ease.

They graze on gases common to the upper layers of many gas giants. It is highly unlikely, to say the least, that this is their only food source, but intake of other nutrients has yet to be observed.

They will rarely, if ever, attack, even when provoked. They can safely be ignored.
story.501.desc.gesta:
The spaceborne lifeforms - which we call "Tiyanki" - are docile creatures. Capable of accessing some lower dimension of subspace, they roam from system to system with remarkable ease.

They graze on gases common to the upper layers of many gas giants. It is highly unlikely, to say the least, that this is their only food source, but intake of other nutrients has yet to be observed.

They will not attack unless provoked. They can safely be ignored.
story.501.a.mater: Hunting them would be a net loss anyway.
galactic_features.361.name: Effluvial Offspring
galactic_features.361.desc:
Following the destruction of our fleet in the [From.From.From.GetStarName] system, the local Void Cloud appears to have gathered enough material from the debris to undergo what can best be described as a form of mitosis on the macro level - asexual reproduction.

There is now one more Void Cloud haunting [From.From.From.GetStarName].
galactic_features.361.a.tooltip: Void Cloud spawned in the [From.From.From.GetStarName] system.
uplift.6000.ocean.desc:
According to the [Root.GetName], one [presapient_species.GetSpeciesClass] species native to [From.GetName] has not only achieved a tentative mastery of the planet's vast oceans, but also the small plots of land that dot its surface.

[Owner.GetScientistCapital] [Root.GetLeaderName] proposes that we should monitor their development closely, and possibly help them along the path to full sapience.
uplift.6000.b: Something to keep in mind for the future.
uplift.6010.name: Uplift Successful
uplift.6010.continental.desc: The dominant species on [Root.GetName], the [From.GetName], have been uplifted. Only minor genetic alterations were needed to unlock their inherent potential for vastly improved cognitive ability and manual dexterity, while members of previous generations will be fitted with small, cybernetic implants.
uplift.6010.ocean.desc: Our efforts to accelerate the evolution of the [From.GetName] along a favorable trajectory have been tremendously successful. Educational programs are in place for the youngest specimens - individuals, now - while their elders are proving receptive to psycho-genetic conditioning.
uplift.6010.tropical.desc: The [From.GetName] have been successfully uplifted to become productive citizens of the [Root.Owner.GetName] and inhabitants of our colony on the tropical planet [Root.GetName].
uplift.6010.arid.desc:
Success!

The [From.GetName] native to [This.GetName] have been uplifted to become citizens of the [This.Owner.GetName].
uplift.6010.desert.desc: The [From.GetName] now stand as living testament to the scientific and technological might of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
uplift.6010.savannah.desc: Our efforts to uplift the [From.GetName] have borne fruit: with some relatively minor modifications to their genetic code, we have succeeded in raising their cognitive faculties.
uplift.6010.tundra.desc:
The [From.GetName] are now sapient, and fairly intelligent at that.

They now fall under the dominion of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
uplift.6010.arctic.desc:
The [From.GetName], risen from the icy plains of [Root.GetName], have achieved sapience with [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] help.

They have joined our colony on their native planet [Root.GetName] as productive members of [Root.Owner.GetName] society.
uplift.6010.alpine.desc: The genetic modifications we made to the [From.GetName] have successfully raised the species to full sapience. Now, as they gaze up at the stars from their mountain homes, they do so with a true sense of themselves.
uplift.6010.nuked.desc: From their humble beginnings, the [From.GetName] have risen to join the [Root.Owner.GetName].
uplift.6010.gaia.desc: Thanks to our efforts, the [From.GetName] have been successfully uplifted. What a gift, to fully understand the paradise they inhabit.
uplift.6010.relic.desc: All across their ruined world, the dominant species of [Root.GetName] have awoken from their long slumber. Our efforts to uplift them to full sapience have been a resounding success.
uplift.6010.fallback.desc: Uplifted to full sapience, the [From.GetName] now stand as a living testament to the scientific and technological might of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
uplift.7000.name: Lift Up, Follow Up
uplift.7000.desc:
The [From.From.From.GetName] have been among us for several days now.

All is well on planet [From.GetName].
uplift.7010.name: A Rocky Start
uplift.7010.desc:
The integration of the [From.From.From.GetName] who we uplifted is going more smoothly than expected, but not as smoothly as we had hoped.

Despite our efforts to soft-shape of their psychology, the [From.From.From.GetName] still occasionally struggle with the way we do things in the [From.Owner.GetName].
uplift.7200.name: Looking Inwards
uplift.7200.desc:
A statistically significant group of [From.From.From.GetName] citizens appear unsatisfied with our teachings on the nature of the cosmos.

An unknown individual or group among them is circulating some spurious codex that attaches undue importance to the [From.From.From.GetName] and their uplifting by the [Root.Owner.GetName].
uplift.7200.c: Set them straight by any means necessary.
uplift.7205.name: Conscientious Objectors
uplift.7205.desc: Some issues have arisen on [Root.GetName] as a result of the [From.From.From.GetName] populace's aversion to arms. A representative has made a formal request for clearly delineated demilitarized zones.
uplift.7205.b: The courage of their convictions should be celebrated.
uplift.7205.c: They must learn that the specter of war looms over us all.
uplift.7210.name: Stranger Danger
uplift.7210.desc: According to reports, newly-uplifted [From.From.From.GetName] citizens on [Root.GetName] grow anxious as their [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] teachers bring up the likelihood of contact with as-yet-unknown entities from the far reaches of space.
uplift.7210.b: What is alien to us is simply opportunity in disguise.
uplift.7210.c: They are right to fear the unknown.
uplift.7215.name: Familial Fission
uplift.7215.desc:
While the [Root.Owner.GetName] provides a solid structure upon which to model their internal social order, it may not necessarily be what suits the uplifted [From.From.From.GetName] best.

Their sudden rise to becoming our intellectual equals robbed them of millennia of potential societal and cultural development. Perhaps as a result of this, the [From.From.From.GetName] social order is in a state of extreme flux; one day the family unit is paramount, and the next day community leaders are calling for a dissolution of all clan-like bonds.
uplift.7215.b: May the [From.From.From.GetName] find themselves, in each other.
uplift.7500.name: Forked Chain
uplift.7500.desc:
A number of individuals belonging to the pre-sapient, native population of [From.GetName] somehow got into a secure compound on the outskirts of our colony. They were chased off within hours, but not before severely damaging several interstellar uplinks dedicated to currency transfers.

We fear several hundred Credits may have been lost in the ether.
uplift.7510.name: In Vivo
uplift.7510.desc:
Xeno-researchers on [Root.GetName] have published an open letter demanding that the local legislation restricting experiments on near-sapient alien species be relaxed.

They make a convincing case for the scientific benefits, and warn that the output of the entire scientific community on [Root.GetName] will suffer unless the laws are revised.

The ethics of it all remain questionable.
uplift.7510.a.tooltip: The local scientists will not be happy about this.
uplift.7510.b: We will accede to their demands.
uplift.7510.b.tooltip: The locals will not be happy about this.
uplift.7510.c: Ethics? We care little for the fate of lesser beings.
uplift.7510.c.tooltip: Your Empire gains the Fanatic Xenophobe Ethic.
uplift.7520.name: Fidgeting
uplift.7520.desc: The near-sapient natives of [Root.GetName] are causing a ruckus on the outskirts of our colony. Something about the [Root.Owner.GetName]'s continued presence here visibly agitates them, as packs of them scurry to and fro between the settlement's borders and some unknown point to the east.
uplift.7520.a: Drive them off. Gently, if possible.
uplift.7520.a.tooltip: The indigenous creatures will not bother the colonists again.
uplift.7520.b: Send these dumb animals a violent message.
uplift.7520.b.tooltip: The grotesque creatures will not bother the colonists again.
uplift.7520.c: Try to figure out where they are going.
uplift.7525.name: Lost and Forgotten
uplift.7525.desc:
A group of xenologists departed the colony together with a contingent of military personnel, tracking the movements of the native life-forms.

What they found were the remains of some ancient seed-ship, evidently the nucleus of some small, [Owner.GetPreFTLLower] civilization, long since decayed into nothing.

The dominant native species of [Root.GetName] seem to be the product of some age-old seeding or genetic manipulation program; going by the structures surrounding the seed ship, they were once distinctly tribal, with greater intelligence and even a rudimentary written language.

We cannot begin to guess what caused their species-wide devolution, but their behavior makes more sense now. On some instinctual level they recognize us [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] as similar to their original uplifters from the stars. Perhaps our ordered society calls out to some instilled impulse to order, drowned out by their baser nature.

Maybe we can eventually ease their evolutionary anxiety by uplifting them to our level, but for now, we have gained valuable insights into the manipulation of organics by ancient spacefaring cultures.
amoebas_2_chain_desc: Eliminate 4 more Space Amoebas to get a better understanding of their biology.
crystals_1_chain_desc: Destroy a Crystalline Entity formation to retrieve a mineral sample.
crystals_2_chain_desc: Crush 4 Crystalline Entity fleets to gather further combat scenario data.
drones_1_chain_desc: Disable and attempt to reverse-engineer a Mining Drone.
clouds_1_chain_desc: Neutralize a Void Cloud to sift through its primordial star-stuff.
mineral_planet_chain_desc: Using techniques derived from the Ancient Mining Drones' assessment systems, we have pin-pointed a handful of stellar bodies that are likely to be particularly rich in minerals.
mineral_planet_poi_desc: Using techniques derived from the Ancient Mining Drones' assessment systems, we have pin-pointed a handful of star systems that are likely to have particularly mineral-rich planetary bodies.
cloud_chain_desc:
All Void Clouds are entangled with one another on the quantum level; it is possible that the energies animating the individual specimens are nothing but multiple instances of a singular sub-space entity.

Through careful study of one Void Cloud, we have been able to locate a number of systems that are likely to house other Clouds.
cloud_poi_desc: Quantum entanglement points to these systems being home to Void Clouds.
find_sol_chain_desc: An alien artifact provides the coordinates for a particular system.
sol_1_desc_neutral: Whatever beings sent the artifact into space seem to have originated here. It would be prudent to investigate.
old_gods_shrine_poi_1_desc: Radiometric findings indicate that an object similar to the shrine to the Untold might orbiting this star.
old_gods_shrine_poi_2_desc: Radiometric findings indicate that another object similar to the shrine to the Untold might be orbiting this star.
old_gods_shrine_poi_3_desc: Radiometric findings indicate that a third object similar to the shrine to the Untold might be orbiting this star.
shrine_object_tooltip: A shrine dedicated to one of our people's old gods, lost in space.
shrine_object_desc: A shrine dedicated to one of our people's old gods, lost in space.
old_gods_chain_desc: After the discovery of the mysterious asteroid-shrine to the Untold, top scientists have proposed that there may be additional shrines dedicated to our - or what we believed was only our - pantheon, in neighboring systems.
ransomeer_chain_desc:
A band of pirates calling themselves the "Ransomeers" have kidnapped the crew of a [Root.GetSpeciesAdj] private transport vessel.

We intend to free them before the pirates can make any demands.
ransomeer_poi_desc: The Ransomeers have made a home out of an abandoned alien mining station.
wrecked_fleet_chain_desc:
Millennia ago, treachery saw a fleet of allied ships turn on each other. With swift strikes to critical systems and known weak points in the hull designs, the formerly allied crews were wiped out with ruthless efficiency, supposedly leaving the depressurized hulks of the ships largely intact.

We have gleaned enough information to model this ship graveyard's slow drift through the cosmos.
wrecked_fleet_poi_desc: We have calculated the drifting battlefield's current position to be somewhere in the indicated system. It would be prudent to investigate the site, given the opportunity.
rogue_scientist_1_chain_desc:
The Chair of the [Root.GetName]'s Abstract Sciences Board has gone missing along with an unorthodox Science Ship prototype.

Their current whereabouts have been narrowed down to three likely locations, to be investigated in turn.
rogue_scientist_2_chain_desc: The Chair has vanished again, but this time they left a trail.
rogue_scientist_3_chain_desc:
Whatever their motives may be, the Chair must be brought back to [Root.Capital.GetName].

Whether they will write a revolutionary thesis or simply face disciplinary action remains to be seen.
scientist_poi_1_desc: The last known location of the Chair's Science Ship, outside of the [Root.Capital.GetStarName] system's borders.
scientist_poi_2_desc: The Chair's destination, as per their last message to [Root.Capital.GetName].
scientist_poi_3_desc:
As luck would have it, a long-distance sensor array on [Root.Capital.GetName] picked up faint energy signatures that may or may not have resulted from FTL travel.

The trajectory does not match any known flight paths, making the Chair a likely suspect.
scientist_poi_4_desc: Having deciphered the prototype Science Ship's peculiar energy signatures and applied some fairly complex mathematics, we now know what system the Chair fled to.
scientist_poi_5_desc: It seems the Chair is about to reach their final destination.
mass_extinction_chain_desc: To avoid a potential apocalypse on [Root.Capital.GetName], we must study the effects that major calamities have had on other planets.
massex_poi_1_desc: An asteroid belt orbits a star as the only witness to some great cataclysm.
massex_poi_2_desc: This planet wallows in its own infernal crucible.
massex_poi_3_desc: This planet is impressively barren, despite advantageous conditions for sustaining life.
massex_poi_4_desc: The toxic fumes that now dominate this planet's atmosphere appear to have originated fairly recently and suddenly.
massex_poi_5_desc: Astronomical records indicate that this planet was not always a frozen wasteland.
UPLIFT_SNAKEOID_CAT_DESC: Something moves with near-purpose through the sands of [Root.GetName]...
UPLIFT_GENERIC_CAT_DESC: Something moves with near-purpose down on [Root.GetName]...
UPLIFT_OCEAN_CAT_DESC: There are distinct signs of life in and near the seas of [Root.GetName].
UPLIFT_ARID_CAT_DESC: Even weak optical arrays can easily pick out traces of biological activity on the surface of [Root.GetName].
UPLIFT_CONTINENTAL_CAT_DESC: It seems life has found a way, even on a planet torn between the extremes of rocky soils and liquid seas.
UPLIFT_TROPICAL_CAT_DESC: The conditions on [Root.GetName] are ideal for life, at least on the microbial level - and maybe beyond.
UPLIFT_TUNDRA_CAT_DESC: [Root.GetName] is frozen and anonymous to optical scans, but heat signatures indicate some activity just below the surface.
UPLIFT_ARCTIC_CAT_DESC: Somewhere below the ice-storms and above the permafrost of [Root.GetName], there is movement.
UPLIFT_DESERT_CAT_DESC: It is hard to imagine life on [Root.GetName], its surface an endless sea of silicate particles. And yet...
UPLIFT_ROACHOID_CAT_DESC: Arthropodal herds navigate [Root.GetName]'s blasted surface with ease.
anomaly_failure.2500.desc: On closer inspection, the asteroid [From.From.GetName] is found to be silent. One of [Root.GetLeaderName]'s assistants eventually confesses that they may have misread the instruments.
anomaly_failure.2501.desc: The [Root.GetName] struggles to safely navigate the dense debris field surrounding [From.From.GetName]. Whatever their sensors picked up on is gone by the time [Root.GetLeaderName] and crew arrive.
anomaly_failure.2502.desc: The [Root.GetName]'s probes find over the course of their many sweeps over [From.From.GetName]'s surface. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has issued a formal apology for wasting time and resources on a detailed, fruitless, survey of the planet.
anomaly_failure.2503.desc: What appeared from space to be impressive structures are, up close, somewhat disappointing. The [Root.GetName] remained in orbit around [From.GetName] for a time to study the planet's weather patterns, after which Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] was able to confirm that the planetary structures are the result of mundane meteorological factors and not the efforts of intelligent life.
anomaly_failure.2504.desc: Before the crew of the [Root.GetName] could decisively triangulate the distress signal from the super-heated surface of [From.From.GetName], it disappeared. Without a specific geographic point to focus on, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] deems a rescue attempt too dangerous to pursue.
anomaly_failure.2535.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] of the [Root.GetName] reports that the structures on the surface of [From.From.GetName] are utterly beneath our notice and their time is better spent elsewhere.
anomaly_failure.2540.desc:
The crew of the [Root.GetName] report that the asteroid, carved into the likeness of some sort of temple, is indeed pretty.

That is all.
anomaly_failure.2545.desc:
[Root.GetLeaderName]'s crew aboard the [Root.GetName] have determined that the unique aural features of [From.From.GetName] are due to the wildlife on the planet coming together in a capella renditions of unknown, alien songs.

They did not see fit to investigate the matter further.
anomaly_failure.2550.desc: The [Root.GetName] was unable to recover any samples of interest from the ice giant [From.From.GetName].
anomaly_failure.2555.desc: The [Root.GetName]'s exploratory probe uncover a fairly slapdash configuration of alien technology. Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName]'s ill-advised attempts to activate the thing unfortunately lead to its destruction.
anomaly_failure.2560.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has issued a report indicating that they are none too pleased having been ordered to study [From.From.GetName], where they have found nothing of interest.
anomaly_failure.2600.desc:
The [Root.GetName] had been orbiting [From.GetName] for some time, monitoring its emanations without incident, when Science Officer [Root.GetName] decided to suit up and spacewalk on the asteroid and procure some mineral samples.

As they touched down on its surface, [From.From.GetName]'s radio-like transmissions suddenly and drastically started increasing in intensity. The microwaves boiled [Root.GetLeaderName] alive within minutes.
anomaly_failure.2601.desc:
We lost track of the [Root.GetName] shortly after it entered the dense field of debris surrounding [From.From.GetName].

Days later, we recovered an escape pod from the edge of the field; Science Officer [Root.GetName] survived, but has no memory of what became of the [Root.GetName] or her crew.
anomaly_failure.2602.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName]'s careless probing of [From.GetName] has angered the two massive Tiyanki that orbit the planet. These creatures pose a substantial threat to the [Root.GetName].
anomaly_failure.2603.desc: The curious formations on [From.From.GetName] are an ancient trap. Before the [Root.GetName] was able to land, the ship was set upon by a small number of old combat drones.
anomaly_failure.2604.desc:
The [Root.GetName] was struck by a sudden eruption of magma from the surface of [From.From.GetName] as it was flying low, trying to get a lock on the distress signal.

There were no survivors.
anomaly_failure.2635.desc:
The point of interest on [From.From.GetName] was once, according to reports from the [Root.GetName], some sort of area dedicated to recreation and amusement. Its age is uncertain, as is the reason why it was established on [From.From.GetName] in the first place.

The crew of the [Root.GetName] also report the regrettable passing of their Science Officer, who was crushed by a toppling structure identified only as a "Ferris wheel."
anomaly_failure.2640.desc:
Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] remains adamant that the crew of the [Root.GetName] found nothing within the ornately sculpted, hollowed-out [From.From.GetName].

But something about the scientist has changed.
anomaly_failure.2645.desc: In their last message, the crew of the [Root.GetName] reported aural activity spiking on [From.From.GetName] as they were approaching the surface. Communications were cut off shortly after, and the ship and all aboard are missing, presumed dead.
anomaly_failure.2650.desc:
The crew let the [Root.GetName] slip below minimum safe altitude in their attempt to gather as many ice samples as possible. By some happenstance atmospheric supercritical fluids got into the ship's rear thrusters, with disastrous results.

There were no survivors.
anomaly_failure.2655.desc: As the [Root.GetName] approaches [From.From.GetName], it is intercepted by a couple of less-than-friendly smuggling ships. The hostiles turn their weapons on the asteroid, destroying all evidence of whatever operation they were running there. The [Root.GetName] is next, it seems.
anomaly_failure.2660.desc:
The crew of the [Root.GetName] report that the ship's Science Officer took a particular interest in the rain on [From.From.GetName], as it is, in their words, "kind of purple."

Unfortunately, the precipitation samples retrieved turned out to be highly volatile, and once unsealed in the lab aboard the [Root.GetName] the liquid violently combusted, killing the Science Officer instantly.
anomaly_failure.2665.desc: In their last message, the crew of the [Root.GetName] reported activity spiking on [From.From.GetName] as they approached the surface. Communications were cut off shortly thereafter, and the ship and all aboard are missing, presumed dead.
anomaly_failure.2670.desc:
It appears as if the [Root.GetName]'s enthusiastic probing of the old construct's systems has, quite literally, backfired.

Before the ancient circuits finally fried, the [Root.GetName] managed to remotely activate the orbital station's positional thrusters - promptly knocking it out of its gentle orbit and into the star's gravity well. The mission's unfortunate outcome has had a profound impact on the ship's commander, [Root.GetLeaderName], who has grown from the experience.
colony.1500.name: A Prelude
colony.1500.desc:
Something stirs on the moon of [Root.GetName].

Preliminary scans indicate that some ancient technology has become active, possibly as a response to our colonization efforts.

Several of our top scientists are eager to take a closer look at the moon, and have prepared a special research project.
colony.1501.name: Ancient Drones: Discovery
colony.1501.desc:
It is a gaggle of wayward drones, of course.

Initial disappointment was swept away by the drones' erroneous IFF classification of us - they think we are a race affiliated with their long-dead masters! They seemed very excited, if old AI constructs can be excited, to see us. Unfortunately, the drones again lapsed into inactivity shortly after and we have been unable to resuscitate them.

Or take them apart, for that matter.
colony.1501.a: Keep an eye on the situation.
colony.1502.name: Ancient Drones: Awakening
colony.1502.desc: The drones woke from their slumber and descended to the surface of [Root.GetName]. Attempts to communicate were met with polite dismissal as they set about terraforming a small area of the planet. We do not know the nature of whatever ancient directive they are executing, but it does not seem detrimental to the colony.
colony.1502.a: Well, as long as their activities benefit us...
colony.1502.a.tooltip: The drones remove a random £ Tile Blocker from the surface, leaving the planet otherwise untouched.
colony.1503.name: Ancient Drones: Reaching For Past Skies
colony.1503.desc:
The old drones fitfully dormant on [Root.GetName]'s moon have become active again, and their work is a mixed blessing.

Under the cover of night and spotty airspace surveillance, they have erected the framework of some gigantic structure a short distance away from our primary settlement on [Root.GetName]. Our engineers are convinced it is the realization of some outmoded concept known as a "space elevator," perhaps a common sight in the times before we [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] first took to the stars. It will eventually have to be razed as it stands in the way of our expansion plans for the colony, and bringing it down safely will take some time. At least our engineers are giddy with excitement at the prospect of studying the thing up close.
colony.1504.name: Ancient Drones: Spontaneous Generosity
colony.1504.desc:
After waking yet again, the drones briefly disappeared from sensors. When they returned, it was with a large cache of minerals of unknown origin in tow. They dumped it on the surface of [Root.GetName] after sending a badly corrupted burst transmission indicating that they had fulfilled a requisition request.

Then they went back to the moon.
colony.1505.name: Ancient Drones: An Estranged Relative
colony.1505.desc: Frantic signal bursts from the moon alerted us to the fact that the old drones on [Root.GetPlanetMoon] have woken yet again. This time they bring us a significant prize, as they have unearthed an ancient satellite from the depths of their moon and partially repaired it. We do not know how the satellite ended up there, nor why the drones have ignored it until now. Regardless, if even a fragment of its databanks have survived, there is a lot we can learn about day-to-day life in the empires that the drones first served.
colony.1506.name: Ancient Drones: Drone Debacle
colony.1506.desc:
The erratic behavior of the narcoleptic drones have taken a violent turn. A number of them woke and entered the atmosphere of [Root.GetName], as is their wont, only to slam into the surface of the planet at full thrust.

Repeatedly, in many cases.

Damage to the colony was negligible but the nigh-invulnerable drones were destroyed in bright showers of blue sparks, indicative of the tremendous force of, and dedication to, their self-destruction.
colony.1506.a: Can we find out what was wrong with them?
colony.1507.name: Ancient Drones: Looking For Drones
colony.1507.desc:
The surviving drones have been missing since the suicide incident. History buffs on [Root.GetName] are convinced the drones are still in close proximity, shielded from view by some lost technology, but the expected time window for their next activation has come and gone.

Progress on deep analysis of the destroyed drones' remains has been slow, but a breakthrough is expected soon.
colony.1508.name: Ancient Drones: Panning For Gold
colony.1508.desc: Sorting out the errant innards of the shattered drones took much longer than anticipated, as each drone seems to have been built from a slightly different design, assembled from slightly different parts. Once this fact was established, one thing stood out - the parts that were identical. Separated from the rest, it is clear these parts are of somewhat modern, if alien, make. It is likely that someone has done what we could not, and tampered with the drones.
colony.1509.name: Ancient Drones: Alien to the Aliens
colony.1509.desc: Having pieced them together, the foreign objects inside the destroyed drones have been identified by our experts as one-way transmitters. Since they are not set to receive, it is safe to assume that the drones were not acting at the behest of some third party. Rather, some entity has been keeping tabs on the drones' activities. It is advisable to look into this matter.
colony.1510.name: Ancient Drones: Answers Above
colony.1510.desc:
We have found the remaining drones, drifting into orbit around [Root.GetPlanetMoon]. We have learned that they are unwitting pawns in an elaborate scheme set up by an unknown faction.

Going by the modus operandi of this operation, this faction is most likely a particularly old and particularly clever pirate syndicate. They must have found the drones drifting through space and done what we could not; modified them. While not as impressive as it sounds - all they did was introduce self-contained alien technology into the drones - fact remains that these alien pirates possess a technological know-how far in advance of our own, at least in certain areas. Having installed their comms devices in the drones, the pirates let them drift through space again, knowing that they are set to assist their original masters' colonists and that the drones' ability to accurately identify such colonists has degraded with age. The drones have essentially been fattening up our colony as the pirates watch, waiting for the ideal time to strike.

Our military analysts predict that the pirates will strike within the next two years.
colony.1510.b: Capture the drones, send them to destroy their would-be masters.
colony.1510.c: We must not let this happen again. Dismantle the drones.
colony.1511.name: Ancient Drones: A Final Goodbye
colony.1511.desc: We have captured the drones and fitted them with explosive charges. Reprogramming them proved to be a relatively easy task now that we know how to break them open, and we have plotted a course for the estimated location of the pirate fleet. Top [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] scientists have implemented our own IFF technology to minimize the risk of the drones attacking innocents.
colony.1512.name: Ancient Drones: Wounded and Volatile
colony.1512.desc: The pirate fleet is inbound, earlier than expected. It is likely our preemptive strike was successful both in provoking and damaging them - their fleet is roughly 30% smaller than projected.
colony.1513.name: Ancient Drones: They're Everywhere
colony.1513.desc: The pirate fleet has arrived, somewhat later than expected. Judging by the makeup of the fleet and formations used, they have rallied their allies in an effort to pillage and burn [Root.GetName] as quickly and decisively as possible.
colony.1513.a: They will do no such thing.
colony.1514.name: Ancient Drones: Showdown
colony.1514.desc: The time has come, and the pirate armada arrives on cue.
colony.1514.a: This fight has been a long time coming.
colony.1520.name: Mharin Kharin: Floral Fascination
colony.1520.desc:
Several plants native to [Root.GetName], where we recently established a colony, exude copious amounts of a pollen with an astounding chemical complexity.

A special research project has been prepared for further study of this flora.
colony.1521.name: Mharin Kharin: Olfactory Arousal
colony.1521.desc: Long-term exposure to the pollen naturally occurring in [Root.GetName]'s atmosphere acts on the colonists' pheromone receptors with a mild aphrodisiac effect, accompanied by a barely-perceptible "high." The plant that produces the most potent strain is a flower common to all areas of the planet; squirreled away into some obscure taxonomic nook by scientists on [Root.GetName] but known in the local [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] dialect as "Mharin Kharin."
colony.1521.b: We cannot allow mind-altering particles in the atmosphere.
colony.1521.c: We do not have the resources to exterminate the plant.
colony.1522.name: Mharin Kharin: Making Time for Petals
colony.1522.desc:
Reports from [Root.GetName] indicate that worker productivity has declined recently, becoming stable at levels several percent lower than the [Root.Owner.GetName] average.

This may or may not be due to the stimulating effects of the pollen native to the planet.

It probably is.

A Special Project has been prepared should we wish to make our production pipelines more efficient to make up for the loss.
colony.1522.a: Let's see what can be done.
colony.1523.name: Mharin Kharin: Work Over Flowers
colony.1523.desc:
Far-reaching changes to time management paradigms and the way responsibility is delegated within all fields of production and other duties on [Root.GetName] have produced good results. The populace has an evident desire - outside observers would call it an outright need - to be in close proximity to the native flora.

With clever scheduling and additional checks in place, productivity remains low but has risen above the lower limit of what can be deemed acceptable.
colony.1524.name: Mharin Kharin: Rooted in Place
colony.1524.desc:
A recent survey indicates that residents of [Root.GetName] are much less likely than other denizens of the [Root.Owner.GetName] to migrate to other planets.

The survey does not address whether this could be due to a psychological dependency on the low-level sensory arousal caused by Mharin Kharin and its sibling-plants.
colony.1525.name: Mharin Kharin: Transmission Trouble
colony.1525.desc: While productivity is no longer declining on the planet, communications between the colony on [Root.GetName] and the capital on [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] are breaking down. Senior officials on [Root.GetName] are growing increasingly distant, and our clerks are complaining that even relaying simple directives is becoming an exercise in frustration.
colony.1525.b: Deploy an administrative task force. Code mauve.
colony.1526.name: Mharin Kharin: Upper Management Betrayal
colony.1526.desc: It appears that the crack team of administrators we sent to [Root.GetName] in order to set things straight have been turned. Fortunately for us, their plot to do as little work as possible was, unsurprisingly, sloppily executed and easily discovered. Heads will roll - metaphorically speaking of course - as our last recourse is to depose the local government and manage the colony's affairs from the capital.
colony.1527.name: Mharin Kharin: With an Iron Fist, From Afar
colony.1527.desc: Our remote-government of [Root.GetName] is now firmly established. It has met with some success in suppressing the proliferation of the pollen-bearing plant Mharin Kharin as well as in eroding the community's acceptance of "using" it - no small feat considering the act is as innocent as smelling a flower.
colony.1528.name: Mharin Kharin: Slash and Burn
colony.1528.desc: Our remote-governance of [Root.GetName] continues to be a somewhat awkward but effective arrangement. The council in charge has allegedly secured the loyalty of a faction of our armed forces on the planet - apparently they prefer staying indoors to breathing in the Mharin Kharin pollen. The remote-government wishes to use these troops to mount an offensive on the flower, having them erect atmospheric purifiers and wiping the plant from all urban areas entirely.
colony.1528.a: We should have done this a long time ago.
colony.1528.a.tooltip: The intoxicating plant is strictly controlled and contained outside of populated areas, removing all related modifiers.
colony.1529.name: Mharin Kharin: Pollen Worship
colony.1529.desc:
Fringe elements on [Root.GetName] have banded together to form a quasi-religious organization seeking to control all aspects of the Mharin Kharin flower and its cultivation. Their leader, a self-styled "Green Hierophant" of this "Flower Temple" claims to speak for all flora and fauna of [Root.GetName] and demands exclusive trading rights for the plant.

This is of course completely unacceptable and impossible, as the native flora of [Root.GetName] is of little strategic or economic value and thus may not be brought off-world by law.

Unfortunately, they are unlikely to accept this fact gracefully.
colony.1530.name: Mharin Kharin: Beginning of Pollen's End
colony.1530.desc:
The Flower Temple and its followers now make up a sizable minority of the population on [Root.GetName], and reports indicate a disturbing change in the movement. Their futile attempts to smuggle Mharin Kharin specimen off-world have been growing less enthusiastic by the day, as the Flower Temple seems to be transitioning into a doomsday cult. There is likely a correlation with the recent changes in the Mharin Kharin pollen's chemical makeup, detected by atmospheric sensors.

A Special Project has been prepared to assess the risks associated with this, and it is recommended to complete it before something goes horribly wrong.
colony.1531.name: Mharin Kharin: Disaster Averted
colony.1531.desc:
Quick and decisive action allowed us to identify the risks associated with the rapid changes in the pollen native to [Root.GetName] and take the necessary steps.

The necessary steps were a complete planetary evacuation and a planet-wide tactical pesticide bombing run, targeting the Mharin Kharin flower and its ilk.

The plants were rapidly mutating and their unique pollen would, had they not been destroyed, soon have begun delivering a potent neurotoxin to the olfactory organs of all sapient life on [Root.GetName].

The scientists on the colonization council theorize that this is part of a natural cycle on [Root.GetName] and that the pollen's adverse effects on us, in the form of a crumbling local administration, the rise of the Flower Temple cult, and eventual pollen toxicity, were chance side-effects rather than the product of a plant's sinister self-defense mechanism.

Regardless, any and all traces of the flower have been wiped from the planet's surface, and our colonists are safe and free of the pollen's influence.
colony.1531.a.tooltip: The planet has been purged of the dangerous flower, removing all related modifiers.
colony.1532.name: Mharin Kharin: The Pollen's End of Us
colony.1532.desc:
Something went horribly wrong.

Vast swaths of Mharin Kharin flowers spontaneously mutated in unison, spreading like wildfire and turning their pollen poisonous, and we were too late.

Both our evacuation efforts and our attempts to neutralize the pollen fell short of the mark and the inhabitants of [Root.GetName] paid the price.

The plant life of [Root.GetName] achieved only a pyrrhic victory, though this fact is scant consolation. The whole genus that Mharin Kharin belonged to burned in the fire of its own unnaturally rapid proliferation. The soil is starved of the specific nutrients the pollinating plants need - once the currently living specimens die, which will be soon, it will be a long time before that flora can again establish a foothold in the ecosystem, if it ever will.

The inhabitants of [Root.GetName] are dead, and the planet's atmosphere is temporarily noxious with plant emissions.
colony.1532.a: We will not forget this tragedy.
colony.1533.name: Mharin Kharin: A New Beginning
colony.1533.desc:
A planetary surveillance team reports that the toxic miasma that enveloped a planet two years ago and led to the destruction of our colony has lifted. The planet is different now, changed into a desert world after the violent blooming of Mharin Kharin and the atmosphere becoming saturated with pollen.

It will take more than these two years for the [Root.Owner.GetName] to forget the tragic fate of those who lived there, but the planet itself is no longer actively hostile to sapient life.
pheromonefrenzy.revived.tooltip: Your former colony has changed into a desert planet, and can be colonized with the right technology.
colony.1534.name: Mharin Kharin: Pistil Pondering
colony.1534.desc: On closer examination, the plants native to [Root.GetName] turn out to be rather dull. Some excrete pollen that have a mild stimulating effect and they are likely to have a propensity for rapid genetic change; hardly impressive enough to warrant adopting as a strategic or luxury resource.
communications_spread.1.name: Communications Intercepted
communications_spread.1.desc: By intercepting a message sent to the [CommSpreader.GetName], we have learned that they are in regular contact with another spacefaring empire that we ourselves have no contact with. By tracing this message to its source, we have been able to establish our own line of communications with this previously unknown actor on the galactic stage.
communications_spread.2.name: New Contact
communications_spread.2.desc: We have received a communiqué from a previously unknown spacefaring empire that call themselves the [From.GetName]. They claim to have learned of our existence by listening in on the communications of another empire we are in contact with.
fallen_empires.2.name: [From.GetName] assassinate [Root.GetRulerTitle]!
fallen_empires.2.desc:
As if to punish us for not only warring with the Stagnant Ascendancy of the [From.GetName] but for then accepting defeat, [From.GetAdj] agents appeared by [Root.GetRulerTitle] [rulername.GetName]'s side after the peace negotiations concluded.

They dispatched our [Root.GetRulerTitle] with unseen weaponry and practiced brutality before melting away as if they were never there.
fallen_empires.2.a: We are defeated and humiliated, but will rise again.
fallen_empires.4.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.4.desc: Arrogant little wretch! Did you think that the [Root.GetSpeciesName] colonists sullying our holy places would go unnoticed? Leave our worlds immediately or face the might of our fleets!
fallen_empires.4.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.5.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.5.desc: [Root.GetSpeciesName], we have observed your fumbling attempts at creating artificial intelligence and come to the conclusion that you are headed down the path of spiritual self-destruction. Abandon this foolish endeavour at once, or we will MAKE you.
fallen_empires.5.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.5.a.tooltip: Artificial Intelligence policy will be set to Outlawed.
fallen_empires.6.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.6.desc: [Root.GetSpeciesName] barbarians! Your crimes have not gone unnoticed. The enslavement and butchery that you are so wantonly engaging threatens the future of the entire galaxy. We present you with a choice: end your barbarous practices, or prepare to face our righteous might.
fallen_empires.6.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.6.a.tooltip:
Slavery policy will be set to Prohibited.
Purge policy will be set to Prohibited.
fallen_empires.7.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.7.desc: Filthy [From.GetSpeciesNamePluralInsult]! You have encroached upon our space for the last time! Withdraw immediately, or we will cleanse the stain upon the universe that is your worthless species.
fallen_empires.7.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.8.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.8.desc: Foolish [Root.GetSpeciesName]. The lack of respect you show for your elders will be your undoing. Prostrate yourselves before us and beg our forgiveness, and we may refrain from annihilating your worthless little empire.
fallen_empires.8.desc.control: Disharmonious [Root.GetSpeciesName]. Don't you see that by inviting chaos you force us to intervene. Harmonize now or we will tune you.
fallen_empires.8.desc.growth: Stagnant [Root.GetSpeciesName], your refusal to grow and evolve is an affront to life itself. Embrace our teachings, or we will uproot your failure and sow the seeds of progress ourselves
fallen_empires.8.desc.war: Cowardly [Root.GetSpeciesName]. Your empire is a testament to frailty. Now swallow your weakness, apologize, and get ready to meet our challenge -  or we will shatter you and replace you with someone more worthy.
fallen_empires.8.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.8.a.tooltip:
Ends rivalry with [fallen_empire_humiliator.GetName]
[Root.GetName] loses any claims to the [fallen_empire_humiliator.GetName]'s systems
fallen_empires.9.name: Communication from [From.GetName]
fallen_empires.9.desc: Blasphemous [Root.GetSpeciesName]! You tread carelessly in the halls of the dead, crushing history underfoot, thinking nothing of the spirits whose rest you disturb. No more! Leave the dead in peace or answer to the living - to us.
fallen_empires.9.a: We have no choice but to accept...
fallen_empires.100.B.desc.spi:
$fallen_empires.100.desc.spi_intro$

We believe [from.GetName] was worshipped as a deity, or else has been regarded as a holy place. The decorative styling on the buoy suggests it may even be the [spi_fallen_empire.GetName] who once revered this place. It is unclear whether or not that is still the case.
fallen_empires.100.B.desc.gestalt:
Our survey of [from.GetName] suggests this bountiful world in the [from.solar_system.GetName] system was once a subject of keen interest to an advanced - though sentimental - life-form. A long-disused navigation buoy in high orbit has been etched with intricate designs similar to those displayed by the [spi_fallen_empire.GetName].

It seems the [spi_fallen_empire.GetSpeciesNamePlural] once sought to preserve this [from.GetClassAdj] world, though they give no indication if that is still the case.
fallen_empires.100.a: We shall honor this place also.
fallen_empires.100.b: It is ours for the taking.
scion_found_holy_world_desc: Religious scholars and lay practitioners alike are rejoicing in the discovery of a Holy World - once feared by some to be little more than a myth.
scion_suspicious_holy_world_desc: This society is coming to terms with the fact its keepers hid certain truths from them - not least the existence and whereabouts of a known Holy World.
origin.13.hasmet.desc:
$origin.13.desc.intro$

The sheer sophistication of this device parallels that of even [overlord.GetAdj] technology; we therefore believe the marker belongs to the nearby [spi_fallen_empire.GetName]. As to its purpose: we cannot say for sure, but it seems likely the [spi_fallen_empire.GetSpeciesNamePlural] consider this world to be holy.
origin.13.notmet.desc:
$origin.13.desc.intro$

The sheer sophistication of this device parallels that of even [overlord.GetAdj] technology, however its design is distinctly alien. We must therefore assume the marker belongs to some contemporary of theirs, past or present. Judging by the various symbols etched onto its exterior: it may even be marking out a holy site.
fallen_empire_refuse_tooltip: [From.GetName] will be very angry, and are likely to attack us.
fallen_empire_happy_tooltip: [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetName] will be pleased, and may show us favor in the future.
fallen_empire_angry_tooltip: [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetName] will be most displeased, and may decide to teach us a lesson.
fallen_empire_enigmatic_tooltip: [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetName] may or may not react to our refusal.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.name: Communication from [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetName]
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.a.materialis: [Root.GetSpeciesName], we have decided to grace your empire with a gift of resources as a token of our esteem. Do not squander our generosity or take our favor for granted.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.a.xenophile: [Root.GetSpeciesName], your species is a most worthwhile addition to the galactic community. As a token of our esteem, we have decided to bestow on you a generous gift of valuable minerals and resources.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.a.machine.o: Custodian protocol 712-4 activated. Initiating resource transfer to compliant organic civilization. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.a.machine.s: Custodian protocol 718-4 activated. Initiating resource transfer to compliant synthetic intelligence. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.a.spirituali: [Root.GetSpeciesName]! Your species is a worthy one, and your adherence to the immutable doctrines of faith are to be commended. Accept this gift of resources as a token of our boundless benevolence.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.b.materialis: [Root.GetSpeciesName], the sheer inefficiency of your technology pains us. As you are a valuable client to the [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetName], we have decided to share with you some of our understanding of the universe. This is not something we do for just any species, so be sure to continue to be of use to us - ingratitude is not a desirable trait in children.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.b.xenophile: [Root.GetSpeciesName], we have observed your lack of technological progress with concern. At your current pace, we fear that you will never reach your true potential before you wipe yourselves out or are conquered by a more advanced species. In order to help you along, we will transfer a data cache of [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetSpeciesName] scientific knowledge. You will no doubt find its contents to be of invaluable worth to your empire.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.b.machine.o: Custodian protocol 712-6 activated. Initiating data store transfer to primitive organic civilization. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.b.machine.s: Custodian protocol 718-6 activated. Initiating data store transfer to rudimentary synthetic intelligence. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.b.spirituali: [Root.GetSpeciesName]! Your species is a worthy one, and your adherence to the immutable doctrines of faith are to be commended. Accept this gift of sacred knowledge as a token of our boundless benevolence.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.c.materialis:
[Root.GetSpeciesName], as a [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetSpeciesName] client the state of your fleets also reflects on us, and those crude hulks you call "warships" reflect very poorly indeed. To this end we have decided to gift you a squadron of surplus escort ships that should look most impressive to the other savages you regularly interact with.

We have replaced some of their more advanced components with cruder devices so that you are not overly confused by their operation, and the rest have been fitted with anti-tinkering devices, so do not attempt to analyze or disassemble the ships. You would be unlikely to understand their inner workings regardless.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.c.xenophile:
We [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetSpeciesName] believe that [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are an important species for maintaining the balance and biodiversity of the galaxy, but we worry that your fleets are simply too weak for you to be able to stand against other, more aggressive species. To help you defend yourselves, we have decided to gift you a squadron of surplus escort ships.

We have replaced some of their more advanced components with technology that should be more familiar to [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural], so you should have no trouble operating them. Also, please do not attempt to analyze or disassemble the ships, we would not wish you to hurt yourselves!
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.c.machine.o: Custodian protocol 712-1 activated. Initiating war asset transfer to compliant organic civilization. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.c.machine.s: Custodian protocol 718-1 activated. Initiating war asset transfer to compliant synthetic intelligence. Message follows: <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>> <<ERROR: DATA BLOCK CORRUPTED>>
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.c.spirituali:
[Root.GetSpeciesName]! We have consulted the oracles and determined that your species has an important role to play in the great undertaking of the faith. To ensure that you can carry out this task, we have decided to gift you a squadron of surplus escort ships that should be more than adequate to destroy any primitive fleets of the other lesser races that might stand in your path.

Do not be tempted to tamper with the ships' systems, they may be older models of ours, but are still far beyond your current level of intellectual development.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.d.materialis:
[Root.GetSpeciesName], as a [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetSpeciesName] client the state of your fleets also reflects on us, and those crude hulks you call "warships" reflect very poorly indeed. To this end we have decided to gift you a surplus battlecruiser that should look most impressive to the other savages you regularly interact with.

We have replaced some of its more advanced components with cruder devices so that you are not overly confused by their operation, and the rest have been fitted with anti-tinkering devices, so do not attempt to analyze or disassemble the ship. You would be unlikely to understand its inner workings regardless.
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.d.xenophile:
We [FallenEmpireTaskOrigin.GetSpeciesName] believe that [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] are an important species for maintaining the balance and biodiversity of the galaxy, but we worry that your fleets are simply too weak for you to be able to stand against other, more aggressive species. To help you defend yourselves, we have decided to gift you one of our surplus battlecruisers.

We have replaced some of its more advanced components with technology that you should be more familiar to [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural], so you should have no trouble operating them. Also, please do not attempt to analyze or disassemble the ship, we would not wish you to hurt yourselves!
fallen_empires_tasks.2.desc.d.spirituali:
