leviathans.5.name: Leviathan Defeated
leviathans.5.desc: [leviathan_destroyer_country.GetName] has vanquished an ancient threat in the distant [leviathan_destroyed_system.GetName] system.
leviathans.98.name: Communications Established
leviathans.98.desc: We are receiving a transmission from the independent space station of the [From.GetName]! They appear to have successfully translated our language.
leviathans.99.name: Communications Established
leviathans.99.desc: After successfully translating their language, we have established communications with the independent space station of the [From.From.GetName].
leviathans.102.name: First Contact With the [From.GetName]
leviathans.102a.desc:
Welcome to XuraCorp!

We are a business conglomerate operating out of the [trader_system.GetName] system, specializing in trade - the very building blocks of civilization, as we like to say here at XuraCorp.

Please, do not hesitate to contact us if you're interested in making a good deal.
leviathans.102b.desc:
I speak on behalf of the Riggan Commerce Exchange. We have facilitated trade negotiations between interested parties on our station in the [trader_system.GetName] system for more than a thousand of your years.

If you happen to possess more resources than you need, we are more than willing to take it off your hands. You will be duly compensated, of course.
leviathans.102c.desc:
Well met, friends! I represent the Muutagan Merchant Guild, and let me be the first to welcome you to the [trader_system.GetName] system. Our organization consists of hundreds of independent Muutagan merchant captains who brave the spaceways in search of the next good deal.

At our facilities, you will be able to trade away some of your excess resources. Please contact us if you are interested in such an arrangement.
leviathans.100.a: We wish to make a trade.
leviathans.100.name: XuraCorp
leviathans.100a.desc: We do not discriminate against prospective buyers here at XuraCorp. Who are we to judge the morals of your star nation?
leviathans.100b.desc: Perhaps you need minerals for building warships. Perhaps you need them for building orphanages! Here at XuraCorp, we make it our business not to care!
leviathans.100c.desc: No questions asked - just quality resources, ready to be pumped right into the arteries of your industry!
leviathans.100d.desc: No refunds, I'm afraid. Company policy... It's out of my [xuracorp_country.species.GetHandNamePlural].
leviathans.100e.desc: Can we interest you in some off-brand distillation equipment? No? How about particulate detectors?
leviathans.100f.desc: You have reached XuraCorp. How may we help you?
leviathans.103.name: Riggan Commerce Exchange
leviathans.103a.desc: All of our clients remain anonymous.
leviathans.103b.desc: Where do our resources come from? Trust me... It's best for all involved parties - including the [Root.GetName] - if we keep that little bit of information to ourselves...
leviathans.103c.desc: We do not deal in slaves. Sorry, no exceptions.
leviathans.103d.desc: The Riggan Commerce Exchange greets you.
leviathans.103e.desc: A thousand years and we are still in business. If that doesn't speak to our credibility, I don't know what will.
leviathans.103f.desc: Several parties on our starbase have expressed interest in dealing with the [Root.GetName]. Shall we negotiate a deal?
leviathans.104.name: Muutagan Merchant Guild
leviathans.104a.desc: Thousands of years ago, the Muutagan Empire spanned a good portion of the galaxy. We are all that remain.
leviathans.104b.desc: It is said that a Muutagan can smell a good deal from a distance of twelve parsecs. This is an exaggeration... In truth, the distance is only eight parsecs.
leviathans.104c.desc: The Muutagan Merchant Guild welcomes you. Would you like to make a deal?
leviathans.104d.desc: A Muutagan and a Rixidaran walk into a bar... Never mind, this does not make for appropriate conversation. I beg your forgiveness.
leviathans.104e.desc: Greetings, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. You are here to trade with us, yes?
leviathans.104f.desc: The word "discount" is considered a profanity among my people. Please keep this in mind when engaging in conversation with us.
leviathans.105.c: We are interested in Strategic Resources.
trader_tt_strategicresource: Purchase monthly shipments of strategic resources.
leviathans.105.c.sr1: We already have a Riggan Trade Deal
leviathans.105.c.sr2: We already have a XuraCorp Trade Deal
leviathans.105.c.sr3: We already have a Muutagan Trade Deal
leviathans.105.c.trust:
Requires this Trader Enclave to have:
£ Opinion +50
leviathans.105.z: We wish to hire a consultant.
leviathans.110.a.reply: Thank you for your business. Please come again!
leviathans.110.b.reply: An excellent choice. You will not be disappointed by the quality of our minerals.
leviathans.110.c.reply: Big spender, eh? Looks like we can close early today!
leviathans.110.d: We were interested in something else...
leviathans.120.a.reply: Here are your credits. We have already arranged for the transfer of the minerals.
leviathans.120.b.reply: Excellent. Let us know if you want to offload more minerals in the future.
leviathans.120.c.reply: If only all of our customers traded with us in such bulk! Transferring credits to you now.
leviathans.125.desc.z1: We have a talented executive standing by, ready to migrate to the [Root.GetName] and get any of your sectors back out of the red. Entrust your £ Trade to an expert!
leviathans.125.desc.z1.gestalt:
We have a talented executive standing by, ready to... Hm. Are you sure?

'Buyer beware' is all well and good, but still: I feel obliged to inform you that our consultants really only specialize in £ Trade. I'm not sure they would be a good fit for you, given your... unusual relationship with that concept.
leviathans.125.z1.gestalt: We understand, and wish to proceed anyway.
leviathans.126.desc: Excellent! We are happy to share our skills with the [Root.GetName].
leviathans.126.desc.alt: Excellent! May we both profit from each other's... distinct approach to commerce.
already_hired_trader_official: We have already recruited a leader from the [enclave_country.GetName].
recruit_trader_leader: Adds a [enclave_country.GetAdj] Official with a Trader Liaison Trait to the Leaders pool.
requires_trader_enclave: Requires a Trader Enclave in the system.
sm_trader_proxy_office_desc: The Trader Enclaves enjoy special privileges on the Galactic Market, which can also benefit us.
requires_trade_enclave: Requires a Trader Enclave in the system.
leader_trait_enclave_trader_desc: Recruited from one of the independent merchant Enclaves, this leader is particularly adept at maximizing Trade.
leader_trait_xuracorp_liaison_desc: Recruited from XuraCorp, this leader holds shares in several Exotic Gas production facilities.
xuracorp_trader_desc: Recruited from XuraCorp, this leader holds shares in several Exotic Gas production facilities.
leader_trait_riggan_liaison_desc: Recruited from the Riggan Commerce Exchange, this leader spends their spare time dealing in Volatile Mote futures.
riggan_trader_desc: Recruited from the Riggan Commerce Exchange, this leader spends their spare time dealing in Volatile Mote futures.
leader_trait_muutagan_liaison_desc: Recruited from the Muutagan Merchant Guild, this leader owns several private Rare Crystal mines.
muutagan_trader_desc: Recruited from the Muutagan Merchant Guild, this leader owns several private Rare Crystal mines.
councilor_enclave_trader_desc: A liaison from one of the three hubs of galactic commerce sits on the council, granting insider information on brokerages across the galaxy.
councilor_enclave_trader_conditional_too: Leader has a Trader Liaison Trait.
unlocks_trader_council_position:
Allows the unlocking of Council Position:
$t$Trader Liaison
$tt$£ Empire Effects per Skill Level:
$ttt$£ Trade: +2%
$ttt$Market Fee -1%

Available for:
$t$£ Official

Requirements:
$t$Leader has a Trader Liaison Trait.
leviathans.131.desc:
The Volatile Mote is a prized Riggan condiment. It is renowned throughout the galaxy for its distinct flavor, which is unlike any other - and its explosiveness, which is also unlike any other. We sell it only to our most valued trading partners, among which we count the [Root.GetName].

If you can meet our modest price, we are willing to export Volatile Motes to you for a period of ten standard years.
leviathans.131.a.reply: You will not be sorry. Unless you consume too much spice, of course... Then there is a small chance that you will spontaneously combust. A very small chance, to be sure.
leviathans.130.desc:
This is a product that we here at XuraCorp are particularly proud of. Our Medical Division has recently begun refining a gas with unique properties that will significantly ease the often difficult process of adapting to a foreign planetary environment. It is however unlikely to be compatible with alien physiology!

We are willing to export our Exotic Gas to you for a period of ten standard years, after which the contract will have to be renegotiated.
leviathans.130.a.reply:
That's the XuraCorp way! Our freighters will begin making deliveries immediately.

By purchasing this product, you agree that XuraCorp cannot be held responsible for any adverse effects that may result from its use, including but not limited to: skin irritation, psychotic episodes, ocular discoloration, aggressive mutation, increased colonist suicide rates, precognitive trances, biosphere depletion, dangerous strangelet production, micro black hole generation, grain elevator explosions, societal collapse, mass extinction events, unexpected supernova detonations, the complete or partial destruction of your star nation, sudden gamma-ray bursts, time travel paradoxes, vacuum metastability events, universal entropy, the collapse of the space-time continuum...
leviathans.132.desc:
Shi'rakkat-Du - or Rare Crystals as they are known to those who are not of our species - have come to symbolize our entire civilization. When these "singing" crystals vibrate, they emit a unique musical tone that has a calming effect on most sapients.

Although we typically do not share the wonders of the Shi'rakkat-Du with outsiders, we are willing to make an exception in your case. If you can afford it, we are willing to export our crystals to you for a period of ten years.
leviathans.132.a.reply: Excellent. Our merchants will begin shipping the crystals to your planets at once. May the Shi'rakkat-Du sing to you.
leviathans.141.desc: Our fleet assets have destroyed the [From.GetName] headquarters. Efforts are well under way to recover as many valuables as possible from the shattered remnants of their starbase. We have gained a large amount of resources.
leviathans.142.a.desc: The corporate headquarters of XuraCorp in the [trader_system.GetName] system was recently destroyed. Reports suggest the attack force belongs to the [trader_destroyer.GetName]! The few surviving board members have declared bankruptcy, and the corporation's remaining assets are being liquidated.
leviathans.142.b.desc: The corporate headquarters of XuraCorp in the [trader_system.GetName] system was recently destroyed. According to our intel, this act was perpetrated by forces as yet unknown to us. The few surviving board members have declared bankruptcy, and the corporation's remaining assets are being liquidated.
leviathans.142.c.desc:
The corporate headquarters of XuraCorp in the [trader_system.GetName] system was recently destroyed. Reports suggest the attack force belongs to the [trader_destroyer.GetName]! The few surviving board members have declared bankruptcy, and the corporation's remaining assets are being liquidated.

Unfortunately, their production facilities for the Exotic Gas were destroyed along with the XuraCorp HQ, and we will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.142.d.desc:
The corporate headquarters of XuraCorp in the [trader_system.GetName] system was recently destroyed. According to our intel, this act was perpetrated by forces as yet unknown to us. The few surviving board members have declared bankruptcy, and the corporation's remaining assets are being liquidated.

Unfortunately, their production facilities for the Exotic Gas were destroyed along with the XuraCorp HQ, and we will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.142.desc.first: The corporate headquarters of XuraCorp in the [trader_system.GetName] system was recently destroyed.
leviathans.142.desc.known: Reports suggest the attack force belongs to the [trader_destroyer.GetName]!
leviathans.142.desc.unknown: According to our intel, this act was perpetrated by forces as yet unknown to us.
leviathans.142.desc.second: The few surviving board members have declared bankruptcy, and the corporation's remaining assets are being liquidated.
leviathans.142.desc.trade: Unfortunately, their production facilities for the Exotic Gas were destroyed along with the XuraCorp HQ, and we will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.142.b: We paid a lot of credits for that gas!
leviathans.143.a.desc: The starbase belonging to the Riggan Commerce Exchange has been destroyed in the [trader_system.GetName] system. This free outpost had facilitated trade between interstellar civilizations for over a millennium, but no longer. The forces of the [trader_destroyer.GetName] made certain of that.
leviathans.143.b.desc: The starbase belonging to the Riggan Commerce Exchange has been destroyed in the [trader_system.GetName] system. This free outpost had facilitated trade between interstellar civilizations for over a millennium, but no longer. Forces from an unidentified aggressor have made certain of that.
leviathans.143.c.desc:
The starbase belonging to the Riggan Commerce Exchange has been destroyed in the [trader_system.GetName] system. This free outpost had facilitated trade between interstellar civilizations for over a millennium, but no longer. The forces of the [trader_destroyer.GetName] made certain of that.

Unfortunately, this has also eliminated a source of Volatile Motes. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.143.d.desc:
The starbase belonging to the Riggan Commerce Exchange has been destroyed in the [trader_system.GetName] system. This free outpost had facilitated trade between interstellar civilizations for over a millennium, but no longer. Forces from an unidentified aggressor have made certain of that.

Unfortunately, this has also eliminated a source of Volatile Motes. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.143.desc.first: The starbase belonging to the Riggan Commerce Exchange has been destroyed in the [trader_system.GetName] system. This free outpost had facilitated trade between interstellar civilizations for over a millennium, but no longer.
leviathans.143.desc.known: The forces of the [trader_destroyer.GetName] made certain of that.
leviathans.143.desc.unknown: Forces from an unidentified aggressor have made certain of that.
leviathans.143.desc.trade: Unfortunately, this has also eliminated a source of Volatile Motes. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.143.b: We had paid in full for that spice!
leviathans.144.a.desc: Reports are coming in that the headquarters of the Muutagan Merchant Guild in the [trader_system.GetName] system has been pulverized. Forces belonging to the [trader_destroyer.GetName] appear to be behind this attack. The few surviving Muutagan merchant captains have scattered across the galaxy.
leviathans.144.b.desc: Reports are coming in that the headquarters of the Muutagan Merchant Guild in the [trader_system.GetName] system has been pulverized. The attackers appear to hail from an empire which is, as yet, unknown to us. The few surviving Muutagan merchant captains have scattered across the galaxy.
leviathans.144.c.desc:
Reports are coming in that the headquarters of the Muutagan Merchant Guild in the [trader_system.GetName] system has been pulverized. Forces belonging to the [trader_destroyer.GetName] appear to be behind this attack. The few surviving Muutagan merchant captains have scattered across the galaxy.

Unfortunately, this means an end to their production of the prized Rare Crystals. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.144.d.desc:
Reports are coming in that the headquarters of the Muutagan Merchant Guild in the [trader_system.GetName] system has been pulverized. The attackers appear to hail from an empire which is, as yet, unknown to us. The few surviving Muutagan merchant captains have scattered across the galaxy.

Unfortunately, this means an end to their production of the prized Rare Crystals. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.144.desc.first: Reports are coming in that the headquarters of the Muutagan Merchant Guild in the [trader_system.GetName] system has been pulverized.
leviathans.144.desc.known: Forces belonging to the [trader_destroyer.GetName] appear to be behind this attack.
leviathans.144.desc.unknown: The attackers appear to hail from an empire which is, as yet, unknown to us.
leviathans.144.desc.second: The few surviving Muutagan merchant captains have scattered across the galaxy.
leviathans.144.desc.trade: Unfortunately, this means an end to their production of the prized Rare Crystals. We will no longer have access to this strategic resource channel.
leviathans.144.b: Our crystals! This must not go unanswered!
leviathans.150.desc: Dearest customer, we regret to inform you that the trade deal we negotiated for the export of Exotic Gas to the worlds of the [Root.GetName] has run its course. We are of course more than willing to extend the deal for another ten years if you have the energy credits to spare...
leviathans.150.a: Very well. We wish to extend the deal.
leviathans.150.b: We can do without your gas for now.
leviathans.150.c: We can't afford to continue this deal.
leviathans.151.desc: We have reached the end of our agreement, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. We have shipped Volatile Motes to your worlds for ten years. Should we continue for another ten, or do you wish to end this arrangement?
leviathans.151.a: Let us continue. The motes must flow.
leviathans.151.b: We have no need of your spice for now.
leviathans.152.desc: The years just fly by, don't they, [Root.GetSpeciesName]? It has now been ten years since we arranged our trade deal for Rare Crystals. Do you wish to extend the deal for another decade?
leviathans.152.a: Yes. Let us continue this deal.
leviathans.152.b: We will pass on your crystals for now.
leviathans.156.desc: Your reckless attacks have put XuraCorp property and employees at risk. We have no choice but to terminate our current trade agreement. There will be no refunds.
leviathans.156.desc.notrade: Your reckless attack endangers XuraCorp property and employees alike. You would do well to remember that good customer relations go both ways.
leviathans.157a.desc: I'm afraid it's against company policy to do business with pirates.
leviathans.157b.desc: You are not an acceptable customer.
leviathans.157c.desc: We have nothing to discuss with you.
leviathans.159.desc: Your attacks against our station are intolerable! You are cut off, do you understand? You may consider our trade agreement null and void.
leviathans.160a.desc: You are a nation of bandits and cutthroats. We will have nothing to do with you.
leviathans.162.desc: Ah, so the pirates shows their true colors! You can forget about our trade deals! No Muutagan will do business with the [Root.GetName] again.
leviathans.162.desc.notrade: You dare to attack us?! Know this, pirates: we do not stand for such barbarism.
leviathans.163a.desc: You are terrorists! Do not think we will forget your aggression against our people.
leviathans.163b.desc: You will find that Muutagans have very long memories, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. We never forget a slight.
leviathans.163c.desc: We will never trust the [Root.GetName] again.
leviathans.295.desc:
A visitor! This is a joyous occasion indeed! Oh, forgive my manners. I believe introductions are in order. We are the Artisan Troupe.

Our members have dedicated their lives to the pursuit of art, music, culture and all the other things which makes existence bearable to a sapient being. Please, if you would like to share in the wonder of our creations, do not hesitate to contact us!
leviathans.300.name: Enclave: The Artisan Troupe
leviathans.300a.desc: Hm? Oh, please excuse my reverie. Sometimes this muse of mine is simply... overpowering. Is there anything else we can do for you?
leviathans.300b.desc: Have you ever stopped to wonder at the sheer majesty of it all? Here we are, and there you are. What fantastic odds! I feel a ballad coming on.
leviathans.300c.desc: Yes? Hello? Ah, it's you! Forgive me; I was stuck chasing a particularly elusive stanza. How can I help?
leviathans.300.a: We want to commission an art piece.
leviathans.300.a.reply: Sadly we cannot offer any more, lest we come to believe that you didn't appreciate the ones you already purchased. We have our integrity to think about, you see.
leviathans.300.b: We wish to become your patron.
leviathans.300.b.stop: We wish to cancel our patronage.
leviathans.300.b.reply:
Oh, I see. That is unfortunate, [root.GetSpeciesAdj], but we thank you for your initial support.

Goodbye.
leviathans.300.c: Organize a festival across our worlds.
leviathans.300.c.allow:
Requires the Artisan Troupe to have:
£ Opinion +50
leviathans.300.c.outofstock: We may only host one Festival of Worlds every 20 years.
leviathans.300.d: Tell us more about your troupe.
leviathans.300.d.reply:
We are the Artisan Troupe. The troupe consists of several stations inhabited by creatives from many worlds, all unified in the desire to create new beauty in these safe havens. They bring their ideas and methods from all around the galaxy, and together we uncover the ultimate expressions of the self!

We provide many services to those who wish to enjoy art. If you help sponsor our work we might even be willing to organize larger events for your people!
leviathans.300.f: We want to invest in a Ministry of Culture.
leviathans.301.desc: The Artisan Troupe won't respond to our hails.
leviathans.301.desc.unknown: Translations aside, once we exchanged our information with [From.GetName] they closed down all channels and refused to speak to us.
leviathans.304a.desc: Thank you so very much! Ah, such a noble act it is to help bring more art into the universe. We are confident you will be satisfied.
leviathans.304b.desc: The stars shine that bit more brightly by your actions here today!
leviathans.304c.desc: We knew there was something special about you [root.GetSpeciesAdj]. Truly, you are beings of refined taste.
leviathans.305.desc: Fabulous! We'd be glad to entrust you with one of our creations. It is sure to bring joy to the people of your empire.
leviathans.305.a.tooltip:
Gain access to an £ Exhibit Art Monument Decision that can be enacted on one planet with the following effects:
£ Amenities +15%
Immigration Pull: +50%
leviathans.305.a.reply:
Excellent! The piece will be sent to your storage facility post-haste. Simply ask your planetary administration to enact the Decision on any planet you wish.

We humbly thank you for your patronage.
leviathans.330.desc: Organizing a festival of that scale would require all of our artists to bring their talent to bear. Not an easy job, nor a cheap one.
leviathans.330.a.reply: Excellent! We will be delighted to create this magnificent Festival of Worlds!
leviathans.310.desc: That would be very helpful, allowing us to try new ideas and take more risks in our creation process. We have a ten year program with a one-time up-front cost.
leviathans.310.a.tooltip: Gain £ Opinion +1 with the Artisan Troupe each month
leviathans.310.a.reply: Thank you very much! Now, with your generous contribution, we will be able to expand on the concept of art itself! We will of course also send out a regular newsletter to all patrons.
leviathans.307.desc: Our economy cannot support being a patron of the Artisan Troupe anymore. They will no longer receive funding from our empire. This will surely sour our relationship with the enclave.
leviathans.307.a.tooltip: Removes the empire modifier Patron of the Arts
leviathans.335.name: The Outrage
leviathans.335.desc:
The Festival of Worlds organized by the Artisan Troupe had, for a time, brought joy to the people of the [Root.GetName]. Alas, it was not meant to last.
On [this_planet.GetName], festival activities have resulted in a huge crowd stampeding and killing thousands of citizens. It is not clear what circumstances led to this tragic loss of life, but there is now growing resentment towards our administration and the festival's organizers alike.
leviathans.336.name: The Joy
leviathans.336.desc: Due to the overabundance of happiness being spread by the Festival of Worlds, some of the event's organizers have begun to fall in love with our way of life. They claim they wish to remain here; to settle down and become a part of our empire.
leviathans.337.name: The Betrayal
leviathans.337.desc:
The Festival of Worlds has abruptly stopped. The Artisan Troupe has packed their bags and left, without saying a word about why.

Thorough searches of their campsites and arenas have revealed only that a substantial quantity of resources has disappeared.
leviathans.337.a.tooltip: The Artisan Troupe will refuse any communique for 10 years.
leviathans.337.b.tooltip: The Artisan Troupe are forgiven for their transgressions.
leviathans.315.desc:
Esteemed [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName]: a decade ago the [Root.GetName] pledged to support the Artisan Troupe, and so you have.

The time of your patronage is coming to an end, but it would be remiss of us not to ask: would you care to renew your subscription to the finest arts and crafts in the galaxy?
leviathans.321.name: Patron Newsletter
leviathans.321.desc: Here follows the latest newsletter for all our patrons:
leviathans.321.desc.a:
Sadly nothing much has been produced in the enclave. Most of the artists have fallen into a deep melancholy from where no inspiration can be drawn. The mood is dire, but hopeful. Creation takes time, after all.

Any donations that might help the group rekindle their interest in the material plane would be of tremendous help.
leviathans.321.desc.b:
The enclave has been busy the last couple of months. Our halls are abuzz with a new kind of technology invented by a resident, capable of transmitting sensations of smell to a user. This remarkable piece of machinery will surely change everything.

In order to further develop this idea we will require more donations.
leviathans.321.desc.c:
The enclave is in a frisky mood. The creation of the Scentilus Rift has caused many an artist to shift their primary focus to creating new experiences for it. So far the most noteworthy to come out of this endeavor is an orchestral piece conveyed via scent.

Our work continues and any donations would be gladly accepted.
leviathans.321.desc.d:
We have abandoned the attempts to create scent-centered media. It was a foolish idea and has brought nothing but wasted time and unpleasant odors.

In order to find our way back again we will need donations from our trusted patrons. We thank you for your continued support!
leviathans.321.c: We cannot afford to donate now.
leviathans.321.b: We wish to unsubscribe from this newsletter.
leviathans.322.name: Patrons with Benefits
leviathans.322.desc:
Greetings, patron [Root.GetRulerName]! We have come up with a gorgeous new type of architecture, specifically tuned to improve crowds' understanding of one another - a Ministry of Culture. It functions thanks to a mix of using the populace's subconscious bias against each other and art, then smashing it all and presenting a new form of unity.

Would you like to purchase this building? It will surely prove useful to binding your empire together. And it's a bargain, if I may say so myself!
leviathans.322.a.tooltip:
Gain access to a £ Ministry of Culture with the following Empire effects:
Artist Jobs: +3
£ $concept_unity$ from £ Jobs: +15%
leviathans.322.a.tooltip.hive:
Gain access to a £ Ministry of Culture with the following Empire effects:
Coordinator Jobs: +3
£ $concept_unity$ from £ Jobs: +15%
leviathans.322.a.tooltip.machine:
Gain access to a £ Ministry of Culture with the following Empire effects:
[evaluator.GetName] Jobs: +3
£ $concept_unity$ from £ Jobs: +15%
leviathans.323.name: Lackluster Update
leviathans.323.desc: We apologize, patron [Root.GetRulerName]: we have sadly reached something of a creative roadblock. The enclave is in disarray and we have nothing to offer at this time. We thank you for your patronage, as always.
leviathans.324.name: Broken Artistry
leviathans.324.desc: Greetings, patron [Root.GetRulerName]. We have recently been forced to scrap most of our technical equipment due to a major malfunction. Would the materials and scrap be of any use to you, by any chance?
leviathans.324.b: We will repair it for you.
leviathans.325.desc: We are exceptionally sorry to hear that, o patron! Without the newsletter we won't be able to keep you up-to-date on our latest accomplishments...
leviathans.345.name: The Ministry of Culture
leviathans.345.desc: Ah, the Ministry of Culture... It was designed to challenge divergent ideas and promote greater unity throughout your empire through the medium of art. A true masterpiece, if I may say so myself.
leviathans.345.a.reply:
Excellent! The piece will be sent to your storage facility immediately. Simply ask your builders to erect it on any planet you wish.
We humbly thank you for your patronage.
leviathans.352.desc: We have received a transmission from the Artisan Troupe. One of their stations has been destroyed!
leviathans.353.desc: We received a distress signal from the headmaster of the Artisan Troupe. Their last station and cultural haven has been destroyed. There were few survivors, and the troupe is essentially no more.
leviathans.354.desc: After having destroyed the Artisan Troupe's station we found many resources to salvage from the wreckage. Donations, gifts and creations stacked in its halls now drift in space, ready for the taking.
leviathans.354.desc.unknown: After destroying the station facility floating in the [station_system.GetName] system, we have found plenty of valuable resources amongst its remains.
leviathans.500.name: Curators
leviathans.500a.desc: Perhaps you are wondering about the significance of the shapes you see on the mural behind me. That is a good question with a very interesting answer! The fee for this information is 15 quadrillion energy credits.
leviathans.500b.desc: You have reached the Curators. How may we assist you?
leviathans.500c.desc: Did you know that this conversation is being closely monitored by entities from seven different subspace realms? Alas, I fear that the technology to communicate with them is too far beyond the present capabilities of your civilization to do you any good.
leviathans.500d.desc: Fear not. We have updated our archives with information about the [Root.GetName] for future generations. You will be remembered long after the inevitable collapse of your star nation.
leviathans.500e.desc: There is so much I wish I could tell you, but I simply can't do it for free. This space station requires a lot of energy to operate... we must consider our overhead.
leviathans.500f.desc: Greetings on behalf of the Curator order. Was there something you wanted?
leviathans.500g.desc: As always, it is a pleasure doing business with your government. Can we interest you in some technology?
leviathans.500h.desc: It is good to see you. I am sure we can come to some sort of mutually beneficial agreement before this day is over.
leviathans.500i.desc: Knowledge in the wrong gripping appendages can be dangerous, but what can we do? We need energy to keep the lights on...
leviathans.500j.desc: There is much that you do not yet know, [Root.GetSpeciesName]. Please... let us educate you about the universe.
leviathans.500k.desc: We possess detailed star charts of the entire galaxy, gathered by explorers from a hundred different races. Perhaps they would be of interest to you?
leviathans.500l.desc: Knowledge is everything. It must be preserved.
leviathans.502.name: First Contact with the [curator_enclave_country.GetName]
leviathans.502a.desc:
Greetings, star travelers. We are the Curators.

Our ancient order was established eons ago by the various galactic powers in ascendancy at the time. We were dedicated towards the preservation of all knowledge, in an effort to safeguard the galaxy from descending into yet another dark age of mass extinctions and barbarism.

We failed.

Few of us remain today, but we are no less committed to our sacred mission than our predecessors were. We are willing to share some of our knowledge with you... for a price.
leviathans.502b.desc: Well met, explorers. You are speaking to the [curator_enclave_country.GetName]. Perhaps you are already familiar with the tenets of our ancient order. Like our esteemed colleagues in the other Curator enclaves, we are willing to trade provided that you can meet our rates.
leviathans.500.a: We are interested in procuring new star charts.
leviathans.500.b: Can you aid us in our research?
leviathans.500.b.alreadyaided: The Curators are already improving our research capabilities.
leviathans.500.c: Tell us about the mysteries of the universe.
leviathans.500.d: Could we recruit one of your scientists?
leviathans.500.d.alreadyrecruited: We already employ a Curator scientist.
leviathans.500.d.opinion:
Requires the Curators to have:
£ Opinion +50
leviathans.500.e: Can you share the fundamental principles of knowledge?
leviathans.500.e.alreadyshared: We have already shared the Curator principles.
leviathans.500.e.opinion:
Requires the Curators to have:
£ Opinion +50
leviathans.500.h: Can you tell us about your other customers?
leviathans.500.i: What do you know about the L-Gates?
leviathans.500.i.tooltip.noclue: It takes the [curator_enclave_country.GetName] approximately a decade to identify each new L-Gate Insight.
leviathans.500.j: Can you help us populate our Vivarium?
leviathans.500.j.opinion:
Requires the Curators to have:
£ Opinion +80
leviathans.500.k: Can you assist us with our Collection?
leviathans.500.k.reply.reward_unavailabl: We apologize, but we have nothing to offer you at this time. Try collecting and displaying more $specimens$. Perhaps we can then share our expertise.
leviathans.500.k.reply.over:
We apologize, but we have nothing left to offer you! Your collection is truly magnificent. We are honored to have you as a partner in our galaxy.

You are an asset to the preservation of knowledge.
leviathans.504a.desc: Our order thanks you, esteemed customer.
leviathans.504b.desc: Thank you, [root.GetSpeciesAdj]. Clarity and curiosity be with you.
leviathans.504c.desc: A pleasure doing business with you. How else might our keen insights and inestimable records be of service to you?
leviathans.506.d: What else did you have to offer?
leviathans.507.name: Enclave: The Curators Research Aid
leviathans.507.desc:
Of course. We are prepared to offer you limited access to our extensive databanks for a period of ten standard years. This should provide a significant boost to the research efforts of your planetside Research Labs.

We will require compensation for this service, naturally, but I think you'll find that our prices are very reasonable.
leviathans.507.a: We would like to purchase this service.
leviathans.507.a.reply: A wise choice, that future generations of [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural] will no doubt laud you for.
leviathans.508.name: Mysteries
leviathans.508.desc: There are exceedingly powerful entities lurking within certain star systems in our galaxy. At great cost in both lives and resources, Curator agents have painstakingly gathered knowledge that should make these beings easier to deal with the next time you encounter them.
leviathans.508.a.reply: This might interest you... We have marked a star system in your Situation Log.
leviathans.506.f: How would our current fleet fare against it in battle?
leviathans.5106.f1.reply:
Poorly. Very poorly.

Wait a second, you're not actually thinking of...? My goodness, with the ships you have? It... it would be a slaughter!
leviathans.5106.f2.reply: I would strongly advise against it. Your attacks would likely be more of an annoyance than a threat.
leviathans.5106.f3.reply: Hmmm, yes... Yes, I suppose you might actually stand a chance. If you combined your entire fleet... It would not be an easy victory, mind you, but one that is at least within the realm of possibility.
leviathans.5106.f4.reply: Yours is a mighty fleet, comparable to some of the greatest armadas recorded in the annals of the Curator Order. Victory is certainly within your reach.
leviathans.500.f: We would like to establish a mutual Think Tank.
leviathans.511.name: Think Tank
leviathans.511.desc: Yes... yes, such a facility would benefit the advancement of Galactic Science. You may build this Think Tank at your starbase in the system you share with us. Our Curators will come to mingle with your scientists.
leviathans.511.a: Excellent. What else do you have to offer?
leviathans.511.a.tooltip: We can now build the Curator Think Tank Starbase Building in the [curator_system.GetName] system.
leviathans.550.name: Voidspawn
leviathans.550.desc: If our suspicions hold true, the Voidspawn is far away from home. We believe it is the progeny of an extragalactic predator of unthinkable proportions: one that stalks the void of space in search of its prey. Though we have never before encountered a live specimen, we have heard tales of the destruction and chaos grown Voidspawn leave in their wake. It is said that worlds fester under their shadow.
leviathans.550.a.reply:
From what we can tell, the mother lays its planet-sized eggs in orbit of a star, where they then incubate for thousands of years, sometimes even long enough to develop an atmosphere and organic life.

They feed off of living matter, and adult Voidspawn are said to exert a strange influence on all living things. Fortunately this spawn seems to have been abandoned by its parents.

Perhaps it would be best to stifle the creature while it is still young and vulnerable?
leviathans.550.b.reply: We have never heard of a grown Voidspawn being defeated in battle, but this one is newly hatched. The Voidspawn projects corrosive spittle and spikes that can burn through the thickest of armor, but applying a protective acid-proof coating may slow its progress. We will help you make it. The Voidspawn is a threat to us all.
leviathans.555.name: Scavenger
leviathans.555.desc:
Ah, the scrap bot. The Scavenger is a curious construct from a lost age. Endlessly it searches through the debris fields of the galaxy, welding the guns, engines, and materials scavenged from countless derelicts onto its own hull. Its mass and firepower have been increasing in such a fashion for centuries, with no sign of relenting.

No-one knows if there is an upper limit to how massive it could become, given enough time and scrap to work with.
leviathans.555.a.reply:
Unfortunately, no definitive data regarding the Scavenger's origin is known to exist. Some researchers believe it to be a malfunctioning scrap collection service machine from a lost empire, its purpose long since muddled by hardware degradation. Others believe it to have originated as a single microscopic nanobot, programmed to endlessly build itself larger and stronger by exploiting its environment. Still others reckon it may have started out as a robotic ship's captain; the sole survivor of an intergalactic battle waged millennia ago. Perhaps its reasoning systems were irrevocably damaged by the sudden destruction of its entire civilization.

Of course, this is all just speculation.
leviathans.555.b.reply:
Over the years there have been many attempts to communicate with it, or else to alter the programming of the Scavenger. Unfortunately, most of those expeditions ended up part of the cosmic scrap yards where the Scavenger Bot dwells. Only those who were able to outrun it survived.

The Scavenger has welded enough heavy artillery onto its patchwork frame to single-handedly destroy an entire nation's fleet - an event that may already have occurred on more than one occasion. Of course, any such destructive encounters would only have served to further strengthen the Scavenger, providing it with more ship components to repurpose.
leviathans.555.c: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.555.c.reply:
As you may have surmised: the Scavenger was not built according to any definitive, pre-existing schematics. As a result, some of its parts fit together... less than optimally, leading to a discrete number of structural weaknesses. Of course, to the uninitiated, most of these are obscured from view - but our advanced sensors have managed to isolate them.

Tell your fleets to focus fire on the indicated sections of the Scavenger's hull, and it should substantially reduce the amount of damage the construct is able to take before collapsing.
leviathans.555.bb: Remind us about attempts at communicating with it.
leviathans.556.name: Tiyanki Matriarch
leviathans.556.desc: Magnificent, is she not? A wizened old Matriarch, her hide bleached and hardened by the eons, her tentacles capable of snapping the hulls of battleships like oyster shells. Decades ago, our researchers heard rumors of a captain sworn to hunt the Matriarch to the ends of the galaxy. However, considering her continued existence, we cannot imagine he met with success.
leviathans.556.a: Why is the Matriarch so much larger than other Tiyanki?
leviathans.556.a.reply:
Her incredible size is an anomaly, to be sure. We believe the Matriarch is a wanderer from another galaxy in deep space, where a species of Tiyanki far greater in size and strength diverged evolutionarily from the Tiyanki found in our own.

Of course, it is also possible the Matriarch is simply suffering from an advanced form of gigantism - though this would fail to explain her extended lifespan.
leviathans.556.b: What do you know about the captain hunting the Matriarch?
leviathans.556.b.reply: Very little. It is quite possible the captain chased the Matriarch here from another galaxy. Though why one would be foolish enough to challenge a creature capable of destroying entire fleets with just one vessel is beyond us.
leviathans.556.c: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.556.c.reply:
The Matriarch is formidable, but not indestructible. While her armored hide protects her from a wide range of projectiles, she carries with her a remarkable weakness.

There is a massive proton torpedo lodged in her back: a wound from a recent battle that has healed poorly. While seemingly defective, our scans of the torpedo suggest it can still be detonated, if agitated with a specific energy pulse.

We will transmit the details to you now.
leviathans.556.aa: Remind us why the Matriarch is larger than other Tiyanki.
leviathans.556.bb: Remind us about the captain hunting the Matriarch.
leviathans.558.name: The Toxic God
leviathans.558.desc: The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. We have heard that it has been tracked to the [toxic_god_system.GetName] system.
leviathans.558.desc.knights:
The Toxic Entity is an elusive being. It has roamed the galaxy for millennia, occasionally choosing to spurt venom at worlds in what we can only imagine is a natural stage of its life cycle. But you already knew this, of course!

We are sorry, but we cannot help you find its present whereabouts - it has not been spotted by any of our contacts for quite some time.
leviathans.558.AA: Remind us what you know of it.
leviathans.558.A.reply: It is not documented where the Toxic Entity came from. The first sighting was several thousand years ago, and since then it has been seen every few centuries. Some have called it a deity, but that is for you to decide. What we can tell you is that it is an extremely formidable organic being with arthropoid characteristics. Reports suggest that it is sufficiently large that an entire ecosystem has developed on it, though acquiring samples of its biology has proved understandably challenging.
leviathans.558.BB: Remind us how we can fight it.
leviathans.558.B.reply: There have been few survivors to its past encounters. According to reports, its corrosive poisons are able to burn through all forms of armor. Shields are only slightly more useful. Furthermore, the creatures living on its back will supposedly act as an attack swarm when it is threatened. We can only suggest you approach it with overwhelming force.
leviathans.559.name: $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$
leviathans.559.desc: That rather twitchy automaton is a relative newcomer to the galaxy, but don't be fooled by such novelty. The $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$'s creators were counted among the finest engineers in their sector even before they were assimilated by a tyrannical machine. We do not know what harsh fate has befallen the machine consciousness since then, but if the Sentinel's agonized writhing is anything to go by: the whole situation appears quite volatile. Tread carefully, should you decide to slake your curiosity.
leviathans.559.desc.unplugged:
Forgive my impertinence, but I assumed you would know more about it than we do! That rather twitchy automaton is a newcomer compared to what we usually study here, but is no less fearsome an opponent.

We know that even before they were assimilated, the engineers behind the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ were counted among the finest in their sector. That warship is therefore not to be underestimated. What is less clear to us is how the vessel became so detached from the [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]. We gather from the Sentinel's agonized writhing that the whole situation remains quite volatile. Would you agree with assessment, [root.GetSpeciesName]?
leviathans.559.a: You say it is guarding something?
leviathans.559.a.reply: Indeed, though we do not know precisely what. Some of our contacts believe the Sentinel is defending whatever remains of the splintered [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetName]; others suggest the planet itself holds some treasure. What we do know is that this warship was built more robustly than any of its [origin_unplugged_assimilator_empire.GetAdj] peers by an order of magnitude. Whatever it is protecting out there, the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ perseveres despite clear signs of distress, or perhaps even agony.
leviathans.559.b: We prefer not to talk about it.
leviathans.559.b.reply:
Quite understandable. We are merely curious.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
leviathans.559.c: Where can we find this entity?
leviathans.559.c.reply:
Seeing as how you are one of our more trustworthy clients... I can tell you the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ was last seen guarding the [origin_unplugged_machine_legacy_core.GetName] system.

Given how much we still do not know about this ferociously troubled warship, rest assured: we shall observe the particulars of your encounter with keen interest!
unplugged_curator_poi_opus_sentinel_desc: We bought these coordinates from the Curators, who report the $NAME_Opus_Sentinel$ was last seen in this area.
leviathans.590.name: Hire Scientist
leviathans.590.desc:
We are willing to pledge the services of one of our most brilliant scientists to your cause. This is not an offer we make to just anyone, you understand!

A suitable... donation will of course be necessary, before traveling arrangements can be made.
leviathans.590.a: Of course. You shall have your donation.
leviathans.590.a.reply: Excellent. You will now have unfettered access to one of the greatest minds of our time!
leviathans.590.tt_scientist: We may only employ one Curator scientist at a time.
leviathans.598.name: Shared Principles
leviathans.598.desc:
We are willing to infuse your collective with the fundamental principles of knowledge. A serious procedure, and one only available to a shared consciousness.

Even for us, it is no easy thing to achieve. The cost is not insignificant. But of all commodities, knowledge remains the most precious.
leviathans.598.a: Of course. You shall have your donation.
leviathans.598.tt_principles: The fundamental principles of the Curators have already been shared with us.
leviathans.599.name: Buy Intelligence
leviathans.599.desc:
Since you are one of our trusted customers, we are able to divulge to you certain information on our... less favored clients. What you do with this information is entirely up to you, of course.

Who do you want to know about?
leviathans.599.b: What do you know of the [curator_customer_2.GetName]?
leviathans.599.c: We wish to know about the [curator_customer_3.GetName].
leviathans.599.d: The [curator_customer_4.GetName] is of interest to us.
leviathans.599.yes.reply: Excellent. The information will be transferred to you immediately via the most secure interstellar datalink in the galaxy.
leviathans.600.name: L-Gate Insights
leviathans.600.desc:
The L-Gates? Yes, like the other Gateways they predate even the oldest Stagnant Ascendancy, but we are sure you have figured that out already.

Why are they different? Where do they lead? We have opted not to delve too deeply into those particular mysteries - "thrice bitten, zero-point-seventeen shy" you know how it is - but we are willing to share some recent revelations that just might be related.

For a price.
leviathans.596.desc:
It would appear that we grossly overestimated your capacity to act as a civilized nation. Strange... We are usually able to identify the violent ones at an early stage.

We have severed your access to our databanks, of course.
leviathans.597a.desc: You fool! By attacking us, you are condemning future generations to lives of low-tech misery!
leviathans.597b.desc: Your base instincts compelled you to attack us, and now you must pay the price. We will never share our knowledge with the [Root.GetName] again.
leviathans.597c.desc: We had so much to offer you [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural], and yet you would throw it all away. Neo-barbarian scum!
leviathans.597d.desc: You have been declared an enemy of the entire Curator Order.
leviathans.510.name: Ether Drake
leviathans.510.desc: The Ether Drake species is ill-suited to life in our universe. The last dragon is strong, but not invincible.
leviathans.510.a.reply:
By all accounts, the Ether Drakes predate all galactic civilization. There once were multitudes, but their race has been wasting away for eons.

They are ill-suited to life, here and now. Something about the physical laws of the universe does not agree with them, like they evolved in another reality. They did, in fact. We believe that they are but the last dregs of a universe that ended before ours began, the sole survivors of some "big crunch."

The dragon not far from here is the last of its kind in the galaxy, perhaps the universe.
leviathans.510.b: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.510.b.reply:
Its scales respond to percussive rhythms. To be more precise, certain frequencies have a relaxing effect on the sub-dermal musculature controlling the positioning and shock absorption of their scale plates. A reflex that once played a key role in Ether Drake social interactions, it is now a clear and obvious weakness.

Adjusting the firing pattern of your vessels according to a particular rhythm will greatly increase the damage you can inflict on the last dragon. It was never meant for our age - put it out of its misery.
leviathans.515.name: Enigmatic Fortress
leviathans.515.desc: It is the kind of absurd, massive and self-perpetuating construction that you don't see built anymore. Maybe that is for the best.
leviathans.515.a.reply: The Fortress has been defeated before, but it always recovers. Some of the ancient empires of this galaxy were driven to madness by their vain efforts to unlock its deeper secrets, or else to permanently destroy it. It appears so focused on maintaining itself that we doubt it has any other serious purpose.
leviathans.515.b.reply: It can and it has been, although that attempt is now nearly forgotten. The fortress maintains only partial power while in shutdown, however it will attempt to draw power from nearby sources in order to jump-start its systems again. Proceed with caution.
leviathans.515.c.reply: Whoever they were, they must have been fond of puzzles and enigmas. The only items to have been recovered from the fortress are strange metal shapes: components of perplexing contraptions which seem designed to be rearranged into more satisfying forms. Those who brought them back did so because they failed, and they barely escaped with their lives. Many others didn't.
leviathans.515.d.reply:
The power system must have been built at a time between initial construction of the hull, and installation of its defense systems. The system's recovery method is unknown to us, but we have discovered that the fortress contains large quantities of dark matter. That substance and its relationship to black holes are key to understanding how the fortress has lasted so long.

No one has ever found the source of its power, but it is likely to be extremely volatile.
leviathans.515.dd: Remind us how it is powered.
leviathans.520.name: Stellar Devourer
leviathans.520.desc: The Stellar Devourer is a new parasite on the galactic hunting ground, not unlike your empire in many ways. It was born out of fear and nuclear fusion. It roams the galaxy, submerging itself into stars, feasting on them from within. And it certainly does not like being disturbed.
leviathans.520.a.reply:
The star-feaster is a rare breed. A new type of beast of unknown origin. The accounts we have collected are few and sparse with intel. Few sources even have firsthand experience with the thing.

All our data points to the same fact, however: it is a terror that brings nothing but ruin.

The Stellar Devourer is capable of feeding off of fusion itself. Our very educated guess is that its biology is the result of some outer-dimensional fusing of dark matter and solar matter. It dives into stars, feasting on their innards in order to fuel its own, internal fusion reactor. It brings death to all systems it reaches. Either they shatter like ice after its banquet, or they burn from being exposed to a second sun from within the being's belly.

It wants to feed, and it will stop at nothing to get its share. When you gaze at it, what you see is a survivor's raw fury.
leviathans.520.b.reply:
The only thing we know for sure is that the collected core is the most important aspect of the Stellar Devourer. The creature desperately needs to keep its furnace burning, lest the cold void of space reaches its vital organs deeper within and makes it collapse in on itself. Without that stellar matter, it is nothing.

You can use this to your advantage. Calibrate your weapons to our specifications and you can then home in on the very membranes that hold the Devourer's digestive system together. Wound it and you will see its innards gush out across the solar system.
leviathans.525.name: Dimensional Horror
leviathans.525.desc: Our instruments monitored the immense energy surge when this entity pierced its way into our realm of existence.
leviathans.525.a.reply:
It is a creature of pure malice, born in a dimension that bears more than a striking resemblance to the realm of Hell as described by many galactic religions. What we are seeing is but a small part of a greater whole - the creature in its entirety is multitudes larger.

It is very fortunate that it was unable to complete its transition into our universe. Had it been successful, the creature would likely have consumed all life in the galaxy by now.
leviathans.525.b: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.525.b.reply: The dimensional portal that it spawned from is its greatest weakness - without it, it cannot exist in our universe. We have identified several weak points in the portal's energy matrix that could be exploited by conventional weapons. Transmitting targeting coordinates now.
leviathans.530.name: Asteroid Hiver
leviathans.530.desc: These annoying pests were once far more prevalent in our galaxy. There was a time when you couldn't cruise through a random asteroid belt without the little beasts swarming around your ship!
leviathans.530.a.reply:
They are an aggressively territorial silicon-based life form. Although they once posed a significant threat to spacefaring civilizations, their numbers have been severely culled over the last 500,000 years and the surviving members of their species are fairly reclusive.

Despite rumors to the contrary, there is no evidence that they possess anything that could be described as sapient intelligence. They tend to nest inside asteroids, and they will attack anything which is perceived as a threat.
leviathans.530.b: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.530.b.reply:
The creatures have a tendency to coat their asteroid nests with some kind of unknown substance that acts as a potent armor against ship-based weapons. This substance is not perfectly applied across the entire surface of the asteroid, however.

With the targeting data we are transmitting to you now, your ships will be able to focus their fire on unprotected surface areas, greatly increasing the damage they inflict.
leviathans.535.name: Infinity Machine
leviathans.535.desc:
Ah yes, the chromatic being from long ago. We have studied it for as long as our order has existed. As have several civilizations before us.

This machine is beyond ancient. For all we know, it has always been. And yet, all it does is orbit that black hole. It's fascinating to us, but we understand if it is too much for you to grasp.
leviathans.535.a.reply: The Infinity Machine, as you so bluntly call it, is impervious to extraction. No information comes out from it. No hacker or engineer in the entire galaxy has been able to see through its shiny exterior to gain a glimpse of the knowledge it so obviously withholds from us. We are at a loss. We neither know what it is for, nor what it aims to do once it's done.
leviathans.535.b.reply:
There is perhaps one thing you could do to destroy it. We have been unable to retrieve information from it, but its hull is breakable. Miners have tried to gather resources from it at numerous times, only to come back with their ships barely holding together. But they did find something interesting: The Infinity Machine is not as rigid as it seems.

It is made of a material capable of changing its characteristics. Density, flexibility, heat, you name it! It can analyze damage in real time and change its shell to compensate, thus making itself harder to take down. Change your frequencies, adjust the thermal output of your missiles, whatever you people lumber around with, and keep changing them. That way you can get past its adaptive capabilities.
leviathans.540.name: Automated Dreadnought
leviathans.540.desc: A sad story. Its masters have been dead for millions of years, but this massive warship continues to stand vigil over the broken rubble of their empire.
leviathans.540.a.reply:
It was one of several flagships belonging to an unusually powerful interstellar empire that flourished in a small region of our galaxy some seven million years ago. As is so often the case, that empire was brought to a sudden and violent end at the hands of its neighbors in a series of very destructive wars.

The dreadnought you have encountered is the last of its kind, and it continues to dutifully patrol its assigned system despite the death of its crew. Many attempts have been made throughout the ages to put the old warship to its final rest - none successful.
leviathans.540.b: Tell us how to defeat it.
leviathans.540.b.reply: The dreadnought was designed to operate with a large crew, but it now relies exclusively on automated systems to function. This makes the ship especially vulnerable to attacks that disrupt the relay nodes used by its central computer.
leviathans.545.name: Wraith
leviathans.545.desc: Spectral Wraiths are disturbing creatures, if they are creatures at all. We consider them a rare and extraordinarily efficient natural disaster.
leviathans.545.a: What do you know about these disasters?
leviathans.545.a.reply:
They appear to be illusions of light, but when you get close, it quickly grows apparent that they are far from illusory.

Paradoxically, in that appearance lies the key to their defeat. Their relationship with the visible spectrum of light is their strength, but it diminishes when they approach a light source of a similar frequency. Pay close attention to the color of the Wraith.
leviathans.545.b.reply: Red Wraiths have a frequency of 450THz. Their light is synchronized with that of a Class M Star. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with red dwarfs.
leviathans.545.c.reply: Yellow Wraiths have a frequency of 520THz. Their light is synchronized with that of a Class G Star. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with yellow dwarfs.
leviathans.545.d.reply: Blue Wraiths have a frequency of 650THz. Their light synchronizes with both Class A and Class B Stars. Their ability to avoid conventional weaponry is weakened in systems with blue giants.
leviathans.593.desc: After destroying the ancient Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system, our capable forces combed the area it once occupied for anything valuable. They managed to recover several memory fragments from the Curator databanks that should be a great boon to our research.
leviathans.594.a.desc:
Deep space communication arrays picked up a brief automated distress call from the Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system. The transmission ceased after just a few minutes, and long-range recon probes have confirmed that the ancient space station has been destroyed.

Residual ion trails suggest that forces from the [curator_destroyer.GetName] were behind this attack.
leviathans.594.b.desc:
Deep space communication arrays picked up a brief automated distress call from the Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system. The transmission ceased after just a few minutes, and long-range recon probes have confirmed that the ancient space station has been destroyed.

The forces responsible for this attack remain unidentified.
leviathans.594.ab.desc.start: Deep space communication arrays picked up a brief automated distress call from the Curator station in the [curator_system.GetName] system. The transmission ceased after just a few minutes, and long-range recon probes have confirmed that the ancient space station has been destroyed.
leviathans.594.ab.desc.known: Residual ion trails suggest that forces from the [curator_destroyer.GetName] were behind this attack.
leviathans.594.ab.desc.unknown: The forces responsible for this attack remain unidentified.
leviathans.594.c.desc:
All contact has been lost with the [From.GetName], and our recon assets have confirmed that the ancient Curator station was destroyed. These reports suggest the attack force belonged to the [curator_destroyer.GetName].

Unfortunately, the demise of the Curators means we have also lost access to their extensive databanks.
leviathans.594.d.desc:
All contact has been lost with the [From.GetName], and our recon assets have confirmed that the ancient Curator station was destroyed. The forces responsible for this attack remain unidentified.

Unfortunately, the demise of the Curators means we have also lost access to their extensive databanks.
leviathans.594.cd.desc.start: All contact has been lost with the [From.GetName], and our recon assets have confirmed that the ancient Curator station was destroyed.
leviathans.594.cd.desc.known: These reports suggest the attack force belonged to the [curator_destroyer.GetName].
leviathans.594.cd.desc.trade: Unfortunately, the demise of the Curators means we have also lost access to their extensive databanks.
leviathans.594.a: A sad end to their legacy.
leviathans.610.name: Ether Drake Encounter
leviathans.610.desc:
The creature observed in the [From.GetName] system is unlike anything the [Root.GetName] has previously encountered.

Highly aggressive and with destructive capabilities to match, it guards a planetoid that initial scans indicate is exceptionally resource-rich.
leviathans.610.desc.here_be_dragons:
The creature observed in the [From.GetName] system bears some initial resemblance to the Sky Dragon of our home system, although further scans demonstrate that it is clearly a different species, and probably even evolved independently to it.

Highly aggressive and with destructive capabilities to match, it guards a planetoid that initial scans indicate is exceptionally resource-rich.
leviathans.649.desc:
We received one last transmission from our fleet before it was destroyed. It mentions their gigantic foe seemingly homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...

If the beast has our scent, we should be prepared for savage retaliation.
leviathans.649.desc.gesta:
As the Ether Drake was attacking our vessels, it seemed to be homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...

If the creature has our scent, we should prepare for savage retaliation.
leviathans.650.name: The Dragon Comes
leviathans.650.desc:
We received one last transmission from the [Root.GetName] before the fleet engaged emergency FTL protocols and went dark. It includes mention of the gargantuan creature they had been fighting seemingly homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...

If the beast has our scent, we should be prepared for savage retaliation.
leviathans.650.desc.gesta:
As the Ether Drake was attacking our vessels, it seemed to be homing in on the fleet's FTL signature...

If the creature has our scent, we should prepare for savage retaliation.
leviathans.660.name: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon's Tomb
leviathans.660.desc:
Buried deep in the crust of [From.GetName] are the partial, fossilized remains of what appears to have been a close relative to the Ether Drake that once dwelled in the [From.GetStarName] system.

In the eons since this cousin-Drake's passing, its soft tissues have ossified and its bones indurated, becoming mineral-like in structure.
leviathans.661.name: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon's Brood
leviathans.661.desc:
As our mining station orbiting Dragon's Hoard was repositioning to align with a particularly rich mineral vein, sensors picked up something that had hitherto gone undetected.

An undamaged Ether Drake egg in pristine condition, buried beneath the surface of the planetoid and surrounded by the smashed shells of several less fortunate specimens. The egg has been excavated and removed from the mining site, but its ultimate fate remains undecided.
leviathans.661.a: A young Ether Drake would make a formidable ally...
leviathans.661.b: The last one was killed for a reason.
leviathans.664.name: Dragon's Hoard, Dragon Reborn
leviathans.664.a.tooltip: Young Ether Drake Scile joins the fleets of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
leviathans.665.name: Dragon's Hoard, Best Before
leviathans.665.desc:
The Ether Drake egg recovered from the Dragon's Hoard planetoid has, in the words of the xenobiologist in charge of the ovum, passed its expiry date.

There is no longer any hope of hatching the creature within.
leviathans.665.desc.gesta:
The Ether Drake egg recovered from the Dragon's Hoard planetoid can no longer be considered viable.

The species is extinct.
leviathans.665.desc.machine: The Ether Drake egg is terminated. Biological processes have crashed, and there are no available error reports for debugging.
leviathans.670.name: Dragonslayer
leviathans.670.desc:
The formidable Ether Drake has been slain. The exceptional bravery of Commander [From.From.GetLeaderName] and the [From.From.GetName] will not soon be forgotten.

The planetoid the beast guarded so jealously can now be safely exploited. Who knows what treasures the creature might have amassed over the eons?
leviathans.670.desc.noleader:
The formidable Ether Drake has been slain. The exceptional bravery of the [From.From.GetName] will not soon be forgotten.

The planetoid the beast guarded so jealously can now be safely exploited. Who knows what treasures the creature might have amassed over the eons?
leviathans.670.desc.gesta:
The formidable Ether Drake has been slain.

The planetoid the beast guarded so jealously can now be safely exploited. What treasures might the creature have amassed over the eons?
leviathans.999.name: Shrinking Star
leviathans.999.desc: As the [Root.GetName] enters the [From.GetName] system something seems awry. The sun, previously registered as an ordinary dwarf star, appears to have shrunk, having lost mass at an alarming rate. The planets in the system have as a result recently entered ice ages.
leviathans.1000.name: Stellar Devourer
leviathans.1000.desc:
From deep within the star of the [stellarite_system.GetName] system emerges a gargantuan being, larger than a typical moon. Its body radiates heat, the same wavelength of energy as the one produced by the system's star...

It's eating it!

The creature feasts on sun spots, devours solar flares, and we have interrupted its meal. The beast exudes light waves, rapid pulses at an intense frequency. Like a fluorescent roar.
leviathans.1001.desc.stellarite_system:
From deep within the star of the [Root.GetStarName] system emerges a gargantuan being, larger than a typical moon. Its body radiates heat, the same wavelength of energy as the one produced by the system's star...

It's eating it!

The creature feasts on sun spots, devours solar flares, and we have interrupted its meal. The beast exudes light waves, rapid pulses at an intense frequency. Like a fluorescent roar.
leviathans.1001.desc:
As the [Root.GetName] enters the [Root.GetStarName] system it encounters something monstrous. A giant being, radiating light like a miniature star. Our instruments first thought this to be a binary star system.

The beast exudes light waves, rapid pulses at an intense frequency. Like a fluorescent roar.
leviathans.1016.desc:
The Stellar Devourer has been vanquished. Its remains curled up and evaporated, leaving only its egg sac and its digestive system with the stellar matter it contains.

Some of our scientists have urged us to examine the remains, while others wish for us to retrieve the egg sac. Maybe there is some profound knowledge to be had from understanding its digestive system, or might we gain some insight from the egg sac?
leviathans.1016.desc.gesta:
The Stellar Devourer has been vanquished. Its remains curled up and evaporated, leaving only its egg sac and its digestive tract with the stellar matter it contains.

Maybe there is some profound knowledge to be had from understanding its digestive system, or perhaps the egg sac should be studied back on our capital?
leviathans.1016.b: Make it a trophy for all to see.
leviathans.1017.desc:
Studies of the Stellar Devourer's shining remains have left our scientists perplexed and amazed. The star-feasting being is itself a miniature fusion furnace, harvesting solar matter to synthesize an energy source of its own.

Since the body still contains significant amounts of solar matter from the star of the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system, the one it last fed from, it could be possible to extract the energy and reinvigorate the star. Harvesting the corpse's heat for our own ends could satisfy our energy needs in the short term, but would doom the system to an eternal ice age.
leviathans.1017.desc.gesta:
Studies of the Stellar Devourer's shining remains leave us perplexed and amazed. The star-feasting being is itself a miniature fusion furnace, harvesting solar matter to synthesize an energy source of its own.

Since the body still contains significant amounts of solar matter from the star of the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system, the one it last fed from, it could be possible to extract the energy and reinvigorate the star. Harvesting the corpse's heat for our own ends could satisfy our energy needs in the short term, but would doom the system to an eternal ice age.
leviathans.1018.desc: The project was a success! Submerging the Stellar Devourer's remains in the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system's star has stoked the flames of the solar furnace. The planets in the system are heating up, reverting to their past forms as their ecologies recover. Among them was a frozen world, now thawing to reveal a Gaia world, ripe and ready for colonization.
leviathans.1018.alt.desc:
The project has paid off, but at a cost. Submerging the Stellar Devourer's remains into [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName]'s star has caused the solar furnace to shine a bit brighter, but also to spew out solar flares that engulfed the [Root.GetName] and its crew in a roaring inferno. There were no survivors.
The planets in the system are heating up, reaching temperature levels closer to their original form.
leviathans.1018.a.tooltip:
Changes the planet classes of all planets within the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system.

[stellarite_rich_planet.GetName] becomes a Gaia planet and gains the following resource:
£ +25
£ +10
leviathans.1018.b.tooltip:
The [Root.GetName] is destroyed.

Changes the planet classes of all planets within the [guardians_stellarite_home_system.GetName] system.

[stellarite_rich_planet.GetName] becomes a Tundra planet and gains the following resource:
£ +10
£ +15
